template:
# QFT Zoo entry template.
# Save as data/theories/<id>.yaml, where <id> matches the `id` field below.
# Delete any optional section you don't need. Full field reference: CONTRIBUTING.md
#
# LaTeX tips: wrap LaTeX in 'single quotes' (backslashes are then kept as-is).
#   - Prose fields (summary, description, note, role, ...) are Markdown: use $...$ for math,
#     and cite as [@key] or [@key, Sec. 2] (never a direct link; see CONTRIBUTING.md, Citations).
#   - Pure-math fields (lagrangian, symbol, name of an operator, value, Delta): no $ signs.

id: my-theory                      # lowercase-with-hyphens, = filename
name: 'My theory'                  # may contain $...$ math
aliases: []
d: 3                               # spacetime dimension
summary: >-
  One or two sentences describing the theory.
tags: [CFT, interacting, unitary]  # see schema/theory.schema.json for the allowed list

description: |
  Longer Markdown description. Inline math like $\Delta_\sigma$ and display math
  like $$\langle \phi(x)\phi(0)\rangle = |x|^{-2\Delta}$$ both work.

lagrangian: '\mathcal{L} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial\phi)^2'

parameters:
  - symbol: 'N'
    description: Number of fields.
    range: '$N \geq 1$'

symmetry:
  spacetime: '$O(4,1)$ — 3d conformal group with parity'   # group — colloquial name; see CONTRIBUTING.md, Spacetime symmetry
  supercharges: 0                  # real Poincaré supercharges Q; for SUSY theories also state Q and S in spacetime
  global: '$O(N)$'                 # the global symmetry in words (Markdown)
  parity: true                     # true | false | conditional (docs/REPRESENTATIONS.md)
  global_group:                    # the factors operators' representations refer to; [] if none
    - {id: O(N), group: O(N)}      # group: Z2, Z_n, U(1), O(N), SO(N), SU(N), Sp(N), S_n, D_n, finite
  # gauge: '$SU(N)$'
  # notes: 'Anomalies, emergent symmetries, ...'

quantities:
  - symbol: 'C_T/C_T^{\text{free}}'
    description: Stress-tensor central charge
    value: '0.9(1)'                # parenthesis notation for uncertainties
    method: 'CB, rigorous'         # an abbreviation from data/methods.yaml, then an optional qualifier (CONTRIBUTING.md, Methods)
    refs: ['author2025, Table 2']   # a key, optionally with a locator (CONTRIBUTING.md, Citations)

operators:
  - name: '\phi'
    Delta: '0.5(1)'
    spin: 0
    parity: even                   # even | odd | pair | unknown
    global: {O(N): vector}         # a label per factor of global_group (docs/REPRESENTATIONS.md)
    role: 'order parameter'        # optional remark; never part of the representation
    method: CB
    refs: [author2025]

# Three-point functions: one item per unordered triple of operators (lightest first); each value is the coefficient of
# one structure (docs/THREE_POINT.md).
# three_point_structures:                     # only for a structure that is a choice of a paper, not a standard one
#   - id: author2025
#     name: 'scalar–scalar–spin-$\ell$, ...'   # what it is, in a few words
#     form: '\langle\phi_1(x_1)\,\phi_2(x_2)\,O(x_3,z)\rangle = \lambda\,\cdots'   # in the source's notation
#     ref: 'author2025, Eq. (2.1)'             # the formula that defines it
#     description: 'Normalization of the operators and of the structure or blocks, the symbols of the form ...'
# three_point_functions:
#   - operators: ['\phi', '\phi', 's']        # `name`s from the operators table
#     values:
#       - structure: vector-vector-singlet     # a standard structure (data/three_point_structures.yaml), or an id of three_point_structures
#         value: '0.52(1)'
#         method: CB
#         refs: [author2025]
#         # order: ['s', '\phi', '\phi']      # only if the structure assumes another order of the operators
#         # value_of: square                  # only if the number is the square (or `modulus`) of the coefficient

relations:
  - type: flows_to                 # flows_to | dual_to | related_to
    target: ising-3d               # id of an existing entry
    note: 'Which deformation, and any subtleties.'
    # Optional details for a flow (see CONTRIBUTING.md, "RG flows in detail"):
    # id: my-flow
    # flow:
    #   identification: {status: established, method: 'numerics', refs: [author2025]}
    #   deformations:
    #     - {operator: '\phi^2', coupling: 'm^2', sign: negative, sign_convention: '...', refs: [author2025]}

references:
  - key: author2025                # short handle used in refs: [...] above
    title: Title of the paper
    authors: Author, Another
    year: 2025
    arxiv: '2501.00001'            # or doi: / url:

contributors: [your-github-username]

theories.name: 2d Lee–Yang edge singularity CFT
theories.summary: The non-unitary minimal model $\mathcal{M}(2,5)$, with $c = -\tfrac{22}{5}$ and one non-trivial primary $\phi$ of weight $-\tfrac15$. It describes the Lee–Yang edge singularity of the 2d Ising model in an imaginary magnetic field, with edge exponent $\sigma = -\tfrac16$.
theories.description:
Above the critical temperature, the zeros of the Ising partition function in the complex magnetic
field $h$ lie on the imaginary axis [@lee-yang-2d/lee1952] and become dense beyond an edge $h_c$, near
which their density behaves as $(h - h_c)^\sigma$. Fisher [@lee-yang-2d/fisher1978] recognized the edge as a critical point
and described it by a scalar field theory with an imaginary cubic coupling. Cardy [@lee-yang-2d/cardy1985] showed that in
two dimensions the critical theory is the simplest non-unitary minimal model, $\mathcal{M}(2,5)$
with $c = -\tfrac{22}{5}$, and obtained $\sigma = -\tfrac16$: the first application of conformal
field theory to a non-unitary critical point.

The Kac table has one non-trivial primary, $\phi = \phi_{1,2} \equiv \phi_{1,3}$, with
$h = \bar h = -\tfrac15$, so $\Delta_\phi = -\tfrac25$ and $\sigma = \Delta_\phi/(2 - \Delta_\phi)$.
The fusion rule is $\phi \times \phi = 1 + \phi$; with $\langle\phi(x)\phi(0)\rangle = |x|^{4/5}$
the three-point coefficient is purely imaginary, as expected from the imaginary cubic coupling.
The only modular invariant built from the two characters is the diagonal one,
$Z = |\chi_{1,1}|^2 + |\chi_{1,2}|^2$, and the characters are the Rogers–Ramanujan products
$$\chi_{1,1} = q^{11/60}\prod_{n\ge0}\frac{1}{(1-q^{5n+2})(1-q^{5n+3})}, \qquad
\chi_{1,2} = q^{-1/60}\prod_{n\ge0}\frac{1}{(1-q^{5n+1})(1-q^{5n+4})} ,$$
equal by the Rogers–Ramanujan identities to $q^{11/60}\sum_{n\ge0} q^{n^2+n}/(q)_n$ and
$q^{-1/60}\sum_{n\ge0} q^{n^2}/(q)_n$, with $(q)_n = \prod_{k=1}^{n}(1-q^k)$. Since $h_\phi < 0$,
the lowest state on a circle is $\phi$, not the vacuum, and finite-size scaling (for instance the
free energy of a long periodic strip) is governed by $c_{\rm eff} = c - 24h_\phi = \tfrac25$
instead of $c$ ([@lee-yang-2d/isz1986], with transfer matrices of the Ising model at the edge).

### Related problems
The same universality class describes the singularity of lattice gases with purely repulsive
interactions at negative activity; its pressure exponent $\sigma + 1 = \tfrac56$ in two dimensions
agrees with Baxter's solution of the hard-hexagon model [@lee-yang-2d/baxter1980] (see [@lee-yang-2d/cardy2023]). Parisi and Sourlas [@lee-yang-2d/parisi1981]
related the Yang–Lee edge in $d$ dimensions to branched polymers in $d + 2$ dimensions, so this
theory is expected to describe branched polymers in four dimensions. Perturbing the CFT by $\phi$
gives an integrable massive field theory with a single particle, whose factorized S-matrix was
found by Cardy and Mussardo [@lee-yang-2d/cardymussardo1989]. Imaginary magnetic deformations of the tricritical Ising model reach
this fixed point and, it is argued, its tricritical version $\mathcal{M}(2,7)$ [@lee-yang-2d/lencses2023].

symmetry.spacetime: Two Virasoro algebras, $c = \bar c = -\tfrac{22}{5}$ — 2d conformal symmetry, with parity; Euclidean only (non-unitary statistical model)
symmetry.global: No invertible internal symmetry: since $C_{\phi\phi\phi} \neq 0$, no phase rotation of $\phi$ is allowed (the Ising $\mathbb{Z}_2$ is broken by the imaginary field).
symmetry.notes: Not unitary. The spectrum is real because the quantum Hamiltonian is invariant under complex conjugation, $H \to H^*$, combined with $\phi \to -\phi$ [@lee-yang-2d/cardy2023].

quantities.description: Virasoro central charge ($c_L = c_R$)
Effective central charge, $c - 24h_{\min}$ with $h_{\min} = h_\phi$
quantities.note: Replaces $c$ in the finite-size free energy of a long periodic strip. Transfer-matrix estimates for the Ising model at the edge converge to $\tfrac25$ rather than to $c$ [@lee-yang-2d/isz1986, Table I].

quantities.description: Yang–Lee edge exponent, $\sigma = \Delta_\phi/(2 - \Delta_\phi)$
Correlation-length exponent at the edge, $\xi \sim |H - H_c|^{-\nu}$ with $\nu = 1/(2 - \Delta_\phi)$

values.note: $\approx 1.911312699\,i$ [@lee-yang-2d/arguellocruz2025, Eq. (2.2)], defined by $\phi(x)\times\phi(0) = |x|^{4/5}\,1 + C_{\phi\phi\phi}\,|x|^{2/5}\,\phi$. Purely imaginary; its sign flips under $\phi \to -\phi$.

operators.name: \phi = \phi_{1,2}
operators.note: Also labelled $\phi_{1,3}$. Lies below the vacuum, so it dominates the torus partition function at low temperature.

relations.note: The Lee–Yang edge singularity in $d = 2$ and $d = 3$: one universality class (the $i\phi^3$ theory, upper critical dimension 6) continued in dimension.
The Ising CFT perturbed by the energy operator and a purely imaginary magnetic field flows to the Lee–Yang fixed point [@lee-yang-2d/lencses2023].

theories.name: Non-unitary Virasoro minimal models $\mathcal{M}(p,q)$
theories.summary: The diagonal minimal models $\mathcal{M}(p,q)$ with coprime $2 \le p < q$ and $q - p \ge 2$: rational, non-unitary, with $c = 1 - 6(p-q)^2/(pq)$ and a primary of negative weight. The simplest is the Lee–Yang model $\mathcal{M}(2,5)$.
theories.description:
For coprime integers $2 \le p < q$, the minimal model $\mathcal{M}(p,q)$ [@virasoro-minimal-nonunitary/bpz1984] has central charge $c = 1 - 6(p-q)^2/(pq)$ and finitely many Virasoro primaries
$\phi_{r,s}$, with weights given by the Kac formula
$$h_{r,s} = \frac{(qr - ps)^2 - (q-p)^2}{4pq}, \qquad 1 \le r \le p-1,\ 1 \le s \le q-1,$$
and $(r,s) \sim (p-r, q-s)$, so there are $\tfrac12(p-1)(q-1)$ primaries. The models with
$q = p+1$ are the unitary series of Friedan, Qiu and Shenker [@virasoro-minimal-nonunitary/fqs1984] (a separate entry); this entry
collects the others, $q - p \ge 2$, which are all non-unitary. These are the formulas of
Itzykson, Saleur and Zuber [@virasoro-minimal-nonunitary/isz1986] and of Cappelli, Itzykson and Zuber [@virasoro-minimal-nonunitary/ciz1987], whose $(p, p')$ is our $(q, p)$;
in this labelling the Lee–Yang field of $\mathcal{M}(2,5)$ is $\phi_{1,2}$, with
$h_{1,2} = -\tfrac15$.

The irreducible characters [@virasoro-minimal-nonunitary/rochacaridi1985] are, with $\mathsf{q} = e^{2\pi i\tau}$,
$$\chi_{r,s}(\tau) = \frac{1}{\eta(\tau)}\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\Big(\mathsf{q}^{(2kpq + qr - ps)^2/(4pq)} - \mathsf{q}^{(2kpq + qr + ps)^2/(4pq)}\Big),$$
and the diagonal (A-series) partition function
$$Z = \sum_{(r,s)/\sim}|\chi_{r,s}|^2 = \frac12\sum_{r=1}^{p-1}\sum_{s=1}^{q-1}|\chi_{r,s}|^2$$
is modular invariant for every pair. Cappelli, Itzykson and Zuber [@virasoro-minimal-nonunitary/ciz1987] classified all modular
invariants: they are labelled by pairs of ADE Dynkin diagrams with Coxeter numbers $p$ and $q$,
and since one of $p, q$ is odd, one diagram of the pair is of type A. A D-type invariant exists
when the even one of $p, q$ is at least 6, and E-type ones when it is 12, 18 or 30. This entry is
the diagonal series $(A_{p-1}, A_{q-1})$.

### Negative weights and the effective central charge
For $q - p \ge 2$ there is always a label $(r_0, s_0) \ne (1,1)$ with $|qr_0 - ps_0| = 1$, and
$\phi_{r_0,s_0}$ has the lowest weight,
$$h_{\min} = \frac{1 - (q-p)^2}{4pq} < 0 .$$
The vacuum is therefore not the lowest state on a circle. In finite-size scaling, for instance
the free energy of a long periodic strip, $c$ is replaced by the effective central charge
$$c_{\rm eff} = c - 24h_{\min} = 1 - \frac{6}{pq}$$
[@virasoro-minimal-nonunitary/isz1986]. Castro-Alvaredo, Doyon and Ravanini [@virasoro-minimal-nonunitary/castroalvaredo2017] showed that, along
renormalization-group flows with unbroken $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry, a function interpolating
between the ultraviolet and infrared values of $c_{\rm eff}$ decreases monotonically, which
generalizes Zamolodchikov's $c$-theorem.

### The series $\mathcal{M}(2, 2n+3)$
For $p = 2$ the Kac table is a single row: $\mathcal{M}(2, 2n+3)$, $n \ge 1$, has $n+1$ primaries
$\phi_{1,s}$, $1 \le s \le n+1$, all of non-positive weight, and each character is an infinite
product (Andrews–Gordon identities), which for $\mathcal{M}(2,5)$ are the Rogers–Ramanujan
products [@virasoro-minimal-nonunitary/milas2004]. $\mathcal{M}(2,5)$ is the Lee–Yang edge singularity, and Lencsés, Miscioscia,
Mussardo and Takács [@virasoro-minimal-nonunitary/lencses2023] conjecture that $\mathcal{M}(2, 2n+3)$ controls the $(n+1)$-th multicritical
Yang–Lee point, reached by imaginary magnetic perturbations of the unitary minimal models.

theories.name: 2d $O(n)$ loop model
theories.summary: The critical points of the 2d $O(n)$ loop gas, $-2 \le n \le 2$: two branches (dilute and dense) of non-unitary, logarithmic CFTs with $n = -2\cos(\pi g)$ and $c = 1 - 6(1-g)^2/g$. They contain self-avoiding walks, the Ising model, dense polymers and percolation hulls.
theories.description:
On the honeycomb lattice, the $O(n)$ model with weight $\prod_{\langle xy\rangle}(1 + K\phi(x)\cdot\phi(y))$
for unit $n$-vectors $\phi$ expands into a gas of non-intersecting loops, with weight $K$ per occupied edge
and $n$ per loop, so that $n$ becomes a continuous parameter. For $-2 \le n \le 2$ the loop gas is critical at
$K_c(n) = 1/\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2 - n}}$ [@on-loop-model-2d/nienhuis1982]; its continuum limit is the dilute $O(n)$ CFT. For $K > K_c$
(and $-2 < n < 2$) the whole phase flows to a second CFT, the dense $O(n)$ model. At $n = 2$ the two coincide,
at the Kosterlitz–Thouless point, described by the free boson. Gorbenko and Zan [@on-loop-model-2d/gorbenkozan2020] study the
renormalization-group flow from the dilute to the dense fixed point, and their merger at $n = 2$.

Through a Coulomb-gas (solid-on-solid) mapping, both branches are parametrized by a coupling $g$ with
$$n = -2\cos(\pi g), \qquad c = 1 - \frac{6(1-g)^2}{g},$$
dilute for $1 \le g \le 2$ and dense for $0 < g \le 1$. This is the $g$ of Saleur [@on-loop-model-2d/saleur1992, Eq. (30)] and the $\beta^2$ of
Grans-Samuelsson et al. [@on-loop-model-2d/granssamuelsson2022] and of Jacobsen, Ribault and Saleur [@on-loop-model-2d/jrs2023], who write $c = 13 - 6\beta^2 - 6\beta^{-2}$ (the
same function). As CFTs, both branches are one family, analytic in $g$, which makes sense for
$\mathrm{Re}\, g > 0$.

The continuum limit is expected to be non-unitary, since the non-locality of loops can be traded for local
complex weights. This holds even for integer $n$: the local observables of the $O(1)$ model form the unitary
Ising minimal model, but non-local (loop) observables need a larger, non-unitary CFT
[@on-loop-model-2d/granssamuelsson2022]. Gorbenko and Zan [@on-loop-model-2d/gorbenkozan2020] find that the CFT is logarithmic for every $n$ in the window, with the $O(n)$ currents
in a staggered logarithmic multiplet; the negative-norm states decouple at $n = 2$.

### Spectrum
The torus partition function is known [@on-loop-model-2d/dfsz1987], and Jacobsen, Ribault and Saleur [@on-loop-model-2d/jrs2023]
determine the space of states, including the action of $O(n)$. With
$P_{(r,s)} = \frac12(\beta r - \beta^{-1}s)$ and $\Delta_{(r,s)} = P_{(r,s)}^2 - P_{(1,1)}^2$, it contains
diagonal degenerate fields $V^D_{\langle 1,s\rangle}$ with $s$ odd, which are $O(n)$ singlets, and
non-diagonal fields $V_{(r,s)}$ with weights $(\Delta_{(r,s)}, \Delta_{(r,-s)})$,
$r \in \tfrac12\mathbb{N}^*$, $s \in \tfrac1r\mathbb{Z}$, in representations $\Lambda_{(r,s)}$ of $O(n)$
(logarithmic when $r, s$ are positive integers). The spin field is $V_{(\frac12,0)}$, $V_{(r,0)}$ is the
$2r$-leg (watermelon) operator, and the energy operator is $V^D_{\langle 1,3\rangle}$; their dimensions are
listed below. The formulas for $\Lambda_{(r,s)}$ rest on simple but unproven assumptions about the lattice
model.

### Status
Four-point functions are studied by numerical bootstrap. Grans-Samuelsson et al. [@on-loop-model-2d/granssamuelsson2022] counted the solutions of
crossing symmetry for the 30 simplest four-point functions (from 2 to 6), which saturate the bound from $O(n)$
representation theory in 21 cases. Nivesvivat, Ribault and Jacobsen [@on-loop-model-2d/nrj2024] found analytic expressions for 235
four-point structure constants, each a universal function built from Barnes' double Gamma function times a
polynomial in the loop weights, and conjecture that all structure constants take this form.

operators.name: V_{(\frac{L}{2},0)}
operators.note: $2\Delta_{(\frac{L}{2},0)}$. Agrees with Saleur's [@on-loop-model-2d/saleur1992] $2h_L = (9L^2-4)/48$ for dilute polymers ($g = \tfrac32$) and with his dense-polymer ($g = \tfrac12$) and percolation-hull ($g = \tfrac23$) weights.

operators.name: \varepsilon = V^D_{\langle 1,3\rangle}
operators.note: $2\Delta_{(1,3)}$. Relevant on the dilute branch, marginal at $n = 2$, irrelevant on the dense branch; $\Delta = 1$ at $g = \tfrac43$ (Ising $\epsilon$).

relations.note: The dilute branch is the critical $O(n)$ model in two dimensions; the 3d critical $O(n)$ model can also be defined as a loop model for continuous $n$ [@on-loop-model-2d/gorbenkozan2020].
The dilute member $g = \tfrac43$ ($n = 1$): its local observables form the Ising minimal model, while loop observables need the larger non-unitary CFT.

Boundaries of the Fortuin–Kasteleyn clusters of the critical $Q$-state Potts model form a completely packed loop model with loop weight $\sqrt{Q}$ and Coulomb-gas coupling $g = m/(m+1)$ (Jacobsen and Saleur [@on-loop-model-2d/jacobsensaleur2019, Eqs. (4), (43)]), the coupling of the dense branch at $n = \sqrt{Q}$: the dense members $g = \tfrac12, \tfrac23$ correspond to $Q = 0, 1$. The two CFTs share $c$ but have different spectra and global symmetries ($O(n)$ versus $S_Q$; [@on-loop-model-2d/jrs2023]).

theories.name: 2d Potts CFT at generic $Q$
theories.summary: The critical 2d $Q$-state Potts model, continued to real $0 \le Q \le 4$ through Fortuin–Kasteleyn clusters: a non-rational, non-unitary, logarithmic CFT with $c = 1 - 6/(m(m+1))$, $\sqrt{Q} = 2\cos\frac{\pi}{m+1}$. Percolation is $Q = 1$.
theories.description:
The $Q$-state Potts model has spins $\sigma_i \in \{1, \dots, Q\}$ with interaction
$-K\delta_{\sigma_i,\sigma_j}$ and $S_Q$ symmetry. Fortuin and Kasteleyn [@potts-2d/fk1972] rewrote its partition function as a
sum over subsets $A$ of edges, $Z = \sum_A v^{|A|} Q^{k(A)}$ with $v = e^K - 1$ and $k(A)$ the number of
clusters, which makes sense for any real $Q$. On the square lattice the critical point is $v_c = \sqrt{Q}$,
and the boundaries of the clusters form completely packed loops on the medial lattice with weight $\sqrt{Q}$
per loop (see [@potts-2d/jacobsensaleur2019]). The transition is continuous for $Q \le 4$. For $Q > 4$ it is first order,
weakly so just above $4$, which Gorbenko, Rychkov and Zan [@potts-2d/grz2018] relate to complex CFTs.

Following Jacobsen and Saleur [@potts-2d/jacobsensaleur2019], the critical theory is parametrized by
$$\sqrt{Q} = 2\cos\frac{\pi}{m+1}, \quad m \in [1, \infty], \qquad c = 1 - \frac{6}{m(m+1)}, \qquad h_{r,s} = \frac{[(m+1)r - ms]^2 - 1}{4m(m+1)},$$
with $m$ and the Kac labels $r, s$ not restricted to integers; the Coulomb-gas coupling is $g = m/(m+1)$.
Equivalently [@potts-2d/nivesvivat2023] $Q = 4\cos^2(\pi\beta^2)$ with $\tfrac12 \le \beta^2 \le 1$ and
$c = 13 - 6\beta^2 - 6\beta^{-2}$, where $\beta^2 = m/(m+1)$. The order parameter (spin field) has weights
$h_{1/2,0}$ and the energy field $h_{2,1}$; the energy field is degenerate for generic $Q$.

At $Q = 2, 3, 4$ the critical point, as seen by local spin observables, is a unitary CFT: a minimal model for
$Q = 2, 3$ and an orbifold of the compact boson for $Q = 4$. For non-integer $Q$, and for $Q = 1$, the theory
is real but non-unitary [@potts-2d/grz2018]. Even at integer $Q$, the CFT of cluster observables is
larger than the minimal model: at $Q = 2$ the Potts CFT describes Fortuin–Kasteleyn clusters and is not the
Ising minimal model [@potts-2d/nivesvivat2023]. The Potts CFT is defined by continuation in $c$ to a double cover of the
half-plane $\mathrm{Re}\, c < 13$ (Picco, Ribault and Santachiara [@potts-2d/prs2019]; Nivesvivat [@potts-2d/nivesvivat2023, Sec. 1, Eq. (1.2)]).

### Spectrum
The torus partition function goes back to Di Francesco, Saleur and Zuber [@potts-2d/dfsz1987], and Jacobsen, Ribault and Saleur [@potts-2d/jrs2023]
determine the space of states with the action of $S_Q$. In their notation,
$P_{(r,s)} = \frac12(\beta r - \beta^{-1}s)$ and $\Delta_{(r,s)} = P_{(r,s)}^2 - P_{(1,1)}^2$ (so their
$\Delta_{(r,s)}$ is $h_{s,r}$ above), it consists of diagonal degenerate fields with $\Delta_{(1,s)}$,
$s \in \mathbb{N}^*$ ($S_Q$ singlets); diagonal fields with $\Delta_{(0,s)}$, $s \in \mathbb{N} + \tfrac12$,
in the standard representation of $S_Q$ (the spin field is $s = \tfrac12$); and non-diagonal fields with
weights $(\Delta_{(r,s)}, \Delta_{(r,-s)})$, $r \ge 2$ an integer and $s \in \tfrac1r\mathbb{Z}$, in
representations $\Xi_{(r,s)}$ of $S_Q$. Grans-Samuelsson, Liu, He, Jacobsen and Saleur [@potts-2d/granssamuelsson2020] showed that the
diagonal degenerate fields come in simple modules, while non-diagonal fields with integer labels form
indecomposable "diamond" representations with rank-2 Jordan cells for $L_0$ and $\bar L_0$: the Potts CFT is
logarithmic for generic $Q$.

### Status
The spectrum is exactly known for $0 < Q \le 4$, but not all OPE coefficients are, so the theory has not been
exactly solved [@potts-2d/grz2018]. Most work concerns four-point connectivities, the probabilities
that four points lie in given clusters. Picco, Ribault and Santachiara [@potts-2d/prs2016] proposed a spectrum and bootstrapped
connectivities in agreement with Monte Carlo data; later [@potts-2d/prs2019], comparing with a CFT that interpolates between
D-series minimal models, they argued that the agreement is exact only at $Q = 0, 3, 4$. Jacobsen and Saleur [@potts-2d/jacobsensaleur2019]
found, with lattice algebra and transfer-matrix numerics, that the spectra in the fusion channels are much
richer than proposed. He, Jacobsen and Saleur [@potts-2d/hjs2020] solved the bootstrap numerically with interchiral conformal
blocks, and Nivesvivat and Ribault [@potts-2d/nivesvivatribault2021] computed connectivities to arbitrary precision with logarithmic blocks,
confirming the Delfino–Viti conjecture [@potts-2d/delfinoviti2011] for the three-point connectivity (built from the $c \le 1$ Liouville
structure constant). Nivesvivat [@potts-2d/nivesvivat2023] found extra crossing-symmetric solutions whose interpretation is unknown, and
Nivesvivat, Ribault and Jacobsen [@potts-2d/nrj2024] conjecture that all structure constants of critical loop models are a
universal function, built from Barnes' double Gamma function, times a polynomial in the loop weights. These
are numerical results and conjectures.

theories.name: Symplectic fermions
theories.summary: The $c = -2$ logarithmic CFT of a pair of free anticommuting scalars [@symplectic-fermions/kausch1995; @symplectic-fermions/kausch2000]. It is non-unitary, and $L_0$ has a Jordan block on the vacuum module. Its bosonic $\mathbb{Z}_2$ orbifold is the local CFT of the triplet $\mathcal{W}$-algebra at $c = -2$ [@symplectic-fermions/gk1999].
theories.description:
Two real anticommuting fields $\theta^\alpha$ ($\alpha = \pm$) of weight $(0,0)$, with a kinetic term built from
a symplectic form $J^{\alpha\beta}$ and propagator
$\langle\theta^\alpha\theta^\beta\rangle = -J^{\alpha\beta}\ln|z - w|^2$ ([@symplectic-fermions/kausch1995, Eqs. (65)–(66)], where the
field is called $\Phi^\alpha$). The chiral fields $\chi^\alpha = \partial\theta^\alpha$ have weight $(1, 0)$ and
modes $\{\chi^\alpha_m, \chi^\beta_n\} = m\,d^{\alpha\beta}\delta_{m+n,0}$, with $d^{\alpha\beta}$
antisymmetric; $T = \tfrac12 d_{\alpha\beta}{:}\chi^\alpha\chi^\beta{:}$ has $c = -2$
[@symplectic-fermions/kausch2000, Eqs. (7)–(10)]. There is a global $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ symmetry with the fermions in the fundamental. Since $c < 0$ the
theory is not unitary; its basic fields are fermions of spin zero.

**Logarithmic vacuum module.** The theory is built on the maximal extension of the (unique, irreducible) vacuum
representation of the chiral algebra. It is generated from four ground states, two bosonic, $\Omega$ and
$\omega$, and two fermionic, $\theta^\alpha$, with $\chi^\alpha_0\,\omega = -\theta^\alpha$,
$\chi^\alpha_0\,\theta^\beta = d^{\alpha\beta}\,\Omega$ and $L_0\,\omega = \bar L_0\,\omega = \Omega$. So $L_0$
has a two-dimensional Jordan block and the theory contains logarithmic operators. $\Omega$ acts as the identity
but $\langle\Omega\rangle = 0$, while $\langle\omega\rangle = 1$, and OPEs contain logarithms, e.g.
$\theta^\alpha(x)\theta^\beta \sim d^{\alpha\beta}(\omega + (Z + \ln|x|^2)\,\Omega)$ with $Z$ a constant. All
$2N$-point functions of $\theta^\alpha$ are known in closed form [@symplectic-fermions/kausch2000, Eqs. (12)–(17)].

**The $\eta\xi$ ghost system.** The $(\eta, \xi)$ system of weights $(1, 0)$, also at $c = -2$, contains the
chiral algebra generated by $\eta$ and $\partial\xi$, the two components of $\chi^\alpha$. Adjoining $\xi$,
$\bar\xi$ (rather than $\theta^\alpha$) to it gives the ghost system: the two models are different local slices
of one non-local theory [@symplectic-fermions/kausch2000, Sec. 2]. The value $c = -2$ is the Kac formula $1 - 6(p-q)^2/(pq)$ at
$(p, q) = (1, 2)$, outside the minimal series.

### Bosonic orbifold: the triplet model
The model is consistent on the sphere, but its torus partition function is not modular invariant: sectors with
antiperiodic fermions must be added. The orbifold by $\mathbb{C}_2 = \{\pm 1\} \subset SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ keeps
the bosonic states and adds the twisted sector, in which the fermions are half-integer moded. It is isomorphic
to the local logarithmic CFT of the triplet algebra constructed by Gaberdiel and Kausch
[@symplectic-fermions/gk1999; @symplectic-fermions/kausch2000, Sec. 4.4]. This algebra, generated by $T$ and a triplet of weight-3 fields $W^a$, extends the Virasoro algebra of the
$(1, 2)$ model and has finitely many irreducible representations. The irreducible $\mathcal{V}_{-1/8}$ (a
singlet) and $\mathcal{V}_{3/8}$ (a doublet), together with two reducible but indecomposable representations
$\mathcal{R}_0$ and $\mathcal{R}_1$ that carry $L_0$ Jordan blocks, close under fusion
[@symplectic-fermions/gk1996; @symplectic-fermions/gk1999]. The non-chiral vacuum sector is not a product of left and right representations but a quotient of
one, as locality requires. The partition function is modular invariant
[@symplectic-fermions/gk1999, Sec. 6.3; @symplectic-fermions/kausch2000, Eqs. (39), (64)]:
$$Z = |\eta(\tau)|^{-2}\sum_{k=0}^{3}|\theta_{k,2}(\tau)|^2, \qquad \theta_{k,m}(\tau) = \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}+\frac{k}{2m}} q^{m n^2}.$$
As a function of $\tau$ this equals the compact-boson partition function at $R = 2$ in the convention of that
entry (checked by comparing the series; Gaberdiel and Kausch [@symplectic-fermions/gk1999] note the coincidence with a circle partition
function). The lowest state is the twist field $\mu$, with $h = \bar h = -\tfrac18$, so
$c_{\rm eff} = c - 24h_\mu = 1$.

### Dense polymers
Dense polymers are the $n \to 0$ limit of the low-temperature (dense) phase of the $O(n)$ loop model:
$g = \tfrac12$ in the Coulomb-gas parametrization $n = -2\cos\pi g$, $g \in [0, 1]$ dense
[@symplectic-fermions/saleur1992, Eqs. (30)–(31)]. Saleur [@symplectic-fermions/saleur1992] described their continuum limit by an $\eta\xi$ system; an exactly solvable lattice model
confirms $c = -2$ [@symplectic-fermions/pr2007]. Kausch observed that the dense-polymer partition function and the
$L$-leg exponents $x_L = (L^2 - 4)/16$ are shared by the $\mathbb{C}_4$ orbifolds of the $\eta\xi$ system and of
the symplectic fermions, and gave evidence, from logarithmic four-point functions, that the continuum theory is
the symplectic-fermion $\mathbb{C}_4$ orbifold, adding that a more detailed analysis is needed
[@symplectic-fermions/kausch2000, Sec. 4.5]. Pearce and Rasmussen [@symplectic-fermions/pr2007] list several logarithmic theories at $c = -2$ (the triplet model, symplectic
fermions, the Abelian sandpile and dimers, among others) and note that their precise relation is not yet clear.

theories.name: 2d percolation CFT
theories.summary: The critical point of percolation in two dimensions, the $Q = 1$ member of the 2d Potts CFT: a non-unitary, logarithmic CFT with $c = 0$, whose exponents are exact and, for site percolation on the triangular lattice, proved.
theories.description:
In site percolation each site is occupied independently with probability $p$; on the triangular lattice the
threshold is $p_c = \tfrac12$. Written in Fortuin–Kasteleyn clusters, the $Q$-state Potts model makes sense
for real $Q$, and percolation is its limit $Q \to 1$. The partition function becomes trivial and $c = 0$
[@percolation-2d/cardy1992], but correlation functions describe the geometry of critical clusters: the two-point function of the
spin field is the probability that two points lie in the same cluster.

In the Kac parametrization of the Potts CFT at $Q = 1$ ($m = 2$), the order parameter has weight
$h_{1/2,0} = \tfrac{5}{96}$ and the energy field $h_{2,1} = \tfrac58$. The exponents follow:
$\nu = 1/(2 - \Delta_\epsilon) = \tfrac43$, $\eta = 2\Delta_\sigma = \tfrac{5}{24}$,
$\beta = \nu\Delta_\sigma = \tfrac{5}{36}$, $\gamma = \nu(2 - \eta) = \tfrac{43}{18}$, and clusters have
fractal dimension $2 - \Delta_\sigma = \tfrac{91}{48}$. Cluster boundaries (hulls) have dimension $\tfrac74$
[@percolation-2d/saleurduplantier1987]; they are the loops of the dense $O(n)$ loop model at $n = 1$. These values were
predicted with Coulomb-gas and conformal field theory methods (see the references in [@percolation-2d/smirnovwerner2001]).

Cardy [@percolation-2d/cardy1992] found the probability that a cluster connects the boundary arcs $(x_1, x_2)$ and $(x_3, x_4)$ of a
simply connected domain mapped to the upper half plane,
$$\pi_h = \frac{3\,\Gamma(\tfrac23)}{\Gamma(\tfrac13)^2}\,\lambda^{1/3}\,{}_2F_1\!\left(\tfrac13, \tfrac23; \tfrac43; \lambda\right), \qquad \lambda = \frac{(x_4 - x_3)(x_2 - x_1)}{(x_3 - x_1)(x_4 - x_2)}$$
(Cardy writes $\eta$ for the cross-ratio $\lambda$), from the second-order differential equation of the
boundary-condition-changing operator $\phi_{1,2}$, whose weight vanishes at $c = 0$.

### Proofs
For site percolation on the triangular lattice, the main predictions are theorems. Schramm [@percolation-2d/schramm2000] showed that SLE$_6$
is the only possible conformally invariant scaling limit of cluster interfaces, and that Cardy's formula would
follow from it. Smirnov [@percolation-2d/smirnov2001] proved that the scaling limit exists and is conformally invariant, proving Cardy's
formula and convergence of interfaces to SLE$_6$. Lawler, Schramm and Werner [@percolation-2d/lsw2002] computed the one-arm exponent:
the probability that the cluster of the origin reaches distance $R$ is $R^{-5/48 + o(1)}$. Smirnov and Werner [@percolation-2d/smirnovwerner2001]
combined these results with Kesten's scaling relations [@percolation-2d/kesten1987] to prove the values of $\nu$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and
$\eta$. They listed the extension to other lattices, such as bond percolation on the square lattice, as open.

### Status
The bulk CFT is not fully understood. Jacobsen and Saleur [@percolation-2d/jacobsensaleur2019] describe it as non-unitary, probably logarithmic,
and containing non-degenerate operators that preclude the BPZ differential equations. Vasseur, Jacobsen and
Saleur [@percolation-2d/vasseur2012] found observables whose two-point functions are logarithmic at $Q \to 1$: the energy operator mixes
with a logarithmic partner, the field that creates two propagating clusters. Delfino and Viti [@percolation-2d/delfinoviti2011] conjectured
the three-point connectivity ratio $P_3/\sqrt{P_2P_2P_2} \approx 1.0220$ from the $c \le 1$ Liouville
structure constant; Nivesvivat and Ribault [@percolation-2d/nivesvivatribault2021] confirmed it numerically to about 26 significant digits, and
computed four-point connectivities to arbitrary precision. Saleur [@percolation-2d/saleur1992] proposed a twisted $\mathcal{N}=2$
description at $c = 0$ that explains why percolation and self-avoiding walks share exponents. Four-point
functions at generic $Q$ are discussed in the 2d Potts CFT entry.

theories.name: 2d self-avoiding walk CFT ($O(n\to0)$ model)
theories.summary: The $n \to 0$ limit of the dilute critical point of the 2d $O(n)$ loop model, which describes self-avoiding walks and dilute polymers in the plane. A non-unitary, logarithmic CFT with $c = 0$ and Coulomb-gas exponents $\nu = \tfrac34$, $\gamma = \tfrac{43}{32}$.
theories.description:
A self-avoiding walk (SAW) is a nearest-neighbour lattice path that visits no site twice. The number $c_n$ of
$n$-step walks grows as $\mu^n n^{\gamma - 1}$, and the mean squared end-to-end distance as $n^{2\nu}$. Walks
are the $n \to 0$ limit of the loop expansion of the $O(n)$ model: on the honeycomb lattice the loop gas with
weight $K$ per occupied edge and $n$ per loop is critical at $K_c(n) = 1/\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2 - n}}$ [@saw-2d/nienhuis1982],
which at $n = 0$ gives the connective constant $\mu = 1/K_c = \sqrt{2 + \sqrt2}$, proved by Duminil-Copin and
Smirnov [@saw-2d/dcs2012]. The continuum limit is the dilute branch of the 2d $O(n)$ loop model at $n = 0$, i.e. Coulomb-gas
coupling $g = \tfrac32$, with $c = 0$.

Nienhuis's Coulomb-gas analysis [@saw-2d/nienhuis1982] gives $\nu = \tfrac34$, Flory's value, and $\gamma = \tfrac{43}{32}$; then
$\eta = 2 - \gamma/\nu = \tfrac{5}{24}$ and the walk has fractal dimension $1/\nu = \tfrac43$. In CFT language
the $L$-leg operator, which inserts $L$ mutually avoiding walks at a point, has weight
$$h_L = \frac{9L^2 - 4}{96},$$
so $h_1 = \tfrac{5}{96}$ (end point of a walk, $\eta = 4h_1$) and $h_2 = \tfrac13$ ($1/\nu = 2 - 2h_2$). These
weights are Kac weights with integer labels only for even $L$ [@saw-2d/saleur1992]. Saleur [@saw-2d/saleur1992] proposed that dilute polymers
are described by a twisted $\mathcal{N}=2$ theory at $c = 0$, which also explains why their exponents coincide
with those of percolation (both have $\eta = \tfrac{5}{24}$).

Lawler, Schramm and Werner [@saw-2d/lsw2004] showed that if the scaling limit of SAWs exists and is conformally invariant, it
must be SLE$_{8/3}$, and that the exponents of SLE$_{8/3}$ reproduce $\nu = \tfrac34$ and
$\gamma = \tfrac{43}{32}$; SLE$_{8/3}$ has Hausdorff dimension $\tfrac43$. At the time of these papers neither
the existence of the limit nor the values of the exponents were proved. Duminil-Copin and Smirnov [@saw-2d/dcs2012] note that
the other half of the discrete Cauchy–Riemann relations for their parafermionic observable would imply
convergence to SLE$_{8/3}$.

### Logarithms at $c = 0$
As for percolation, $c = 0$ leads to representations of the Virasoro algebra that are not fully reducible.
Operators that are distinct at generic $n$ can become degenerate as $n \to 0$ and mix, so that correlation
functions acquire logarithms, and a logarithmic partner of the stress tensor avoids the "$c = 0$ catastrophe"
[@saw-2d/vasseur2012]. Here, for instance, the energy operator and the 2-leg operator both have
dimension $\tfrac23$.

theories.name: Free Majorana fermion (2d)
aliases: Free massless Majorana fermion in two dimensions
Critical point of the Kitaev chain
theories.summary: The $c = \tfrac12$ fermionic CFT of a free massless Majorana fermion. It needs a spin structure; summing over spin structures (gauging $(-1)^F$) gives the 2d Ising CFT, and the Ising CFT with an Arf-invariant coupling gives back the fermion.
theories.description:
A real fermion with a holomorphic component $\psi(z)$ of weight $(\tfrac12, 0)$ and an antiholomorphic
component $\bar\psi(\bar z)$ of weight $(0, \tfrac12)$, with $c = \bar c = \tfrac12$
[@free-majorana-fermion-2d/ginsparg-lectures, Eq. (3.5)]. This is a **fermionic** theory: it is defined only after a choice of spin structure, and its
local operators include the spin-$\tfrac12$ field $\psi$. The bilinear $\psi\bar\psi$, of weight
$(\tfrac12, \tfrac12)$, is the mass term.

On a torus a spin structure is a choice of periodic (Ramond, R) or antiperiodic (Neveu–Schwarz, NS)
boundary conditions around each cycle; in the Hamiltonian picture, periodicity in time inserts $(-1)^F$
in the trace. The four partition functions are [@free-majorana-fermion-2d/ginsparg-lectures, Eqs. (7.13), (7.21)–(7.22)]
$$Z_{\rm NS} = \left|\frac{\theta_3}{\eta}\right|,\qquad Z_{\widetilde{\rm NS}} = \operatorname{Tr}_{\rm NS}(-1)^F q^{L_0-\frac{1}{48}}\bar q^{\bar L_0-\frac{1}{48}} = \left|\frac{\theta_4}{\eta}\right|,\qquad Z_{\rm R} = \left|\frac{\theta_2}{\eta}\right|,\qquad Z_{\widetilde{\rm R}} = \left|\frac{\theta_1}{\eta}\right| = 0 .$$
$Z_{\widetilde{\rm R}}$ vanishes because of the fermion zero mode. Under $T$, $Z_{\rm NS}$ and
$Z_{\widetilde{\rm NS}}$ are exchanged; under $S$, $Z_{\widetilde{\rm NS}}$ and $Z_{\rm R}$ are
exchanged [@free-majorana-fermion-2d/ginsparg-lectures, Eqs. (7.12), (7.14)]. The zero modes $\psi_0, \bar\psi_0$ give the Ramond sector
two ground states of weight $(\tfrac{1}{16}, \tfrac{1}{16})$ with opposite fermion parity
[@free-majorana-fermion-2d/ginsparg-lectures, Eq. (7.17); @free-majorana-fermion-2d/ktt2019, Sec. 2.3].

### Bosonization: the Ising model
Summing over the spin structures with weight $\tfrac12$ projects onto $(-1)^F = +1$ in both sectors and
gives the Ising partition function [@free-majorana-fermion-2d/ginsparg-lectures, Eq. (7.22)]:
$$Z_{\rm Ising} = \tfrac12\left(\left|\tfrac{\theta_3}{\eta}\right| + \left|\tfrac{\theta_4}{\eta}\right| + \left|\tfrac{\theta_2}{\eta}\right| \pm \left|\tfrac{\theta_1}{\eta}\right|\right) = |\chi_0|^2 + |\chi_{1/2}|^2 + |\chi_{1/16}|^2 .$$
The NS sector supplies $1$ and $\varepsilon \propto \psi\bar\psi$; the Ramond sector supplies one of its
two ground states. The sign in the Ramond sector is not fixed by modular invariance: the two choices
keep the spin field $\sigma$ or the disorder field $\mu$ and give equivalent theories, related by
Kramers–Wannier duality [@free-majorana-fermion-2d/ginsparg-lectures, after Eq. (7.23)].

Karch, Tong and Turner [@free-majorana-fermion-2d/ktt2019] write this continuum Jordan–Wigner map as dualities between the fermion and the
Ising model coupled to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge fields, with the Arf invariant of the spin structure playing
the role of a Chern–Simons term. Gauging $(-1)^F$ of the fermion, with an Arf-invariant counterterm for
the background field, gives the Ising CFT [@free-majorana-fermion-2d/ktt2019, Eq. (2.17)]; conversely the fermion is the Ising model
with its $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauged and coupled to $\mathrm{Arf}$ [@free-majorana-fermion-2d/ktt2019, Eq. (2.9)], with
$\psi \leftrightarrow \mu\sigma$ [@free-majorana-fermion-2d/ktt2019, Eq. (2.16)].

### Mass deformation, Kitaev chain and the Arf invariant
The mass term gives two gapped phases. One is trivial; the other is the topological phase of the Kitaev
chain, whose low-energy effective action is $i\pi\,\mathrm{Arf}$ [@free-majorana-fermion-2d/ktt2019, Eq. (2.10)].
On the torus the Arf invariant (the mod 2 index of the Dirac operator) is 1 only for the doubly periodic
spin structure. The massless fermion is the transition between the two phases. Its discrete chiral
symmetry, chiral fermion parity $\psi \to \psi$, $\bar\psi \to -\bar\psi$, flips the sign of the mass
and is anomalous: it shifts the action by $i\pi\,\mathrm{Arf}$ [@free-majorana-fermion-2d/ktt2019, Eq. (2.3)]. Stacking the fermion with
the Arf theory before gauging $(-1)^F$ gives the Ising CFT again, with the fermion parity of the kept
Ramond states reversed [@free-majorana-fermion-2d/ktt2019, Eq. (2.19)]; under bosonization the chiral symmetry becomes Kramers–Wannier
duality [@free-majorana-fermion-2d/ktt2019, Sec. 2.5].

theories.description:
The simplest unitary Virasoro minimal model, $\mathcal{M}(4,3)$, with three
primary operators $1$, $\sigma$, $\epsilon$ and fusion rules
$\sigma\times\sigma = 1 + \epsilon$, $\sigma\times\epsilon = \sigma$,
$\epsilon\times\epsilon = 1$.

Onsager [@ising-2d/onsager1944] solved the lattice model exactly; Belavin, Polyakov and
Zamolodchikov [@ising-2d/bpz1984] identified the critical point with this minimal model. The theory is closely
related to a free Majorana fermion (they differ by a sum over spin structures).

theories.summary: The diagonal unitary minimal models, $c = 1 - \frac{6}{m(m+1)}$ for $m \geq 3$: Ising, tricritical Ising, tetracritical Ising, …
theories.description:
The diagonal (A-type) modular invariant $Z = \frac12\sum_{r,s}|\chi_{r,s}|^2$ exists for every $m$.

Weights are given by the Kac formula
$$h_{r,s} = \frac{\big((m+1)r - ms\big)^2 - 1}{4m(m+1)}, \qquad 1 \le r \le m-1,\ 1 \le s \le m,$$
with $(r,s) \sim (m-r, m+1-s)$. Friedan, Qiu and Shenker [@virasoro-minimal-a/fqs1984] showed these are the only unitary
theories with $c<1$; Cappelli, Itzykson and Zuber [@virasoro-minimal-a/ciz1987] classified their modular invariants by pairs of
ADE Dynkin diagrams $(G, G^\prime)$ with Coxeter numbers $m$ and $m+1$.

The lightest non-vacuum primary is $\phi_{2,2}$ with $h = \frac{3}{4m(m+1)}$. Central charges accumulate at $c = 1$.

theories.description:
For odd $m$ the invariant is $(A_{m-1}, D_{(m+3)/2})$ and for even $m$ it is $(D_{m/2+1}, A_m)$. When the D label is even the invariant is block-diagonal (an extended chiral algebra); when it is odd it is a permutation invariant.

Weights are given by the Kac formula
$$h_{r,s} = \frac{\big((m+1)r - ms\big)^2 - 1}{4m(m+1)}, \qquad 1 \le r \le m-1,\ 1 \le s \le m,$$

theories with $c<1$; Cappelli, Itzykson and Zuber [@virasoro-minimal-d/ciz1987] classified their modular invariants by pairs of
ADE Dynkin diagrams $(G, G^\prime)$ with Coxeter numbers $m$ and $m+1$.

The D-projection removes $\phi_{2,2}$ as a scalar, so the gap comes from $\phi_{3,3}$ with $h = \frac{2}{m(m+1)}$.

The E-type invariants exist when $m$ or $m+1$ equals the Coxeter number of $E_6$ (12), $E_7$ (18) or $E_8$ (30). The $E_6$ and $E_8$ invariants are block-diagonal (extended chiral algebras); $E_7$ is a permutation of the $D_{10}$ blocks.

Weights are given by the Kac formula
$$h_{r,s} = \frac{\big((m+1)r - ms\big)^2 - 1}{4m(m+1)}, \qquad 1 \le r \le m-1,\ 1 \le s \le m,$$
with $(r,s) \sim (m-r, m+1-s)$. Friedan, Qiu and Shenker [@virasoro-minimal-e/fqs1984] showed these are the only unitary
theories with $c<1$; Cappelli, Itzykson and Zuber [@virasoro-minimal-e/ciz1987] classified their modular invariants by pairs of
ADE Dynkin diagrams $(G, G^\prime)$ with Coxeter numbers $m$ and $m+1$.

The surviving labels are the exponents of the E diagram ($E_6$: 1, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11; $E_7$: 1, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 17; $E_8$: 1, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 29), so the lightest primary is $\phi_{k,k}$ with $k = 4, 5, 7$ and $\Delta_{\rm gap} = \frac{k^2-1}{2m(m+1)}$.

theories.name: Compact boson ($c=1$ circle branch)
theories.summary: A free scalar valued in a circle of radius $R$: a one-parameter family of $c=1$ CFTs, rational when $R^2$ is rational.
theories.description:
Convention: $X \sim X + 2\pi R$ with $T$-duality $R \to 2/R$ and self-dual radius $R = \sqrt2$. Vertex operators $V_{n,w}$ ($n, w \in \mathbb{Z}$) have $(h, \bar h) = \big(\tfrac12(\tfrac{n}{R} + \tfrac{wR}{2})^2, \tfrac12(\tfrac{n}{R} - \tfrac{wR}{2})^2\big)$, i.e. $\Delta = \frac{n^2}{R^2} + \frac{w^2R^2}{4}$ and spin $nw$. (Ginsparg's radius is $r = R/2$.)

The Virasoro primaries are the $V_{n,w}$ and the $U(1)$ currents $\partial X$, $\bar\partial X$ ($\Delta = 1$). The gap is $\min(1/R^2, R^2/4)$, maximised at the self-dual point where the symmetry enhances to $SU(2)\times SU(2)$ and the theory is the $SU(2)_1$ WZW model. Orbifolds of $SU(2)_1$ by cyclic groups $C_n$ give the points $R = n\sqrt2$. At $R = 2\sqrt2$ this branch meets the orbifold branch.

Convention: $X \sim X + 2\pi R$ with $T$-duality $R \to 2/R$ and self-dual radius $R = \sqrt2$. theories.name: Free Dirac fermion (2d)
aliases: Free massless Dirac fermion in two dimensions
Massless Thirring model at zero coupling
theories.summary: A free massless Dirac fermion (two Majorana fermions with a common spin structure): a $c = 1$ fermionic CFT with $U(1)_V\times U(1)_A$ symmetry and a mixed anomaly between them. Summed over spin structures it is the compact boson at $R = 2$ (equivalently $R = 1$).
theories.description:
A complex fermion built from two Majorana fermions ($\psi_i$, $\bar\psi_i$ with $i = 1, 2$) that share
one spin structure [@free-dirac-fermion-2d/ginsparg-lectures, Sec. 8.2; @free-dirac-fermion-2d/ktt2019, Sec. 3.1]. Its holomorphic
component $\psi_L \propto \psi_1 + i\psi_2$ has weight $(\tfrac12, 0)$ and its antiholomorphic component
$\psi_R \propto \bar\psi_1 + i\bar\psi_2$ has weight $(0, \tfrac12)$; $c = \bar c = 1$. This is a
**fermionic** theory: it needs a spin structure.

The continuous symmetry is $U(1)_L\times U(1)_R = (U(1)_V\times U(1)_A)/\mathbb{Z}_2$, where the common
$\mathbb{Z}_2$ is $(-1)^F$, with a mixed 't Hooft anomaly between $U(1)_V$ and $U(1)_A$ (the 2d chiral
anomaly): the two cannot be coupled to background gauge fields consistently at the same time [@free-dirac-fermion-2d/ktt2019, Eq. (3.2)]. There is also charge conjugation. The discrete chiral transformation of one
Majorana component exchanges $U(1)_V$ and $U(1)_A$; in the bosonic description it is $T$-duality
[@free-dirac-fermion-2d/ktt2019, Sec. 3.1].

The four spin-structure partition functions are the squares of the Majorana ones [@free-dirac-fermion-2d/ginsparg-lectures, Eq. (8.12)]:
$$Z_{\rm NS} = \left|\frac{\theta_3}{\eta}\right|^2,\qquad Z_{\widetilde{\rm NS}} = \left|\frac{\theta_4}{\eta}\right|^2,\qquad Z_{\rm R} = \left|\frac{\theta_2}{\eta}\right|^2,\qquad Z_{\widetilde{\rm R}} = \left|\frac{\theta_1}{\eta}\right|^2 = 0 .$$
Summing instead over the spin structures of the two Majoranas independently gives $Z_{\rm Ising}^2$
[@free-dirac-fermion-2d/ginsparg-lectures, Eq. (8.14)], a different bosonic theory on the orbifold branch of $c = 1$
[@free-dirac-fermion-2d/ktt2019, Fig. 1].

### Bosonization
Summing over the common spin structure (gauging $(-1)^F$) gives
$$\tfrac12\left(\left|\tfrac{\theta_3}{\eta}\right|^2 + \left|\tfrac{\theta_4}{\eta}\right|^2 + \left|\tfrac{\theta_2}{\eta}\right|^2 + \left|\tfrac{\theta_1}{\eta}\right|^2\right) = Z_{\rm circ}\ \text{at Ginsparg's radius } r = 1$$
[@free-dirac-fermion-2d/ginsparg-lectures, Eq. (8.13)]. Ginsparg's $r$ is $R/2$ in the convention of the compact-boson entry, so this is
the member $R = 2$, equivalently $R = 1$ by $T$-duality. Karch, Tong and Turner find $R = 2$ in the same
convention ($S = \frac{R^2}{8\pi}\int(d\theta)^2$, $\theta \sim \theta + 2\pi$, $T$-duality $R \to 2/R$,
self-dual radius $\sqrt2$) from dualities alone: gauging $\mathbb{Z}_2 \subset U(1)_V$ must reproduce
the $T$-dual description [@free-dirac-fermion-2d/ktt2019, Sec. 3.3]. The compact boson is therefore not equivalent to the Dirac
fermion itself, but to the Dirac fermion coupled to a dynamical $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge field. At $R = 2$
the chiral fermions are $\psi_L \propto e^{-i\theta_L}$, $\psi_R \propto e^{i\theta_R}$, which are not
local operators of the boson, while the boson's $e^{i\theta}$ comes from the twisted sector
([@free-dirac-fermion-2d/ktt2019, Eq. (3.15)] and the paragraph after it). The mass term $\bar\psi\psi$ maps to
$-\cos\tilde\theta$ of the dual boson.

The Thirring coupling $\frac{g}{2}(\bar\psi\gamma^\mu\psi)^2$ is exactly marginal and moves along the
compact-boson line, with $(2/R)^2 = 1 + g/\pi$ [@free-dirac-fermion-2d/ktt2019, Eq. (3.16)], following Coleman [@free-dirac-fermion-2d/coleman1975].

theories.name: $\mathcal{N}=2$ minimal models
theories.summary: The unitary $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal theories with $c = \frac{3k}{k+2}$, $k \geq 1$: the coset $SU(2)_k\times U(1)_2/U(1)_{k+2}$ and the infrared limit of the Landau–Ginzburg model $W = \Phi^{k+2}$. This entry is the diagonal (A-series) model.
theories.description:
The $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal algebra has unitary representations with $0 < c < 3$ only at $c = \frac{3k}{k+2}$, $k = 1, 2, \dots$ (Boucher–Friedan–Kent). The minimal model at level $k$ is the coset $\frac{SU(2)_k\times U(1)_2}{U(1)_{k+2}}$ (Di Vecchia–Petersen–Yu–Zheng), the $SU(2)/U(1)$ case of the Kazama–Suzuki construction. Fields are labelled by $(l, m, s)$ with $l = 0, \dots, k$, $m \in \mathbb{Z}_{2(k+2)}$, $s \in \mathbb{Z}_4$, $l + m + s$ even and $(l, m, s) \sim (k-l, m+k+2, s+2)$; even $s$ is the Neveu–Schwarz (NS) sector, odd $s$ the Ramond (R) sector. In the standard range $s \in \{0, 1\}$, $|m - s| \le l$,
$$h^l_{m,s} = \frac{l(l+2) - m^2}{4(k+2)} + \frac{s}{8}, \qquad q^l_{m,s} = \frac{m}{k+2} - \frac{s}{2},$$
with $q$ the $U(1)$ R-charge, normalized so that $G^\pm$ have charge $\pm1$.

The NS chiral primaries are $(l, l, 0)$, with $h = \frac{q}{2} = \frac{l}{2(k+2)}$. Spectral flow by half a unit maps them to the $k+1$ Ramond ground states $(l, l+1, 1)$, with $h = \frac{c}{24}$, the lowest weight allowed in the R sector.

The A-series model at level $k$ is the conjectured infrared limit of the Landau–Ginzburg model of one chiral superfield with superpotential $W = \Phi^{k+2}$, part of the correspondence between $\mathcal{N}=2$ minimal models and the A-D-E simple singularities (Martinec; Vafa–Warner). Witten tested it by computing characters from the Landau–Ginzburg path integral with twisted boundary conditions. Gepner models, orbifolds of tensor products of minimal models, are exactly solvable points in the moduli spaces of Calabi–Yau sigma models (Gepner).

### Modular invariants
This entry is the diagonal (A-series) model. The often-quoted A-D-E classification of $\mathcal{N}=2$ minimal models applies to the space-time supersymmetric ones, in which spectral flow by half a unit on both sides maps the NS$\otimes$NS sector to the R$\otimes$R sector; their partition functions combine an A, D or E invariant of $SU(2)_k$ with the diagonal invariant of the $U(1)$ factor (Gray, §3.1). Many other partition functions appeared in early work (Gepner; Ravanini–Yang). Without the space-time supersymmetry condition Gannon classified all modular invariant partition functions: the A-D-E labels then group many distinct partition functions (several each for $E_6$, $E_7$, $E_8$), and their number at level $k$ is unbounded as $k$ grows. Gray argued that each is realized by an orbifold of the diagonal model or of an exceptional space-time supersymmetric model.

### Spectrum files
The spectrum files ($k = 1, \dots, 8$) are the bosonic diagonal coset theory
$$Z = \sum_{(l,m,s)/\sim} |\chi^l_{m,s}|^2,$$
one term for each of the $2(k+1)(k+2)$ field-identification orbits of the branching functions $\chi^l_{m,s}$. It contains NS$\otimes$NS and R$\otimes$R states with $s_L = s_R$ and no NS$\otimes$R states. This is the diagonal invariant $Z = \sum_{(a,c)\in Q_k}|\chi_{a,c}|^2$ of Cordova–Rizi (their eq. (2.31)) and of Gray (eq. (4) with $M$ the identity), where $\chi_{a,c}$ are the characters of the even and odd fermion-number parts of the $\mathcal{N}=2$ representations. It is the bosonization of the fermionic $\mathcal{N}=2$ minimal model, in which $G^\pm$ are local fields of weight $(\frac32, 0)$: fermionizing the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ generated by the Verlinde line $L_{(k,k+2)}$ gives back the fermionic theory (Chen–Duan–Jia–Lee, supplement A). In the bosonic theory the supercurrents appear only paired with antiholomorphic fermionic states, the lowest being the four states $G^a\bar G^b$ ($a, b = \pm$) at $(h, \bar h) = (\frac32, \frac32)$.

The blocks are computed from the branching identity $\chi^{SU(2)_k}_l(\tau,z)\,\Theta_{s,2}(\tau,z) = \sum_m \chi^l_{m,s}(\tau)\,\Theta_{m,k+2}(\tau,z)$ (Sugawara, eq. (A.16)) with Weyl–Kac characters, and agree with Sugawara's string-function formula (A.18).

theories.name: Free bosons on a torus $T^d$ (Narain CFTs)
theories.summary: The CFTs of $d$ compact free bosons, one for each even self-dual lattice of signature $(d,d)$: a $d^2$-dimensional moduli space $O(d,d;\mathbb{Z})\backslash O(d,d;\mathbb{R})/(O(d)\times O(d))$ with $c = d$, containing the compact boson ($d=1$) and level-one WZW points.
theories.description:
The sigma model on a torus $T^d$ with constant metric $G$ and $B$-field has $c_L = c_R = d$ and a $U(1)^d\times U(1)^d$ current algebra. These theories are believed to be the most general ones with these central charges and abelian current algebras [@narain-cft/mw2020]. Momenta and windings combine into a vector $(p_L, p_R)$ of a lattice $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^{d,d}$, with inner product $p_L\cdot p_L' - p_R\cdot p_R'$, and
$$Z_\Lambda(\tau,\bar\tau) = \frac{1}{|\eta(\tau)|^{2d}}\sum_{(p_L,p_R)\in\Lambda} q^{p_L^2/2}\,\bar q^{p_R^2/2}$$
(Afkhami-Jeddi, Cohn, Hartman and Tajdini (ACHT) [@narain-cft/acht2021, Eq. (2.18)]). Each lattice vector gives a primary with $\Delta = \frac12(p_L^2+p_R^2)$ and spin $\frac12(p_L^2-p_R^2)$. $Z_\Lambda$ is invariant under $T$ because $\Lambda$ is even and under $S$ because it is self-dual. Narain [@narain-cft/narain1986] found this condition for toroidal compactifications of the heterotic string, where the lattice has signature $(26-d', 10-d')$ for $d'$ uncompactified dimensions; Narain, Sarmadi and Witten [@narain-cft/nsw1987] related these theories to conventional toroidal compactification.

**Moduli space.** All even self-dual lattices of signature $(d,d)$ are related by $O(d,d;\mathbb{R})$. Rotations in $O(d)\times O(d)$ leave the spectrum unchanged, and the automorphisms $O(d,d;\mathbb{Z})$ of the lattice (T-dualities) relate equivalent theories, so the moduli space is
$$\mathcal{M}_d = O(d,d;\mathbb{Z})\backslash O(d,d;\mathbb{R})/(O(d)\times O(d))$$
([@narain-cft/gpr1994, Sec. 2.4; @narain-cft/acht2021, Eq. (2.20)]; Maloney and Witten [@narain-cft/mw2020, Eq. (1.1)] use the $SO$ groups). Its real dimension is $d^2$, the number of components of $G$ and $B$ (derived). The Zamolodchikov metric is the homogeneous metric, and the volume is finite for $d > 1$ [@narain-cft/mw2020].

**Currents and gap.** The currents $\partial X^p$, $\bar\partial X^p$ are Virasoro primaries with $\Delta = 1$, so the lightest non-vacuum Virasoro primary has $\Delta = \min(1, \Delta_1)$, where $\Delta_1$ is the smallest $\frac12(p_L^2+p_R^2)$ over non-zero lattice vectors (derived). At special points of the moduli space there are additional currents. At the points of maximal enhancement the symmetry is $G_L\times G_R$ with $G$ simply laced of rank $d$, and the theory is the level-one WZW model of $G$ [@narain-cft/gpr1994]. Rationality is special too: for $d = 2$ the theory is rational exactly when the purely left-moving momenta form a sublattice of finite index in the set of all left-moving momenta, and generically there are none [@narain-cft/gv2004, Sec. 5.2].

### Enhanced symmetry and the largest gap
For $d = 2$ the moduli are the complex structure $\tau$ and the complexified Kähler modulus $\rho$ of the torus. The $(SU(2)\times SU(2))_L\times(SU(2)\times SU(2))_R$ point is $(\tau,\rho) = (i, i)$, and the $SU(3)_L\times SU(3)_R$ point is $\tau = \rho = \frac12 + \frac{\sqrt3}{2}i$ [@narain-cft/gpr1994, Eqs. (2.4.63)–(2.4.65)].

ACHT [@narain-cft/acht2021] bound $\Delta_1$ with the spinning modular bootstrap for $U(1)^d\times U(1)^d$ and search the moduli numerically for the largest $\Delta_1$. The bound is saturated at $d = 1$ by the self-dual radius ($\Delta_1 = \frac12$, proved analytically), at $d = 2$ by the $SU(3)_1$ point ($\Delta_1 = \frac23$, against a numerical bound $\frac23 + 2\times10^{-11}$; an analytic proof is open) and at $d = 4$ by the $SO(8)_1$ point ($\Delta_1 = 1$). Their best lattices for $d = 3, 5, 6, 7, 8$ are the $SU(4)_1$ and $SO(10)_1$ points, the Coxeter–Todd lattice, a lattice not previously known and the Barnes–Wall lattice, with $\Delta_1 = \frac34, 1, \sqrt{4/3}, \sqrt{4/3}, \sqrt2$, below the bootstrap bounds [@narain-cft/acht2021, Table 1, App. B]. For $\Delta_1 > 1$ the Virasoro gap is set by the currents (derived). As $d\to\infty$ there are Narain lattices with $\Delta_1 \geq d/(2\pi e) + o(d)$ [@narain-cft/acht2021].

### Averaging over moduli and U(1) gravity
Maloney and Witten [@narain-cft/mw2020] average $Z$ over $\mathcal{M}_d$ with the normalized Zamolodchikov measure. By the Siegel–Weil formula,
$$\langle Z\rangle = \frac{E_{d/2}(\tau)}{\tau_2^{d/2}|\eta(\tau)|^{2d}},\qquad E_s(\tau) = \sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma_\infty\backslash SL(2,\mathbb{Z})}(\mathrm{Im}\,\gamma\tau)^s,$$
which converges for $d > 2$. This is the sum over handlebodies of the vacuum character $1/|\eta|^{2d}$ of the current algebra, the one-loop partition function of $U(1)^{2d}$ Chern–Simons theory. ACHT [@narain-cft/acht2021] obtained the same result and call the bulk theory U(1) gravity, perturbatively $U(1)^d\times U(1)^d$ Chern–Simons theory with a composite boundary graviton.

### Status
ACHT [@narain-cft/acht2021] conjecture that the ensemble average for $d > 2$ is dual to U(1) gravity. The duality has been checked for the torus partition function; Maloney and Witten [@narain-cft/mw2020] extend the Siegel–Weil formula to higher genus and to disconnected boundaries, where the bulk interpretation is less clear.

theories.name: Non-compact free boson (2d)
aliases: Free boson on the real line
Free massless scalar in two dimensions
theories.summary: A free massless scalar valued in $\mathbb{R}$: a $c = 1$ CFT with a continuous spectrum of vertex operators $e^{ipX}$, $\Delta = p^2$, starting at $\Delta = 0$. It is the $R \to \infty$ limit of the compact boson and has no normalizable $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$-invariant vacuum.
theories.description:
Convention: the same field normalization as the compact-boson entry,
$\mathcal{L} = \frac{1}{8\pi}(\partial X)^2$, which is Tong's $\frac{1}{4\pi\alpha'}(\partial X)^2$ [@noncompact-boson-2d/tong2009] at
$\alpha' = 2$. The vertex operators $V_p = {:}e^{ipX}{:}$, $p \in \mathbb{R}$, are primary with
$h = \bar h = \alpha' p^2/4 = p^2/2$ [@noncompact-boson-2d/tong2009, Sec. 4.3], so $\Delta = p^2$ and the spin is 0. With the
currents $\partial X$, $\bar\partial X$ they generate the theory. The state space is a direct integral
$\int dp\, \mathcal{V}_p \otimes \bar{\mathcal{V}}_p$ of Fock modules over the continuous momentum
[@noncompact-boson-2d/schomerus2006, Eq. (2.9)], and the OPE coefficients are $\delta(p_1 + p_2 - p_3)$ [@noncompact-boson-2d/schomerus2006, Eq. (2.10)].

**Relation to the compact boson.** In the compact-boson entry $V_{n,0}$ has $h = \bar h = n^2/(2R^2)$;
with $p = n/R$ this is $p^2/2$, and as $R \to \infty$ the momenta fill $\mathbb{R}$ while all winding
states become infinitely heavy. Ribault describes this large-$R$ limit as a continuous, diagonal
spectrum, and notes that the compact boson at real radius and this infinite-radius limit are the only
unitary free bosonic theories [@noncompact-boson-2d/ribault2014, Sec. 4.1.3]. Conversely, gauging the $\mathbb{Z}$ generated
by the translation $X \to X + 2\pi R$ gives back the compact boson of radius $R$
[@noncompact-boson-2d/rv2020, Sec. 3.4].

**No normalizable vacuum.** The primaries are only delta-function normalizable,
$\langle V_{p_1}V_{p_2}\rangle \propto \delta(p_1 + p_2)$ [@noncompact-boson-2d/aj2022, Eq. (3.1)]. The identity
is the point $p = 0$ of this continuum, so the $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$-invariant vacuum is not a normalizable
state, and the spectrum has no gap: it starts at $\Delta = 0$. Agia and Jafferis [@noncompact-boson-2d/aj2022] note that, strictly
speaking, the non-compact boson is singular as a CFT, and call its continuous spectrum pathological.

**Torus partition function.** Summing over the continuous momentum gives a result proportional to the
(infinite) length $V$ of the target,
$$Z(\tau) = \frac{V}{2\pi}\,\frac{1}{|\eta(\tau)|^2}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}dp\,(q\bar q)^{p^2/2} = \frac{V}{2\pi\sqrt{2\tau_2}\,|\eta(\tau)|^2},$$
and the combination $1/(\sqrt{\tau_2}\,|\eta|^2)$ is modular invariant ([@noncompact-boson-2d/rv2020, Eq. (3.30)], in their normalization $h = p^2/4$). With $V = 2\pi R$ this is $R/(\sqrt{2\tau_2}\,|\eta|^2)$:
the contribution of the compact-boson path integral without winding around either cycle, which dominates
as $R \to \infty$ ([@noncompact-boson-2d/ginsparg-lectures, Eqs. (8.3), (8.5)]; eq. (8.5) reads $\sqrt{2/\tau_2}\,r/|\eta|^2$ with
$r = R/2$).

With a background charge $Q$ the same field gives the linear dilaton theory, with $c = 1 + 6Q^2$; it is
not unitary for $Q \neq 0$ [@noncompact-boson-2d/ribault2014, Sec. 4.1].

theories.name: $SU(2)_1/I$ (icosahedral $c=1$ orbifold)
theories.summary: One of the three isolated $c=1$ CFTs: the orbifold of the self-dual compact boson ($SU(2)_1$) by the icosahedral group $I \cong A_5$.
theories.description:
The icosahedral rotation group $I \cong A_5$ (order 60) acts on the currents $J^a$, $\bar J^a$ of $SU(2)_1$ through the diagonal $SO(3)$. The only invariant marginal operator, $\sum_a J^a \bar J^a$, has a non-zero three-point coefficient, so it is not exactly marginal: unlike the cyclic and dihedral orbifolds (which lie on the circle and orbifold branches), the $T$, $O$, $I$ orbifolds are isolated points of the $c=1$ moduli space (Ginsparg).

A rotation by angle $2\pi t$ twists the winding by $t$, so its twisted-sector ground state is a scalar Virasoro primary with $h = \bar h = t^2/4$. The smallest rotation in $I$ has order 5, giving $\Delta_{\rm gap} = \frac{1}{2\cdot5^2} = 1/50$; the lightest untwisted invariant has $\Delta = \tfrac12$.

theories.name: SU(2)$_k$ WZW model
theories.summary: The sigma model on the group manifold $SU(2)$ with a Wess–Zumino term at integer level $k$ and the diagonal modular invariant: $c = \frac{3k}{k+2}$, one primary for each spin $j = 0, \frac12, \dots, \frac k2$.
theories.description:
The Wess–Zumino–Witten (WZW) model is the two-dimensional sigma model with target the group manifold $SU(2)$, plus a Wess–Zumino term whose coefficient $k$ must be an integer because the term is defined only modulo $2\pi$ [@su2-wzw/witten1984]. At the coupling $\lambda^2 = 4\pi/k$ the theory is conformal, and the currents $J \sim \partial g\, g^{-1}$ and $\bar J \sim g^{-1}\bar\partial g$ generate two commuting affine $\widehat{su}(2)_k$ algebras. The stress tensor is quadratic in the currents (Sugawara construction), with $c = \frac{3k}{k+2}$, which grows from 1 at $k = 1$ towards 3 as $k \to \infty$.

Unitary highest-weight representations at level $k$ have spin $j = 0, \frac12, \dots, \frac k2$, and any realization of the current algebra by a 2d quantum field theory gives only these integrable representations [@su2-wzw/gepnerwitten1986]. The primary $\Phi_j$ has $h_j = \frac{j(j+1)}{k+2}$; with $l = 2j$, $h_l = \frac{l(l+2)}{4(k+2)}$. Knizhnik and Zamolodchikov [@su2-wzw/kz1984] found these dimensions exactly and showed that correlation functions of primaries obey first-order linear differential equations (the Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov equations).

This entry is the diagonal ($A_{k+1}$) theory, $Z = \sum_{l=0}^{k} |\chi_l|^2$, which exists for every $k$. Cappelli, Itzykson and Zuber [@su2-wzw/ciz1987] classified all modular invariants with non-negative integer multiplicities built from $SU(2)_k$ characters: besides $A_{k+1}$ there is a D-series for even $k \geq 4$ (the orbifold by the centre $\mathbb{Z}_2$, which is the WZW model on $SO(3)$) and three exceptional invariants $E_6$, $E_7$, $E_8$ at $k = 10, 16, 28$. Each has its own entry. The lightest non-vacuum primary is $\Phi_{1/2}$, with $\Delta = \frac{3}{2(k+2)} \leq \frac12$, so the currents ($\Delta = 1$) never set the gap.

At $k = 1$ the theory is the compact boson at the self-dual radius, where the $U(1)$ currents are enhanced to affine $SU(2) \times SU(2)$ at level 1 and $Z = |\chi_0|^2 + |\chi_1|^2$ with $\chi_0 = \eta^{-1}\sum_{n} q^{n^2}$ and $\chi_1 = \eta^{-1}\sum_{n} q^{(n+1/2)^2}$. At $k = 2$, $Z$ equals the partition function of three free Majorana fermions summed over a common spin structure. The coset $SU(2)_k \times SU(2)_1/SU(2)_{k+1}$ has the central charge $c = 1 - \frac{6}{(k+2)(k+3)}$ of the unitary minimal model with $m = k+2$ (the Goddard–Kent–Olive construction), and $SU(2)_k/U(1)$ gives the $\mathbb{Z}_k$ parafermions with $c = \frac{2(k-1)}{k+2}$.
theories.lagrangian: S = -\frac{k}{8\pi}\int d^2x\, \mathrm{tr}\big(g^{-1}\partial^\mu g\, g^{-1}\partial_\mu g\big) + \frac{ik}{12\pi}\int_B \mathrm{tr}\big(\tilde g^{-1}d\tilde g\big)^3, \qquad g \in SU(2)

parameters.description: Level: the integer coefficient of the Wess–Zumino term. In the action, $\mathrm{tr}$ is the trace in the fundamental representation (the normalization of the WZW models page specialized to $SU(2)$, [@su2-wzw/walton1999, Eqs. (2.1)–(2.3)]), the signature is Euclidean with weight $e^{-S}$, and $\tilde g$ extends $g$ to a 3-manifold $B$ bounded by spacetime. The Wess–Zumino term is imaginary, and $e^{-S}$ is independent of the extension because $k$ is an integer; its sign depends on the orientation of $B$.

theories.description:
$\mathcal{N}_m$ denotes the $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal minimal model, the coset $SU(2)_{m-2}\times SU(2)_2/SU(2)_m$ with $c = \frac32 - \frac{12}{m(m+2)}$ ($m=3$ is the tricritical Ising model), made bosonic by summing over spin structures. Weights are $h_{r,s} = \frac{((m+2)r - ms)^2 - 4}{8m(m+2)} + \frac{1-(-1)^{r-s}}{32}$. For even $m$ the invariants come in pairs $\pm$ (the GSO choice): $+$ keeps the Ramond ground state $(c/24, c/24)$ as a scalar, $-$ pairs it as $(c/24, c/24+1)$.

For odd $m$ there is a single invariant. The gap comes from the NS field $(2,2)$: $\Delta_{\rm gap} = \frac{3}{m(m+2)} = \frac14\big(\frac32 - c\big)$.

theories.name: TIM$^2$ with Fibonacci swap
theories.summary: The modular invariant of TIM$^2$ that exchanges only the Fibonacci factors of the two copies.
theories.description: The modular data of TIM factorise as Fibonacci $\boxtimes$ a braided Ising category. Exchanging only the Fibonacci labels, $(f_1 i_1, f_2 i_2) \mapsto (f_2 i_1, f_1 i_2)$, is a braided autoequivalence of Rep(TIM$^2$) and therefore defines a full CFT. Its torus partition function equals that of the orbifold of $\mathrm{PF}_8$ by $\langle r^4, Cr\rangle \cong \mathbb{Z}_2^2$.

theories.name: $X_E = \mathrm{TIM}^2/\mathbb{Z}_4$
theories.summary: Orbifold of TIM$^2$ by $\mathbb{Z}_4 = \langle f_1 s\rangle$; it shares its torus partition function with a different CFT, $X_O$.
theories.description:
The symmetry of TIM$^2$ is the dihedral group $D_4$ of order 8 generated by the spin flips $f_1, f_2$ and the exchange $s$. The orbifolds by $\mathbb{Z}_4$ and by $\langle f_1f_2, s\rangle$ with discrete torsion coincide and give this theory, which is also the block-diagonal bosonized $\mathcal{N}=1$ minimal model $\mathcal{N}_{10}^{(A,E_6)}$.

$X_E$ and $X_O$ have the same chiral algebra and the same torus partition function, but glue left- and right-moving modules differently, so they are not isomorphic as full CFTs.

theories.name: SU(2)$_k$ WZW model, D-series
theories.summary: The $SU(2)_k$ WZW model with the D-type modular invariant, even $k \geq 4$: the orbifold of the diagonal theory by the centre $\mathbb{Z}_2$, equivalently the WZW model on $SO(3)$, with $c = \frac{3k}{k+2}$.
theories.description:
For even $k$ the $SU(2)_k$ characters $\chi_l$ ($l = 2j = 0, \dots, k$, $h_l = \frac{l(l+2)}{4(k+2)}$) admit the Cappelli–Itzykson–Zuber invariant $D_{k/2+2}$ [@su2-wzw-d/ciz1987]. For $k \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ it is block-diagonal,
$$Z = \sum_{l\ \mathrm{even}=0}^{k/2-2} |\chi_l + \chi_{k-l}|^2 + 2|\chi_{k/2}|^2 ,$$
that is, diagonal in the characters of the chiral algebra extended by the simple current $\Phi_{k/2}$ ($l = k$, $h = \frac k4$). For $k \equiv 2 \pmod 4$ it is a permutation invariant,
$$Z = \sum_{l\ \mathrm{even}} |\chi_l|^2 + \sum_{l\ \mathrm{odd}} \chi_l\,\overline{\chi_{k-l}} .$$
At $k = 2$ the D invariant coincides with the diagonal one, so the family starts at $k = 4$.

Both cases are the orbifold of the diagonal theory by its centre $\mathbb{Z}_2$, which acts as $(-1)^{l}$ on the primaries: the untwisted sector keeps even $l$, and the twisted sector adds the integer-spin states $\chi_l\overline{\chi_{k-l}}$ ($l$ even for $k \equiv 0$, odd for $k \equiv 2 \pmod 4$). The $\mathbb{Z}_2$ has a mixed anomaly for odd $k$, so the orbifold exists only for even $k$ [@su2-wzw-d/numasawa2018]. Equivalently, these are the WZW models on the group $SO(3) = SU(2)/\mathbb{Z}_2$, which exist only for even $k$ and have exactly these spectra (Gaberdiel and Gannon [@su2-wzw-d/gaberdielgannon2004, Sec. 2.3], summarizing Gepner and Witten [@su2-wzw-d/gepnerwitten1986] and Felder, Gawędzki and Kupiainen [@su2-wzw-d/fgk1988]).

The orbifold removes $\Phi_{1/2}$, so the lightest primary is $\Phi_1$ ($l = 2$) with $\Delta = 2h_2 = \frac{4}{k+2}$, below the currents for every $k \geq 4$.

At $k = 4$ the extension field has $h = 1$: its five states join the three $SU(2)$ currents to give the eight currents of $SU(3)$. This is the conformal embedding $SU(2)_4 \subset SU(3)_1$, and $Z = |\chi_0 + \chi_4|^2 + 2|\chi_2|^2$ is the partition function of the diagonal $SU(3)_1$ WZW model [@su2-wzw-d/bockenhauerevans1999, Sec. 2.3]. At $k = 16$ the exceptional $E_7$ invariant is obtained from $D_{10}$ by exchanging $\chi_8$ and $\chi_2 + \chi_{14}$ in one chiral half.

theories.name: WZW models $G_k$
theories.summary: Sigma models on a compact simple Lie group $G$ with a Wess–Zumino term at integer level $k$: rational CFTs with $\hat{\mathfrak{g}}_k\times\hat{\mathfrak{g}}_k$ current algebra and $c = k\dim G/(k+h^\vee)$. Diagonal theories for selected $G \neq SU(2)$, including $(E_8)_1$.
theories.description:
The WZW model of a compact, simply connected simple Lie group $G$ at level $k \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ is the sigma model on the group manifold with a Wess–Zumino term (Witten). Its chiral algebra is the affine Lie algebra $\hat{\mathfrak g}_k$ on each side, and the Sugawara stress tensor, a bilinear in the currents, gives
$$c = \frac{k\dim G}{k+h^\vee}, \qquad h_\lambda = \frac{(\lambda,\lambda+2\rho)}{2(k+h^\vee)},$$
with long roots of length$^2$ 2, $\rho$ the Weyl vector and $h^\vee$ the dual Coxeter number. The primary fields carry the integrable highest weights, $(\lambda,\theta) \le k$ for the highest root $\theta$; other fields decouple (Gepner–Witten). Correlation functions of primaries obey the Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov equations, and the characters, given by the Weyl–Kac formula, transform linearly under $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ (Kac–Peterson).

This entry lists the diagonal theories $Z = \sum_\lambda |\chi_\lambda|^2$ for a selection of groups other than $SU(2)$ at low level; $SU(2)_k$ and its non-diagonal invariants have their own pages. As is customary, members are labelled by the current algebra: $SO(N)_k$ means $\mathfrak{so}(N)_k$, whose diagonal theory is the WZW model on the simply connected group $\mathrm{Spin}(N)$. The currents $J^a$ at $(h, \bar h) = (1, 0)$ are Virasoro primaries, so the gap is $\min(1, 2h_{\min})$, where $h_{\min}$ is the lightest non-trivial $h_\lambda$. Several level-one members are free-field theories (lattice bosons or free fermions, see below).

### Level one
For simply-laced $G$ ($SU(N)$, $SO(2N)$, $E_{6,7,8}$) at level 1, $c$ equals the rank $r$ and the theory is the lattice CFT of the root lattice $Q$ (the Frenkel–Kac–Segal vertex-operator construction), with characters $\Theta_{\lambda+Q}/\eta^r$. The current algebra $SO(N)_1$ is realised by $N$ free Majorana fermions, and the diagonal theory is their sum over spin structures, $Z = \tfrac12\big(|\theta_3/\eta|^N + |\theta_4/\eta|^N + |\theta_2/\eta|^N\big)$; this covers $SO(5)_1$, $SU(4)_1 = SO(6)_1$ and $SO(8)_1$. The three 8-dimensional primaries of $SO(8)_1$ have identical characters and are permuted by triality.

$(E_8)_1$ has the vacuum as its only primary, and its character is $j(\tau)^{1/3}$, so $Z = |j(\tau)|^{2/3}$. Its chiral half is the holomorphic CFT of the self-dual $E_8$ lattice ($c = 8$), whose character is modular invariant only up to a phase. Pairs of level-one theories embed conformally in $(E_8)_1$: for $(SU(3)_1, (E_6)_1)$, $((G_2)_1, (F_4)_1)$ and $(SO(8)_1, SO(8)_1)$ the central charges add up to 8, the weights of the non-trivial primaries add up to 1, and $\sum_i \chi_i\tilde\chi_i = j(\tau)^{1/3}$.
theories.lagrangian: S_k[g] = -\frac{k}{8\pi}\int d^2x\, \mathcal{K}\big(g^{-1}\partial^\mu g,\, g^{-1}\partial_\mu g\big) + \frac{ik}{24\pi}\int_B d^3y\, \epsilon^{ijk}\,\mathcal{K}\big(\tilde g^{-1}\partial_i\tilde g,\, [\tilde g^{-1}\partial_j\tilde g,\, \tilde g^{-1}\partial_k\tilde g]\big)

parameters.description: Compact, simply connected simple Lie group; $\mathcal{K}(x,y) = \mathrm{Tr}(\mathrm{ad}_x\mathrm{ad}_y)/2h^\vee$ in the action. Euclidean signature with path-integral weight $e^{-S_k}$: the Wess–Zumino term is imaginary, so it contributes the phase $\exp 2\pi i k\tilde S$ of Walton eq. (2.7), which is independent of the extension $\tilde g$ of $g$ to a ball $B$ bounded by spacetime for integer $k$; its sign depends on the orientation of $B$.

theories.name: SU(2)$_k$ WZW model, exceptional invariants
theories.summary: The three $SU(2)_k$ WZW models with an exceptional Cappelli–Itzykson–Zuber invariant: $E_6$ at $k = 10$, $E_7$ at $k = 16$, $E_8$ at $k = 28$. $E_6$ and $E_8$ have the partition functions of $SO(5)_1$ and $(G_2)_1$.
theories.description:
Besides the A- and D-series, the Cappelli–Itzykson–Zuber classification of modular invariants of $SU(2)_k$ contains three exceptional invariants. With $l = 2j$ and $h_l = \frac{l(l+2)}{4(k+2)}$:
$$\begin{aligned} E_6\ (k=10):&\quad |\chi_0+\chi_6|^2 + |\chi_3+\chi_7|^2 + |\chi_4+\chi_{10}|^2,\\ E_7\ (k=16):&\quad |\chi_0+\chi_{16}|^2 + |\chi_4+\chi_{12}|^2 + |\chi_6+\chi_{10}|^2 + |\chi_8|^2 + \big[(\chi_2+\chi_{14})\,\overline{\chi_8} + \mathrm{c.c.}\big],\\ E_8\ (k=28):&\quad |\chi_0+\chi_{10}+\chi_{18}+\chi_{28}|^2 + |\chi_6+\chi_{12}+\chi_{16}+\chi_{22}|^2. \end{aligned}$$
The diagonal labels $l + 1$ are the exponents of the Dynkin diagram, and $k + 2$ is its Coxeter number (12, 18, 30).

$E_6$ and $E_8$ are block-diagonal and come from conformal embeddings: $SU(2)_{10} \subset SO(5)_1 \cong Sp(4)_1$, through the four-dimensional (spin-$\frac32$) representation of $SU(2)$, which is symplectic, and $SU(2)_{28} \subset (G_2)_1$. The blocks are the characters of the larger algebra: $\chi_0+\chi_6$, $\chi_3+\chi_7$ and $\chi_4+\chi_{10}$ are the basic, spinor and vector characters of $SO(5)_1$, and the two $E_8$ blocks are the two characters of $(G_2)_1$. These theories therefore have the torus partition functions of the diagonal $SO(5)_1$ and $(G_2)_1$ WZW models. The weight-one states of $\chi_6$ (7 of them) and of $\chi_{10}$ (11) join the three $SU(2)$ currents into the 10 currents of $SO(5)$ and the 14 of $G_2$.

$E_7$ is not block-diagonal and does not come from an extension of the chiral algebra. It is the $D_{10}$ invariant of $SU(2)_{16}$ (the D-series theory at $k = 16$) with an automorphism of the extended fusion rules applied to one chiral half, which exchanges $\chi_8$ with $\chi_2 + \chi_{14}$.

The gap is set by the lightest primary kept by each invariant: $l = 3$ ($\Delta = \frac58$) for $E_6$, $l = 4$ ($\Delta = \frac23$) for $E_7$ and $l = 6$ ($\Delta = \frac45$) for $E_8$.

theories.name: Gepner models
aliases: Orbifolds of tensor products of $\mathcal{N}=2$ minimal models
theories.summary: Orbifolds of tensor products of $\mathcal{N}=2$ minimal models onto integral $U(1)$ charges: exactly solvable $\mathcal{N}=(2,2)$ SCFTs with $c = 3, 6, 9$ at special points of the moduli spaces of sigma models on $T^2$, K3 and Calabi–Yau threefolds. Fermionic theories.
theories.description:
A Gepner model starts from the tensor product $(k_1)\cdots(k_r)$ of $\mathcal{N}=2$ minimal models at levels $k_i$, with
$$c = \sum_{i=1}^{r}\frac{3k_i}{k_i+2}.$$
It keeps only the states with integral total $U(1)$ charge, which is an orbifold by $e^{2\pi iJ_0}$ [@gepner-models/greene1997, Sec. 5.3], and aligns the Neveu–Schwarz and Ramond sectors of the factors. For $c = 6$, GHV [@gepner-models/ghv2012, App. C] write it as a $\mathbb{Z}_H$ orbifold with $H = \mathrm{lcm}(k_i+2)$, whose spectrum obeys the charge-integrality and spin-alignment conditions. With $c = 9$, these models give space-time supersymmetric, tachyon-free, modular invariant string compactifications with no free parameters [@gepner-models/gepner1988]. They are fermionic $\mathcal{N}=(2,2)$ theories; the $c = 6$ members have $\mathcal{N}=(4,4)$ symmetry, as K3 sigma models. This entry uses the diagonal (A-type) invariant of every factor.

**Geometry.** Gepner [@gepner-models/gepner1987] solved heterotic compactifications on K3, on manifolds of $SU(3)$ holonomy and beyond, working out the quintic hypersurface in $\mathbb{CP}^4$ in detail. He conjectured that any supersymmetric compactification with an $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal theory is a compactification on a manifold of $SU(N)$ holonomy, and that every such model with $c = 9$ is a Calabi–Yau compactification [@gepner-models/gepner1987]. For $(3,3,3,3,3)$ he found the symmetries and massless spectrum of the quintic $z_1^5+\dots+z_5^5 = 0$, up to extra massless states expected to become massive under small perturbations, and the Yukawa couplings were later found to agree as well [@gepner-models/greene1997, Sec. 5.2].

**Landau–Ginzburg and Calabi–Yau.** The minimal model at level $k$ is the infrared limit of the Landau–Ginzburg model $W = X^{k+2}$, so the tensor product is the Landau–Ginzburg model $W = \sum_j X_j^{k_j+2}$. For $r = d+2$ factors, $c = 3d$ is equivalent to $\sum_j \frac{1}{k_j+2} = 1$: $W$ is then homogeneous with degree equal to the sum of the weights, and $W = 0$ is a Calabi–Yau hypersurface in a weighted projective space. The identification of the $X_j$ as homogeneous coordinates is exactly the Gepner quotient by $e^{2\pi iJ_0}$ [@gepner-models/greene1997, Sec. 5.3]. Greene, Vafa and Warner [@gepner-models/gvw1989] showed in this way that all of Gepner's models correspond to strings on algebraic varieties in weighted projective spaces. In Witten's gauged linear sigma model, a $U(1)$ gauge theory with Fayet–Iliopoulos parameter $r$, the theory flows to the Calabi–Yau sigma model for $r \gg 0$ and to a Landau–Ginzburg orbifold for $r \ll 0$ [@gepner-models/witten1993, Sec. 3.1]. The Landau–Ginzburg description looks like the analytic continuation of the Calabi–Yau sigma model to negative Kähler class [@gepner-models/witten1993].

Gepner models typically describe Calabi–Yau manifolds of small volume [@gepner-models/mt2001]. Gukov and Vafa [@gepner-models/gv2004] note that for the quintic the Gepner point is the only point of the moduli space where the CFT is known exactly.
