theories.summary: $U(N)_k$ Chern–Simons theory coupled to a fundamental complex scalar, in the 't Hooft limit. At $N=\infty$ a two-parameter family of CFTs in $(\lambda, \lambda_6)$, where the conformal vacuum is stable, equivalent to Chern–Simons theory coupled to a critical (Gross–Neveu) fermion.
theories.description:
One complex scalar $\phi$ in the fundamental of $U(N)$, coupled to a $U(N)$
Chern–Simons gauge field at level $k$, with $\lambda = N/k$ as in the fermionic family
($k$ in the dimensional-reduction convention, $-1<\lambda<1$). The scalar mass and the
quartic coupling $(\bar\phi\phi)^2$ are tuned to zero. The sextic coupling
$\tfrac{\lambda_6}{3!\,N^2}(\bar\phi\phi)^3$ is classically marginal (conventions of
[@cs-quasi-bosonic-3d/aharony2012]; their earlier paper [@cs-quasi-bosonic-3d/aharony2011] used real scalars and $\lambda = 4\pi N/k$).

### Planar conformal manifold and finite $N$
At $N=\infty$ the beta function of $\lambda_6$ vanishes to all orders in perturbation
theory, so there is a
two-parameter family of CFTs labelled by $\lambda$ and $\lambda_6$ [@cs-quasi-bosonic-3d/aharony2011, Sec. 3]. At finite $N$ a beta function for $\lambda_6$ of order $1/N$ is
generated. Their two-loop result [@cs-quasi-bosonic-3d/aharony2011, Eqs. (9), (11)] for the $O(N)$ theory has, for $N\ge10$, two lines of
zeros $\lambda_6^\pm(\lambda)\propto\lambda^2$, of which $\lambda_6^+$ is IR-stable, so at
large finite $N$ and small $\lambda$ there is a one-parameter family of CFTs labelled by
$\lambda$ alone; without Chern–Simons coupling, $\lambda_6 > 0$ is IR-free. So $\lambda_6$
is a free parameter only of the planar theory.

The conformal vacuum must also be stable, which restricts $\lambda_6$. Dey et al. [@cs-quasi-bosonic-3d/dey2018]
computed the exact large-$N$ Landau–Ginzburg potential for $\bar\phi\phi$ on both the
unHiggsed and the Higgsed branch. Writing $\lambda_6 = 24\pi^2\lambda^2(1+x_6)$, it is
bounded below only for $\tfrac43\big(\tfrac{1}{(2-|\lambda|)^2}-1\big) \le x_6 \le
\tfrac43\big(\tfrac{1}{\lambda^2}-1\big)$, that is
$8\pi^2\lambda^2\big(\tfrac{4}{(2-|\lambda|)^2}-1\big) \le \lambda_6 \le 8\pi^2(4-\lambda^2)$.
As $\lambda\to0$ this becomes $0 \le \lambda_6 \le 32\pi^2$: below the free theory the
potential is unbounded along $\bar\phi\phi\to+\infty$, and at the upper end conformal
symmetry can be broken spontaneously (the Bardeen–Moshe–Bander phenomenon)
[@cs-quasi-bosonic-3d/aharony2011, Sec. 3.3]. At $|\lambda|=1$ the range shrinks to the single
point $\lambda_6 = 24\pi^2$ ($x_6 = 0$).

The planar data below do not depend on
$\lambda_6$; among planar two- and three-point functions it enters only
$\langle J_0J_0J_0\rangle$.

At $N=\infty$ the spectrum is that of the free theory: conserved currents $J_s$ and one
scalar $J_0 = \bar\phi\phi$ of dimension 1. The planar correlators are those of the
Maldacena–Zhiboedov quasi-bosonic theories, with $\tilde N = 2N\sin(\pi\lambda)/(\pi\lambda)$,
$\tilde\lambda = \tan(\pi\lambda/2)$ and a third parameter set by $\lambda_6$.

### Bosonization
The theory is dual at large $N$ to $U(N_f)$ Chern–Simons theory coupled to a fundamental
fermion at its Gross–Neveu (critical) point, with the same map
$|\lambda_b| + |\lambda_f| = 1$, ${\rm sign}(\lambda_b) = -{\rm sign}(\lambda_f)$,
$N_f = |k_b| - N_b$, and with the sextic couplings related by
$\lambda^b_6 = 8\pi^2(1-|\lambda_f|)^2(3 - 8\pi\lambda_f\lambda^f_6)$, where
$\tfrac{N}{3!}\lambda_6^f\sigma^3$ is the cubic term of the Hubbard–Stratonovich field
$\sigma\sim\bar\psi\psi$ on the fermionic side [@cs-quasi-bosonic-3d/gurari2012; @cs-quasi-bosonic-3d/aharony2012b].
The critical fermion with $\lambda^f_6 = 0$ corresponds to $\lambda_6 = 24\pi^2\lambda^2$.
As $|\lambda|\to1$ the fermionic description becomes weakly coupled: the large-$N$
Gross–Neveu model. A double-trace $(\bar\phi\phi)^2$ deformation, with the mass tuned,
flows to Chern–Simons theory with critical bosons, the quasi-fermionic family.

theories.summary: $U(N)_k$ Chern–Simons theory with a fundamental Dirac fermion, at large $N$ with $\lambda = N/k$ fixed. It interpolates between free fermions ($\lambda=0$) and the critical $U(N)$ vector model ($|\lambda|\to1$), and is equivalent to Chern–Simons theory with critical bosons.
theories.description:
One two-component Dirac fermion $\psi$ in the fundamental of $U(N)$, coupled to a
$U(N)$ Chern–Simons gauge field at level $k$, with the fermion mass tuned to zero.
At finite $N$ the theory is still conformal [@cs-quasi-fermionic-3d/gurari2012]; unlike the scalar
theory it has no classically marginal coupling. In the 't Hooft limit $N, k\to\infty$
with $\lambda = N/k$ fixed, $\lambda$ becomes continuous. Here $k$ is the level defined by dimensional reduction, related to the
Yang–Mills-regularized level by $|k| = |k_{\rm YM}| + N$, so that $-1 < \lambda < 1$
[@cs-quasi-fermionic-3d/giombi2011; @cs-quasi-fermionic-3d/aharony2015]. The $O(N)_k$ version with Majorana fermions has the same planar
even-spin correlators [@cs-quasi-fermionic-3d/aharony2012].

At $N=\infty$ the spectrum does not depend on $\lambda$: the single-trace operators are the
currents $J_s$ ($s = 1, 2, \dots$; odd spins appear for $U(N)$), which are conserved at
$N=\infty$, and one scalar $J_0 = \bar\psi\psi$ of dimension 2 [@cs-quasi-fermionic-3d/giombi2011]. Maldacena
and Zhiboedov [@cs-quasi-fermionic-3d/maldacena2012] showed that the slightly broken higher-spin symmetry fixes all planar
three-point functions in terms of two parameters, $\tilde N$ (the normalization of
$\langle TT\rangle$, counted in free real scalars) and $\tilde\lambda$; they call such
theories quasi-fermionic. For this theory $\tilde N = 2N\sin(\pi\lambda)/(\pi\lambda)$ and
$\tilde\lambda = \tan(\pi\lambda/2)$ [@cs-quasi-fermionic-3d/gurari2012]. The singlet sector is conjectured
to be dual to a parity-violating Vasiliev higher-spin theory in AdS$_4$ [@cs-quasi-fermionic-3d/giombi2011].

### Bosonization
The same planar correlators arise from $U(N_b)_{k_b}$ Chern–Simons theory coupled to a
fundamental scalar at its Wilson–Fisher (critical) point, with
$|\lambda_b| + |\lambda_f| = 1$, ${\rm sign}(\lambda_b) = -{\rm sign}(\lambda_f)$ and
$N_b/|\lambda_b| = N_f/|\lambda_f|$, i.e. $|k_b| = |k_f|$ and $N_b = |k_f| - N_f$
[@cs-quasi-fermionic-3d/aharony2012; @cs-quasi-fermionic-3d/gurari2012; @cs-quasi-fermionic-3d/aharony2012b, Eq. (5.30)]. So $|\lambda|\to1$
is the weakly coupled critical boson. The thermal free energies also match [@cs-quasi-fermionic-3d/aharony2012b].
Precise finite-$N$ versions, related by level-rank duality, were proposed by Aharony [@cs-quasi-fermionic-3d/aharony2015],
for example $SU(N)_k$ with $N_f$ scalars $\leftrightarrow$ $U(k)_{-N+N_f/2,\,-N+N_f/2}$ with
$N_f$ fermions in Yang–Mills regularization (with the Legendre transform on one side).
They are conjectures supported by large-$N$ computations.

theories.name: 3d cubic fixed point ($N=3$)
aliases: Cubic fixed point of three scalars
theories.summary: The fixed point of three real scalars with a cubic-symmetric quartic interaction. Cubic anisotropy is relevant at the $O(3)$ (Heisenberg) point, so for one sign of it cubic magnets flow here; the exponents differ from Heisenberg ones by less than $10^{-3}$.
theories.description:
Three real scalars with the most general quartic potential invariant under the cubic
group (sign flips and permutations of the three components). In the $\epsilon$-expansion
the quartic couplings $(u, v)$ have, besides the free theory, three fixed points: three
decoupled Ising models ($u = 0$), the $O(3)$ point ($v = 0$) and the cubic point
($u, v \neq 0$) [@cubic-3d/aharony1973].
The cubic term $\sum_i \phi_i^4$ is a singlet plus a component of the rank-4 traceless
symmetric operator $t_4$ of $O(3)$, so the stability of the $O(3)$ point is decided by
$\Delta_{t_4}$. The bootstrap proves $\Delta_{t_4} < 2.99056$ [@cubic-3d/chester2020] and Monte
Carlo gives $\Delta_{t_4} = 2.9858(6)$ [@cubic-3d/hasenbusch2023], so the $O(3)$ point is unstable and the cubic
point is the stable one. Depending on the sign of the anisotropy, the transition of a
cubic system is either continuous and governed by this fixed point, or first order
[@cubic-3d/hasenbusch2023].

Because $3 - \Delta_{t_4} \approx 0.014$ is so small, the cubic point lies close to
the $O(3)$ point and the flow between them is extremely slow: the leading irrelevant
cubic-invariant scalar has $\Delta = 3 + \omega_2$ with $\omega_2 = 0.0133(8)$.
Conformal perturbation theory around $O(3)$, with $\delta = \Delta_X - 3 \approx 0.01$ at
the cubic point, shifts $\Delta_\phi$ and $\Delta_s$ only at order $\delta^2$, while
$\Delta_t$ (rank 2) shifts at order $\delta$ [@cubic-3d/chester2020]. Monte Carlo confirms that
$\nu$ and $\eta$ barely move.

The numerical bootstrap has not yet isolated this fixed point. Single-correlator bounds
with cubic symmetry have singlet-sector kinks that coincide with the $O(N)$ ones
[@cubic-3d/stergiou2018], and mixed-correlator studies [@cubic-3d/kousvos2018; @cubic-3d/kousvos2019] found an island that
contains the decoupled Ising theory and a candidate "Platonic" CFT, whose dimensions do
not match the cubic fixed point found in Monte Carlo [@cubic-3d/chester2020; @cubic-3d/hasenbusch2023].

theories.name: 3d deconfined quantum critical point (NCCP$^1$, $SO(5)$)
theories.summary: Status disputed: the Néel–VBS transition of spin-1/2 square-lattice magnets, described by scalar QED$_3$ with $N=2$ complex scalars (the NCCP$^1$ model) with emergent $SO(5)$. It may be a unitary CFT, a weakly first-order transition near complex fixed points, or a multicritical point.
theories.description:
Two complex scalars $z_\alpha$ (spinons) coupled to a noncompact $U(1)$ gauge field, with
one $SU(2)$-invariant mass tuned. It was proposed as the continuum theory of a direct,
continuous transition between Néel and columnar valence-bond-solid (VBS) order of spin-1/2
antiferromagnets on the square lattice. The Néel vector is $z^\dagger\vec\sigma z$ and the
VBS order parameter is the minimal monopole; the square lattice allows only quadrupled
monopoles, argued to be irrelevant at the transition. Sign-free lattice realizations include
$J$–$Q$ spin models, 3d classical loop models and the cubic dimer model.

At the transition the Néel (3 components) and VBS (2 components) order parameters are
found numerically to combine into a vector $\Phi$ of an emergent $SO(5)$. The driving
operator is then a component of the rank-2 symmetric tensor $T$ (as is the charge-2
monopole), and a continuous transition requires the $SO(5)$ singlet $S$ to be irrelevant.
Proposed dual descriptions with the same anomalous $SO(5)$ include the $SO(5)$ nonlinear
sigma model with a Wess–Zumino–Witten term, QED$_3$–Gross–Neveu with $N_f = 2$ and
$SU(2)$ gauge theory with $N_f = 2$ fermions; the resulting duality web implies that
NCCP$^1$ is self-dual [@dqcp-3d/wang2017].

### Status
**Numerics.** Loop-model simulations up to linear size $L = 512$ see no conventional
first-order signal, but finite-size scaling fails: the estimate of $\nu$ drifts from
$0.62(1)$ ($L \le 64$) to $0.476(18)$ ($L \ge 256$), and finite-size estimates of
$\eta_{\rm N\acute eel}$ and $\eta_{\rm VBS}$ drift to negative values, which unitarity
forbids, while correlators at $r \ll L$ give $\eta \approx 0.25$ [@dqcp-3d/nahum2015a]. Early
$J$–$Q$ simulations gave $\nu = 0.78(3)$ [@dqcp-3d/sandvik2007].

**Bootstrap.** For a unitary $SO(5)$-invariant CFT, an irrelevant singlet $S$ requires
$\Delta_\Phi > 0.76$, whereas the measured value is $\Delta_\Phi \approx 0.63$
([@dqcp-3d/nakayama2016]; Simmons-Duffin made the same observation [@dqcp-3d/nakayama2016, fn. 33]; the bound $0.76$ is quoted in
[@dqcp-3d/poland2019; @dqcp-3d/gorbenko2018]). Li [@dqcp-3d/li2022] also excludes the lattice and perturbative estimates once
$S$ is assumed irrelevant. So the measured exponents cannot belong to a unitary $SO(5)$
CFT without a relevant singlet.

**Interpretations.** (i) A weakly first-order, pseudo-critical transition, with walking RG
flow near a pair of complex fixed points (complex CFTs), which would explain the drifts
[@dqcp-3d/nahum2015a; @dqcp-3d/wang2017; @dqcp-3d/gorbenko2018]. The fuzzy-sphere study of the $SO(5)$
WZW model sees approximate conformal symmetry and a singlet $\Delta_S$ that drifts from
slightly irrelevant to slightly relevant with system size, supporting this [@dqcp-3d/zhou2024].
(ii) A tricritical point, at which the singlet $S$ is relevant too: bootstrap bounds for
$SO(5)$ CFTs with one relevant singlet are saturated by the large-$N$ monopole dimensions
extrapolated to $N = 2$ and predict $\Delta_S \approx 2.36$ [@dqcp-3d/chester2024], and $J$–$Q$
simulations find weak first-order transitions controlled by a nearby $SO(5)$ multicritical point [@dqcp-3d/takahashi2024] (preprint).
The values below are effective exponents from specific studies, not settled CFT data.

theories.name: 3d free Majorana fermion
theories.summary: A free massless two-component Majorana fermion in three dimensions; two of them form a free Dirac fermion. The free Dirac fermion is a node of the 3d duality web: it is dual to the $O(2)$ Wilson–Fisher fixed point coupled to $U(1)_1$ Chern–Simons theory.
theories.description:
A two-component Majorana fermion $\psi$ has $\Delta_\psi = 1$. Its mass operator
$\bar\psi\psi$ ($\Delta = 2$) is odd under parity and time reversal, so these
symmetries forbid a mass. A gapless Majorana fermion protected by time reversal
appears on the surface of a $3+1$d topological superconductor [@free-fermion-3d/grover2014]. Coupling $N$ Majorana fermions to a real pseudoscalar through
$\phi\,\bar\psi_i\psi_i$, with the scalar mass tuned, gives the $O(N)$
Gross–Neveu–Yukawa fixed points.

Two Majorana fermions form one two-component Dirac fermion $\Psi$, with an $O(2)$
symmetry ($U(1)$ charge and charge conjugation). Data below are per Majorana fermion
unless stated; for a Dirac fermion $F$ and $C_T$ are twice as large. A single Dirac
fermion has the parity anomaly: with its $U(1)$ coupled to a background gauge field it
is time-reversal invariant only as the boundary of a $3+1$d topological insulator
[@free-fermion-3d/seiberg2016].

### Duality web
Seiberg, Senthil, Wang and Witten [@free-fermion-3d/seiberg2016] take as a seed the duality between a free Dirac
fermion coupled to a background spin$^c$ connection $A$ and the $O(2)$ Wilson–Fisher
scalar whose $U(1)$ is gauged by a dynamical $b$ with a level-1 Chern–Simons term,
$$i\bar\Psi\gamma^\mu D^{A}_\mu\Psi \;\longleftrightarrow\; |D_b\phi|^2 - |\phi|^4 + \tfrac{1}{4\pi}\,b\,db + \tfrac{1}{2\pi}\,b\,dA .$$
Gauging background fields and adding Chern–Simons counterterms then gives a web of
dualities [@free-fermion-3d/seiberg2016; @free-fermion-3d/karch2016], including bosonic
particle–vortex duality (the $O(2)$ model and scalar QED$_3$) and its fermionic
counterpart, which relates the free Dirac fermion to a Dirac fermion coupled to a
dynamical $U(1)$ gauge field. The fermionic version was proposed by Son [@free-fermion-3d/son2015] for the
half-filled Landau level, and by Wang and Senthil [@free-fermion-3d/wangsenthil2015] and by Metlitski and Vishwanath [@free-fermion-3d/mv2016] for
topological-insulator surfaces; Seiberg et al. [@free-fermion-3d/seiberg2016] give it
with properly quantized Chern–Simons terms. These are infrared dualities, conjectured
rather than proven.

theories.name: 3d Gross–Neveu–Yukawa models ($O(N)$ family)
theories.summary: Critical points of $N$ two-component Majorana fermions coupled to a real pseudoscalar through $\phi\,\bar\psi_i\psi_i$, with $O(N)$ symmetry; for $N\ge2$ equivalently the UV fixed points of the Gross–Neveu four-fermion model. $N=1$ has emergent $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetry.
theories.description:
$N$ counts two-component Majorana fermions, as in the member entries: $N=2$ is one
two-component Dirac fermion, $N=4$ one four-component Dirac fermion, $N=8$ two of them.
Papers that use $N_f$ four-component Dirac fermions have $N = 4N_f$ ([@gny-3d/fei2016]; Diab
et al. [@gny-3d/diab2016] write $N = \tilde N\,{\rm Tr}\,\mathbb{1}$). The pseudoscalar $\sigma\sim\phi$ is odd
under parity and time reversal; the only relevant parity-even singlet is expected to be
$\epsilon\sim\phi^2$, whose coefficient is tuned [@gny-3d/erramilli2022].

The Gross–Neveu model [@gny-3d/grossneveu1974],
$\mathcal{L} = \bar\psi_i\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu\psi_i + \tfrac{g}{2}(\bar\psi_i\psi_i)^2$,
is non-renormalizable in $2<d<4$, but it has an interacting UV fixed point, under control in
the $1/N$ expansion, at which $\sigma\sim\bar\psi_i\psi_i$ has $\Delta = 1 + O(1/N)$. Its
flow to the IR ends at $N$ free Majorana fermions [@gny-3d/klebanov2011]. The Yukawa
theory below is its UV completion [@gny-3d/zinnjustin1991; @gny-3d/fei2016]: the GNY infrared fixed point
is the GN ultraviolet fixed point. This equivalence requires $N\ge2$: for a single
Majorana fermion $(\bar\psi\psi)^2$ vanishes identically [@gny-3d/fei2016], so the $N=1$ member
is defined only as the infrared fixed point of the Yukawa theory, where it has emergent
$\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetry (the super-Ising model).

### Chiral Ising variants are different CFTs
The "chiral Ising" GNY models have two species $\psi_{L}$, $\psi_{R}$ of $N/2$ Majorana
fermions with opposite Yukawa couplings, $\phi(\bar\psi_L\psi_L - \bar\psi_R\psi_R)$, and
symmetry $O(N/2)^2\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$. Erramilli et al. [@gny-3d/erramilli2022, Sec. 2.4] show that this is a
different fixed point: fermion loops with an odd number ($\ge 5$) of Yukawa vertices
cancel there but not in the $O(N)$ model, so the two differ first at order $1/N^3$ in
$\Delta_\phi$ and at high loop order in the $\epsilon$-expansion. The lattice transitions to
charge-density-wave order on the honeycomb lattice (spinless, $N=4$; spinful, $N=8$)
are in the chiral class, while the $d_{x^2-y^2}+id_{xy}$ pairing transition of $d$-wave
superconductors is in the $O(8)$ class [@gny-3d/erramilli2022, Sec. 2.5]. No chiral-class data
are used in this family.

### Large $N$
The expansions below are in $d=3$ with $N$ counting Majorana fermions
[@gny-3d/erramilli2022, Table 2; @gny-3d/fei2016, Eq. (2.49)] (both with the same $N$). At $N=\infty$, $\Delta_\psi = 1$,
$\Delta_\sigma = 1$ and $\Delta_\epsilon = 2$; the singlet sector is conjectured to be dual
to the type B Vasiliev higher-spin theory in AdS$_4$ (as reviewed in [@gny-3d/aharony2012]).

theories.summary: Two four-component Dirac fermions coupled to an $O(3)$ vector order parameter. It describes the transition of the half-filled honeycomb Hubbard model from a Dirac semimetal to an antiferromagnetic Mott insulator.
theories.description:
The spin-1/2 electrons of graphene's honeycomb lattice form two four-component
Dirac fermions ($N=8$ Majorana components). An on-site repulsion $U$ drives a
continuous transition to Néel order, described by coupling the fermions to a
three-component order parameter through $\vec\phi\cdot\bar\psi\vec\sigma\psi$.
The Néel order parameter breaks $SU(2)$ spin symmetry, and it gaps the fermions.

Unlike the chiral Ising case, there is no conformal bootstrap island yet, and the
quantum Monte Carlo estimates disagree beyond their error bars, especially for
$\eta_\psi$. The values below are the three most recent large-scale studies.

theories.description:
A real pseudoscalar $\phi$ coupled to one Majorana fermion through $\phi\bar\psi\psi$.
At the critical point the theory has emergent $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetry: it is the
Wess–Zumino model of one real superfield with a cubic superpotential.
It describes the time-reversal-breaking transition on the surface of a $3+1$d
topological superconductor, reached by tuning a single parameter.

Supersymmetry relates the leading operators: $\sigma\sim\phi$, its fermionic partner
$\psi$ and $\epsilon \sim \phi^2$ have $\Delta_\psi = \Delta_\sigma + \tfrac12$ and
$\Delta_\epsilon = \Delta_\sigma + 1$. The same island is found by the GNY bootstrap
without assuming supersymmetry, which supports its emergence.

theories.name: 3d Gross–Neveu–Yukawa model, $N=2$
theories.summary: The critical point of 2 two-component Majorana fermions coupled to a real pseudoscalar order parameter, with $O(2)$ symmetry. It describes a single two-component Dirac cone at an Ising ordering transition.
theories.description:
$N=2$ Majorana fermions $\psi_i$ (one two-component Dirac fermion) coupled through
$\phi\,\bar\psi_i\psi_i$ to a real scalar that is odd under parity (time reversal).
When the scalar orders, the fermions become massive and parity is broken. The
critical point has a single relevant parity-even singlet, $\epsilon \sim \phi^2$.

It describes a single Dirac cone, for example on the surface of a topological insulator or in lattice models with one Dirac cone, at a transition where an Ising order parameter gaps it. Quantum Monte Carlo of such a model (SLAC fermions with on-site repulsion, ferromagnetic order) agrees with the bootstrap for $\eta_\phi$ and $\eta_\psi$.

The values below are from the bootstrap of mixed fermion–scalar correlators, which
confines the theory to an isolated island. They assume that the second parity-odd
singlet $\sigma'$ is irrelevant; a later bootstrap bounds $\sigma'$ and $\epsilon'$
above 3 at this $N$, so only $\sigma$ and $\epsilon$ are relevant singlets.
Lattice models usually realize the closely related chiral GNY class with
$O(N/2)^2\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry, whose low-lying dimensions are expected to be
nearly the same.

theories.description:
$N$ counts two-component Majorana fermions and is even ($N/2$ two-component Dirac
fermions). The Lagrangian is usually written with $N_f$ four-component Dirac fermions,
$N = 4N_f$ [@gny-xy-3d/fei2016]; Zerf et al. [@gny-xy-3d/zerf2017] and Li et al. [@gny-xy-3d/li2017] call $N_f$ "$N$", and their values are
converted here. The complex scalar $\phi = \phi_1 + i\phi_2$ couples through
$\bar\psi(\phi_1 + i\gamma_5\phi_2)\psi$, so the theory is invariant under
$\psi\to e^{i\alpha\gamma_5}\psi$, $\phi\to e^{-2i\alpha}\phi$. When $\phi$ orders, this
$U(1)$ is broken and the fermions are gapped; the mass $m^2|\phi|^2$ is tuned to
criticality. The Yukawa theory is the UV completion of the Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model
$\tfrac{g}{2}[(\bar\psi\psi)^2 - (\bar\psi\gamma_5\psi)^2]$, as in the Gross–Neveu case
[@gny-xy-3d/fei2016].

For $N=2$ (one two-component Dirac fermion, $N_f = 1/2$) the fixed point is expected to
be the $\mathcal{N}=2$ Wess–Zumino model with $W = \Phi^3$, with emergent supersymmetry; the
chiral $U(1)$ becomes the $R$-symmetry ([@gny-xy-3d/fei2016, Sec. 4.1]; four-loop check by Zerf et al. [@gny-xy-3d/zerf2017]).

For $N=8$ ($N_f = 2$: the spin-1/2 electrons of graphene) the class describes
superconducting transitions of the Dirac semimetal and the transition to a Kekulé
valence-bond solid [@gny-xy-3d/zerf2017]. The Kekulé order parameter has a $\mathbb{Z}_3$ cubic
anisotropy; Li, Jiang, Jian and Yao [@gny-xy-3d/li2017] argue that the Dirac fermions make it irrelevant at
this fixed point, and they find continuous transitions in sign-free quantum Monte Carlo
for $N_f = 2,\dots,6$.

### Large $N$
The expansions below are from [@gny-xy-3d/fei2016, Eq. (3.33)], in $d=3$ with the same $N$. The
leading fermion anomalous dimension is twice that of the $O(N)$ Gross–Neveu model.
At $N=\infty$, $\Delta_\psi = \Delta_\phi = 1$ and $\Delta_{|\phi|^2} = 2$.
theories.lagrangian: \mathcal{L} = \bar\psi_j\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu\psi_j + g\,\bar\psi_j(\phi_1 + i\gamma_5\phi_2)\psi_j + |\partial\phi|^2 + m^2|\phi|^2 + \lambda|\phi|^4, \quad j = 1,\dots,N/4 \text{ four-component Dirac} \quad (m^2 \text{ tuned})

theories.name: 3d Ising CFT
theories.summary: The conformal field theory at the critical point of the 3d Ising model; the infrared fixed point of $\phi^4$ theory with one real scalar.
theories.description:
Describes the liquid–vapour critical point, uniaxial magnets, and many other
continuous phase transitions with an order parameter odd under a $\mathbb{Z}_2$
symmetry. It is the IR endpoint of the flow from the free massless scalar
triggered by the relevant $\phi^4$ coupling, with the mass tuned to criticality.

It has exactly two relevant scalar operators, $\sigma$ ($\mathbb{Z}_2$-odd) and
$\epsilon$ ($\mathbb{Z}_2$-even), matching the two parameters (field and
temperature) that must be tuned to reach the critical point.
Its most precise data come from the numerical conformal bootstrap applied to
mixed correlators of $\sigma$, $\epsilon$ and $T_{\mu\nu}$.
theories.lagrangian: \mathcal{L} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial\phi)^2 + \tfrac{1}{2} m^2 \phi^2 + \tfrac{\lambda}{4!}\phi^4 \quad (m^2 \text{ tuned to criticality, flow to the IR})

three_point_structures.name: scalar–scalar–spin-$\ell$, blocks $z^h\bar z^{\bar h}+\dots$
three_point_structures.description: The scalar–scalar–spin-$\ell$ structure of $\langle\phi_1\phi_2 O_{\Delta,\ell}\rangle$, external scalars unit-normalized, with its coefficient normalized by the conformal blocks, as the source defines it: in the conformal block expansion of $\langle\phi_1\phi_2\phi_3\phi_4\rangle$ the exchange of $O$ contributes $\lambda_{12O}\lambda_{43O}\,G^{r,s}_{h,\bar h}(z,\bar z)$, with $h = \frac{\Delta-\ell}{2}$, $\bar h = \frac{\Delta+\ell}{2}$, $r = \frac{\Delta_{12}}{2}$, $s = \frac{\Delta_{34}}{2}$, and the blocks start as $z^h\bar z^{\bar h}$ [@ising-3d/simmonsduffin2016, Eq. (A.16), p. 71] (the source writes the coefficient $f$ and does not write the three-point function itself). At $\ell = 0$ it is the three-scalar structure. In this normalization the Ward identity gives $\lambda_{\sigma\sigma T}/\lambda_{\epsilon\epsilon T} = \Delta_\sigma/\Delta_\epsilon$ and $\lambda_{\phi\phi T}^2 = \frac{3}{8}\Delta_\phi^2\, C_T^{\rm free}/C_T$ (free scalar: $3/32$). The sign depends on the order of the two external operators: $\lambda_{43O} = (-1)^\ell \lambda_{34O}$ [@ising-3d/simmonsduffin2016, p. 71]. In embedding space (derived below, not written in the source) it is $2^{\ell/2}$ times the scalar–scalar–spin-$\ell$ structure $V_{3,12}^\ell$ [@ising-3d/costa2011, Sec. 4.2.1, Eqs. (4.10)–(4.12)], with $P_{ij} \equiv -2P_i\cdot P_j$ [@ising-3d/costa2011, Eq. (2.9)] and $O$ unit-normalized as $\langle O(P_1,Z_1)\,O(P_2,Z_2)\rangle = H_{12}^\ell/P_{12}^{\Delta+\ell}$ [@ising-3d/costa2011, Eqs. (4.9), (4.15)].
three_point_structures.relation: A coefficient in this structure is $2^{-\ell/2}$ times the coefficient of the same three-point function in the structure $[(Z_{123}\cdot\zeta)^\ell - \text{traces}]K_3$ of [@ising-3d/poland2019, Eqs. (22)–(24)] ($V_{3,12}^\ell$ in embedding space). Other papers normalize spinning blocks differently, by spin-dependent factors [@ising-3d/simmonsduffin2016, Eq. (A.17)]. Why $2^{-\ell/2}$: on the Poincaré section $V_{3,12}^\ell$ with unit-normalized operators becomes the structure of [@ising-3d/poland2019, Eqs. (22)–(24)] [@ising-3d/costa2011, Eqs. (4.30), (4.37)]; the exchange of $O$ contributes to the four-point function the product of the two coefficients in that structure times blocks that start as $(-\frac{1}{2})^\ell z^h\bar z^{\bar h}$ [@ising-3d/poland2019, Eqs. (52), (54)] (ordered $12O$, $34O$), and the product of the two coefficients in this structure (ordered $12O$, $43O$) times blocks that start as $z^h\bar z^{\bar h}$ [@ising-3d/simmonsduffin2016, Eq. (A.16)] ($2^\ell$ times those of [@ising-3d/poland2019], as its Table I lists). With the sign $(-1)^\ell$ of reordering $34O \to 43O$, the products differ by $2^{\ell}$, so each coefficient by $2^{\ell/2}$, with the same choice of the sign of $O$. At $\ell = 2$ it agrees with the Ward identity: the square of the stress-tensor coefficient in the structure of [@ising-3d/poland2019] is $\frac{d^2}{(d-1)^2}\Delta_\phi^2/C_T$ for unit-normalized $T$ [@ising-3d/poland2019, Eq. (86)], with $C_T^{\rm free} = d/(d-1)$ [@ising-3d/poland2019, Eq. (87)], i.e. $\frac{3}{2}\Delta_\phi^2\,C_T^{\rm free}/C_T$ in 3d: 4 times the square in this structure, $\frac{3}{8}\Delta_\phi^2\,C_T^{\rm free}/C_T$.

three_point_structures.name: scalar–scalar–spin-$\ell$, $(Z_{123}\cdot\zeta)^\ell$
three_point_structures.description: The scalar–scalar–spin-$\ell$ structure in the normalization that Reehorst et al. use: that of the review of Poland, Rychkov and Vichi [@ising-3d/reehorst2021, p. 6, fn. 3], whose three-point function is the formula above [@ising-3d/poland2019, Eqs. (23)–(24)], with $h_{ijk} \equiv \Delta_i+\Delta_j-\Delta_k$, a polarization $\zeta$ of $O$, and all operators unit-normalized, $\langle O_{\Delta,\ell}(x_1,\zeta_1)O_{\Delta,\ell}(x_2,\zeta_2)\rangle = [(I_{\mu\nu}(x_{12})\zeta_1^\mu\zeta_2^\nu)^\ell - \text{traces}]/(x_{12}^2)^\Delta$ [@ising-3d/poland2019, Eq. (22)]; its blocks start as $(-\frac{1}{2})^\ell z^{(\Delta-\ell)/2}\bar z^{(\Delta+\ell)/2}$ [@ising-3d/poland2019, Eqs. (52), (54)]. The coefficient is antisymmetric for odd $\ell$, $\lambda_{123} = (-1)^\ell\lambda_{213}$ [@ising-3d/poland2019, Eq. (25)]. In embedding space it is the coefficient of $V_{3,12}^\ell$ [@ising-3d/costa2011, Eqs. (4.10)–(4.12), (4.30), (4.37)].
three_point_structures.relation: A coefficient in this structure is $2^{\ell/2}$ times the coefficient of the same three-point function in the block-normalized structure of [@ising-3d/simmonsduffin2016, Eq. (A.16)], twice it at spin 2: the paper notes a factor of 2 relative to the values of [@ising-3d/simmonsduffin2016] from the different block normalization [@ising-3d/reehorst2021, p. 16], and its generalized-free-field coefficients [@ising-3d/reehorst2021, Eq. (2.4)] are $2^\ell$ times those in the normalization of [@ising-3d/simmonsduffin2016] (squares). The same factor follows from the two block normalizations (see the structure of [@ising-3d/simmonsduffin2016, Eq. (A.16)]).

three_point_structures.name: parity-even $\langle TT\epsilon\rangle$
three_point_structures.form: \langle \hat T(X_1,Z_1)\,\hat T(X_2,Z_2)\,\epsilon(X_3)\rangle = \lambda_{TT\epsilon}\,\frac{1}{X_{12}^{\frac{6-\Delta_\epsilon}{2}+2}\, X_{23}^{\frac{\Delta_\epsilon}{2}}\, X_{31}^{\frac{\Delta_\epsilon}{2}}} \Big( V_1^2 V_2^2 + \frac{4(\Delta_\epsilon-4)}{\Delta_\epsilon+2} H_{12} V_1 V_2 + \frac{2(\Delta_\epsilon^2-6\Delta_\epsilon+6)}{\Delta_\epsilon(\Delta_\epsilon+2)} H_{12}^2 \Big)
three_point_structures.description: The parity-even structure of $\langle TT\epsilon\rangle$ as written and normalized by [@ising-3d/chang2024, Eq. (2.2), p. 5], with the unit-normalized stress tensor $\hat T = T/\sqrt{c_T}$, $\langle\hat T\hat T\rangle = H_{12}^2/X_{12}^5$ [@ising-3d/chang2024, Eq. (2.9)], chosen to match the five-point-bootstrap convention of Poland, Prilepina and Tadić [@ising-3d/poland2023]. A choice of these papers, not a standard normalization: other papers normalize this structure differently. The source calls $V_i$ and $H_{ij}$ the standard embedding-space structures of [@ising-3d/costa2011] and writes the points $X_i$; read with the definitions of [@ising-3d/costa2011], $X_{ij} \equiv -2X_i\cdot X_j$ (the $P_{ij}$ of [@ising-3d/costa2011, Eq. (2.9)]), $V_1 \equiv V_{1,23}$, $V_2 \equiv V_{2,31}$ and $H_{12}$ [@ising-3d/costa2011, Eqs. (4.14)–(4.16)], and the unit normalization of $\hat T$ is that of [@ising-3d/costa2011, Eq. (4.9)]. In the $SO(3)_r$ basis it is $-\lambda_{TT\epsilon}\frac{16\Delta_\epsilon}{2+\Delta_\epsilon}\,\mathtt{ScalarParityEven}_{\Delta_\epsilon}$ [@ising-3d/chang2024, Eqs. (2.2)–(2.3)].

theories.name: 3d Ising$^*$ CFT
aliases: Critical point of the 3d $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory
Confinement transition of a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological phase
theories.summary: The 3d Ising CFT with its $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauged: the critical point of the 3d $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory. Its local operators are the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-even Ising operators, and it has a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 1-form symmetry.
theories.description:
Wegner [@ising-star-3d/wegner1971] showed that the 3d Ising model is dual to a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory
(an Ising model on the simple cubic lattice whose Hamiltonian contains products of four
spins), which therefore has a phase transition without a local order parameter. In $2+1$
dimensions the same transition separates a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological phase from a
trivial phase, for example in the toric code in a field, where it is driven by the
condensation of one type of anyon. That anyon field $\phi$ can only be created in
pairs, and $\phi$ and $-\phi$ are indistinguishable, so the critical theory is the Ising
CFT restricted to $\mathbb{Z}_2$-even states, with both periodic and antiperiodic
boundary conditions on a torus [@ising-star-3d/schuler2016].

In modern language, Ising$^*$ is the Ising CFT with its $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 0-form symmetry
gauged. On $\mathbb{R}^3$, or any simply connected space, this does not change the
correlators of $\mathbb{Z}_2$-even local operators, so their dimensions, OPE coefficients
and $C_T$ are those of the 3d Ising CFT; the values below are the Ising values. The
thermal exponent $\nu$ is unchanged. The spin field $\sigma$ is no longer a local
operator: it can only appear at the end of a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ Wilson line. As for any
gauging of a discrete symmetry, the theory acquires a dual $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry, here
a 1-form symmetry, generated by the Wilson lines. The objects charged under it are the
former $\mathbb{Z}_2$ twist lines of the Ising CFT, which become genuine line operators.
Gauging the 1-form symmetry gives back the Ising CFT [@ising-star-3d/gaiotto2015].

The two theories differ on spaces with non-contractible cycles. On a spatial torus the
Ising$^*$ spectrum contains the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-even Ising levels with periodic
boundary conditions, together with the sectors with antiperiodic boundary conditions. It
has four very low-lying levels, the remnant of the four-fold degenerate ground state of the
topological phase; at criticality they scale as $1/L$, like the rest of the spectrum,
instead of becoming exponentially degenerate. Exact diagonalization of the toric code in a field and the $\epsilon$-expansion
agree on this spectrum [@ising-star-3d/schuler2016].

Gauging a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ subgroup of other symmetries gives analogous starred
theories. In XY$^*$, the transition at which fractionalized bosons condense out of a
phase with an emergent $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge field, the physical order parameter is a composite of two
fractionalized fields, and quantum Monte Carlo finds a large anomalous dimension,
$\eta = 1.49(2)$ [@ising-star-3d/isakov2012]. $O(N)^*$ is defined in the same way.

theories.name: 3d Lee–Yang edge singularity CFT
theories.summary: The non-unitary CFT at the Lee–Yang edge singularity, the end of the line of partition-function zeros of the Ising model in an imaginary magnetic field above $T_c$. It is the fixed point of one scalar with an imaginary cubic coupling and has a single relevant primary, $\phi$.
theories.description:
Above the critical temperature, the zeros of the Ising partition function in the
complex magnetic field $h$ lie on the imaginary axis beyond a critical value $h_c(T)$
[@lee-yang-3d/lee1952]. Near this edge their density vanishes as $(h - h_c)^\sigma$, with a
universal edge exponent $\sigma$. Fisher [@lee-yang-3d/fisher1978] described the edge by a scalar field theory with
an imaginary cubic coupling, whose upper critical dimension is 6. The same universality
class describes the repulsive-core singularity of fluids, and, in $d + 2$ dimensions,
branched polymers [@lee-yang-3d/parisi1981].

The only relevant primary is $\phi$. By the equation of motion $\phi^2$ is a descendant
of $\phi$, and the next scalar primary, "$\phi^3$", is irrelevant [@lee-yang-3d/gliozzi2014]. The
exponents follow from $\Delta_\phi$:
$$\sigma = \frac{\Delta_\phi}{3 - \Delta_\phi}, \qquad \eta = 2\Delta_\phi - 1 .$$
$\Delta_\phi \approx 0.21$ lies below the unitarity bound $\tfrac12$. In $d=2$ the
same universality class is the minimal model $\mathcal{M}(2,5)$.

The estimates below come from methods with different, not directly comparable, error
estimates: the $6-\epsilon$ expansion to five loops with resummation [@lee-yang-3d/borinsky2021];
series expansions of the dimer density on bipartite lattices [@lee-yang-3d/butera2012]; the
functional renormalization group [@lee-yang-3d/an2016]; a truncated, non-rigorous bootstrap that
keeps a few operators in the $\phi\times\phi$ OPE [@lee-yang-3d/gliozzi2014], since the positivity-based numerical bootstrap
does not apply to a non-unitary theory; and the fuzzy-sphere regularization of the
Ising model with an imaginary longitudinal field. Two fuzzy-sphere studies disagree.
Arguello Cruz, Klebanov, Tarnopolsky and Xin [@lee-yang-3d/arguellocruz2025] find $\Delta_\phi = 0.214(2)$, consistent
with the series and five-loop values. Fan, Dong and Vishwanath [@lee-yang-3d/fan2025] find
$\Delta_\phi \approx 0.29$, and note that assuming a heavier next irrelevant operator in
their finite-size fit moves it towards the other estimates. Elias Miró and Delouche [@lee-yang-3d/eliasmiro2025] find
the low-lying fuzzy-sphere spectrum compatible with the five-loop estimates.

theories.name: 3d minimal $\mathcal{N}=4$ SCFT $\mathcal{T}_{\rm min}$
aliases: $\mathcal{N}=2$ $U(1)_{-3/2}$ Chern–Simons theory with one chiral of charge 1
theories.summary: The infrared fixed point of 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ $U(1)$ Chern–Simons theory at level $-3/2$ with one chiral multiplet of charge 1, conjectured to have emergent $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetry. A rank-0 SCFT, proposed to be the 3d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SCFT with the smallest $F$ and non-zero $C_T$.
theories.description:
The UV theory is an $\mathcal{N}=2$ $U(1)$ vector multiplet with Chern–Simons level $k=-3/2$
coupled to one chiral multiplet $\Phi$ of gauge charge $+1$; the half-integer level is
required by the quantization condition $k \in \mathbb{Z} + Q^2/2$. Gang et al. [@minimal-n4-scft-3d/gang2021] use a
duality between this theory and $U(1)_{3/2}$ with one chiral, so either sign of the level gives
the same SCFT. $F$-maximization gives the superconformal R-charge $R_\Phi = 1/3$, assuming no
emergent abelian flavor symmetry.

Gang and Yamazaki [@minimal-n4-scft-3d/gang2018] conjectured that the infrared SCFT has $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetry, with
the UV symmetries $U(1)_R\times U(1)_{\rm top}$ combining into the $SO(4)$ R-symmetry. Their
evidence: the two-point coefficients of the $U(1)_R$ and $U(1)_{\rm top}$ currents computed by
localization agree exactly; dressed monopole operators with the quantum numbers of the extra
supercurrent multiplets appear in the semiclassical spectrum and the superconformal index; and
two copies of the theory are dual to $T[SU(2)]$ with its diagonal $SU(2)$ gauged at
Chern–Simons level 3 (later refined to include a decoupled $U(1)_2$ topological sector).

The theory has no chiral primary operators that could parametrize a moduli space, so it has
neither a Higgs nor a Coulomb branch (rank 0), and it admits no UV Lagrangian with manifest
$\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetry. Gang, Kim, Lee, Shim and Yamazaki [@minimal-n4-scft-3d/gang2021] associate a pair of
non-unitary TQFTs with any rank-0 $\mathcal{N}=4$ SCFT; for $\mathcal{T}_{\rm min}$ both are
the Lee–Yang TQFT. Their dictionary gives the lower bound
$F \ge -\log\sqrt{(5-\sqrt5)/10}$ for rank-0 SCFTs, which $\mathcal{T}_{\rm min}$ saturates.
The minimality of $F$ and $C_T$ is a conjecture.

theories.name: 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ super-Ising CFT ($W=\Phi^3$ Wess–Zumino model)
aliases: Chiral XY Gross–Neveu–Yukawa fixed point with one Dirac fermion
theories.summary: The infrared fixed point of one $\mathcal{N}=2$ chiral superfield with cubic superpotential $W=\Phi^3$, i.e. a complex scalar and one two-component Dirac fermion. The chiral primary has the exact dimension $\Delta_\Phi = 2/3$.
theories.description:
One chiral superfield $\Phi$: a complex scalar $\phi$ and one two-component Dirac fermion
$\psi$ (in the counting of the GNY entries, $N=2$ two-component Majorana fermions), with
superpotential $W = \tfrac{\lambda}{3}\Phi^3$. The coupling is relevant in $d=3$ and the
theory flows to an interacting $\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFT. The superpotential fixes the
$U(1)_R$ charge $R_\Phi = 2/3$, so $\Delta_\Phi = 2/3$ exactly, and the equation of motion
gives the chiral-ring relation $\Phi^2 = 0$. The theory has no continuous flavor symmetry.
Continued to $d=2$ it becomes the $c=1$ member of the $\mathcal{N}=(2,2)$ minimal series.

In the $\mathcal{N}=2$ bootstrap of $\langle\Phi\bar\Phi\Phi\bar\Phi\rangle$ the theory sits
at a kink of the upper bound on the leading unprotected scalar $[\bar\Phi\Phi]$ at
$\Delta_\Phi = 2/3$. There the extracted $C_T$ has a minimum that agrees with the exact
localization value, and the coefficient of $\Phi^2$ in $\Phi\times\Phi$ vanishes, as the
chiral-ring relation requires.

The same fixed point is reached from the non-supersymmetric chiral XY GNY model with one
Dirac fermion (the Nambu–Jona-Lasinio–Yukawa model with $N=2$), where the scalar mass is
tuned. In $d=4-\epsilon$ its fixed-point couplings obey the supersymmetric relation to order
$\epsilon^2$, and its chiral $U(1)$ becomes the $U(1)_R$ symmetry, so supersymmetry is
emergent (Fei, Giombi, Klebanov and Tarnopolsky). Physically, it describes the transition
between the Dirac semimetal and the $s$-wave superconductor of a single Dirac cone on the
surface of a 3d topological insulator at zero chemical potential, where the Cooper-pair field
becomes the superpartner of the surface fermion (Ponte and Lee; Grover, Sheng and
Vishwanath). Supersymmetry then gives $\eta_\phi = \eta_\psi = 1/3$ exactly.

theories.name: 3d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SQED with $N_f$ flavours
theories.summary: The infrared fixed points of a 3d $\mathcal{N}=4$ $U(1)$ vector multiplet coupled to $N_f$ hypermultiplets of charge 1. Mirror to the necklace (affine $A_{N_f-1}$) quiver; $N_f=1$ is a free twisted hypermultiplet and $N_f=2$ is the self-mirror $T[SU(2)]$.
theories.description:
An $\mathcal{N}=4$ $U(1)$ vector multiplet (in $\mathcal{N}=2$ language, a vector multiplet
and a neutral chiral $\Phi$) coupled to $N_f$ hypermultiplets, i.e. chirals $Q_a$ and
$\tilde Q^a$ of charge $+1$ and $-1$ with $W = \tilde Q^a\Phi Q_a$. $N_f$ counts
hypermultiplets: $2N_f$ complex scalars and $2N_f$ two-component Dirac fermions. The gauge
coupling is relevant, and the theory flows to an SCFT at the origin of the moduli space,
where the Higgs branch (the centred one-instanton moduli space of $SU(N_f)$) meets the
Coulomb branch (with an $A_{N_f-1}$ singularity). The $SU(2)_H\times SU(2)_C$ R-symmetry
fixes $\Delta_Q = \Delta_{\tilde Q} = 1/2$.

Mirror symmetry [@n4-sqed-3d/intriligator1996] identifies the same fixed point with the infrared
limit of $U(1)^{N_f}/U(1)$ with $N_f$ bifundamental hypermultiplets $Q_i$ of neighbouring
factors $U(1)_i\times U(1)_{i+1}$ ($i$ mod $N_f$), arranged in a necklace. It exchanges the
Higgs and Coulomb branches, and masses with Fayet–Iliopoulos parameters. The hidden
$U(1)^{N_f-1}$ topological symmetry of the necklace quiver becomes the $SU(N_f)$ flavor
symmetry of SQED.

The BPS monopole operators $V_\pm$ of magnetic charge $\pm1$ are chiral, with R-charge
and dimension $N_f/2$ [@n4-sqed-3d/borokhov2002; @n4-sqed-3d/gaiotto2008]. At $N_f=1$ they have
$\Delta = 1/2$ and form a free twisted hypermultiplet, which is the content of the basic
mirror pair. At $N_f=2$ they have $\Delta = 1$ and, together with the topological current,
enhance the $U(1)_J$ symmetry of the Coulomb branch to $SU(2)$. For $N_f\ge3$ no monopole has
$\Delta \le 1$ and $U(1)_J$ is not enhanced.

The $S^3$ partition function localizes to a single integral,
$Z = 2^{-N_f}\int d\lambda\,\cosh^{-N_f}(\pi\lambda)$, which is elementary.

theories.name: 3d $O(2)$ model
theories.summary: The conformal field theory of the 3d XY universality class: the infrared fixed point of a complex scalar with a $|\phi|^4$ interaction. It describes the superfluid transition of helium-4.
theories.description:
Describes the λ transition of superfluid helium-4, easy-plane magnets, and, in
$2+1$ dimensions, the superfluid–Mott insulator transition of bosons at integer
filling. It is the IR endpoint of the flow from two free real scalars triggered
by the $O(2)$-invariant quartic coupling, with the mass tuned to criticality.

The lightest scalars in each charge sector are the singlet $s$ (the thermal
operator), the charge-1 order parameter $\phi$, and the charge-2 $t$. Charge-3
scalars are also relevant ($\Delta \approx 2.108$), but the lightest charge-4 scalar
is irrelevant ($\Delta \approx 3.112$). So a $\mathbb{Z}_q$ clock anisotropy
is irrelevant for $q \ge 4$, and $O(2)$ symmetry emerges at the transition of clock
models. Monte Carlo simulations use this to get the most precise exponents.
The dimensions of the lowest charge-$q$ operators agree with the large-charge
effective theory down to $q = 4$.

Bootstrap and Monte Carlo agree. Both disagree with the specific-heat exponent
$\alpha$ measured near the λ point of helium in microgravity, by about $8\sigma$
($\alpha = 2 - 3\nu = -0.01515(7)$ from the Monte Carlo $\nu$, against
$-0.0127(3)$ measured). This discrepancy is unresolved.

By particle–vortex duality, the same fixed point is the critical point of a
charged scalar coupled to a $U(1)$ gauge field (the Abelian Higgs model, in its
"inverted XY" regime). The global $O(2)$ of one description is the topological
$U(1)$ of the other.

theories.name: 3d $O(3)$ model
theories.summary: The conformal field theory of the 3d Heisenberg universality class: the infrared fixed point of three real scalars with an $O(3)$-invariant quartic interaction. It describes the Curie transition of isotropic magnets.
theories.description:
Describes the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic transitions of isotropic
(Heisenberg) magnets. In $2+1$ dimensions it describes the transition between
Néel order and a paramagnet in dimerized quantum antiferromagnets. It is the IR
endpoint of the flow from three free real scalars triggered by the
$O(3)$-invariant quartic coupling, with the mass tuned to criticality.

The lightest scalars are the vector $\phi$ (the order parameter), the rank-2
symmetric traceless tensor $t$, and the singlet $s$ (the thermal operator). The
tensor $t$ is a uniaxial anisotropy, and it is strongly relevant. An easy axis
drives the flow to the 3d Ising CFT, and an easy plane drives it to the 3d
$O(2)$ model.

The lightest rank-4 scalar $t_4$ is relevant, but only barely: the bootstrap
proves $\Delta_{t_4} < 2.99056$, and Monte Carlo gives $\Delta_{t_4} = 2.9858(6)$.
So the $O(3)$ fixed point is unstable to cubic anisotropy, and magnets on a cubic
lattice ultimately flow to the cubic fixed point. The flow is extremely slow, and
the critical exponents barely change: $\nu_{\rm cubic} - \nu_{O(3)} = -0.00061(10)$.

(13), p. 10]. The paper defines its coefficients by the conformal block expansion $\sum_O(-1)^\ell\lambda_{\varphi_1\varphi_2O}\lambda_{\varphi_3\varphi_4O}T^{\mathcal R}g_{\Delta,\ell}$ of four-point functions [@o3-model-3d/chester2020, Eq. (11)], with blocks normalized as in [@o3-model-3d/poland2019, Table I, second line] and four-point $O(3)$ structures $T^{\mathcal R}$ [@o3-model-3d/chester2020, App. C, Eqs. (29), (32), pp. 26–28] normalized to make the coefficients consistent under permutations, checked in free theory [@o3-model-3d/chester2020, Eq. (33)]; it does not write the three-point tensors. This tensor is inferred from them (not stated by the source): contracted over the exchanged operator it reproduces $T^{\mathbf 0^+}_{\mathbf 2^+\mathbf 2^+\mathbf 0^+\mathbf 0^+} = B_{ttss}$, $T^{\mathbf 2^+}_{\mathbf 2^+\mathbf 0^+\mathbf 2^+\mathbf 0^+} = B_{tsts}$, $T^{\mathbf 0^+}_{\mathbf 2^+\mathbf 2^+\mathbf 2^+\mathbf 2^+} = B^1_{tttt}$ and $T^{\mathbf 0^+}_{\mathbf 2^+\mathbf 2^+\mathbf 1^-\mathbf 1^-} = B^1_{tt\phi\phi}$ exactly (checked numerically). The spacetime dependence is that of three scalars.

three_point_structures.description: $\phi$ is the vector ($\mathbf 1^-$) and $t$ the symmetric traceless tensor ($\mathbf 2^+$) of $O(3)$; indices $k$ are symmetrized with their trace removed, operators normalized as in [@o3-model-3d/chester2020, Eq. (13), p. 10]. As for $\langle tts\rangle$, the paper defines the coefficient through four-point structures [@o3-model-3d/chester2020, Eqs. (11), (32)] and does not write this tensor; it is inferred from them (not stated by the source): with the factor $\sqrt2$ it reproduces exactly (checked numerically) $T^{\mathbf 2^+}_{\mathbf 1^-\mathbf 1^-\mathbf 1^-\mathbf 1^-} = B^2_{\phi\phi\phi\phi}+B^3_{\phi\phi\phi\phi}-\frac23B^1_{\phi\phi\phi\phi}$, $T^{\mathbf 1^-}_{\mathbf 2^+\mathbf 1^-\mathbf 2^+\mathbf 1^-} = 2B^2_{t\phi t\phi}$, $T^{\mathbf 2^+}_{\mathbf 1^-\mathbf 1^-\mathbf 0^+\mathbf 2^+} = \sqrt2 B_{\phi\phi st}$ and, with $\langle ttt\rangle$, $T^{\mathbf 2^+}_{\mathbf 2^+\mathbf 2^+\mathbf 1^-\mathbf 1^-}$. In free theory, $t^{ij} = (\phi^i\phi^j - \text{trace})/\sqrt2$ [@o3-model-3d/chester2020, Eq. (33)] gives $\lambda_{\phi\phi t} = 1$ in this structure.

theories.name: 3d $O(4)$ model
theories.summary: The infrared fixed point of four real scalars with an $O(4)$-invariant quartic interaction. It is the expected universality class of the chiral transition of QCD with two massless quark flavours, if that transition is second order.
theories.description:
The $N=4$ member of the $O(N)$ Wilson–Fisher family: the IR endpoint of the flow from
four free real scalars triggered by the $O(4)$-invariant quartic coupling, with the
mass tuned to criticality.

In QCD with two massless flavours the chiral order parameter is
$M_{ij} = \langle \bar q_{Li} q_{Rj}\rangle$. Since the axial $U(1)$ is broken by the
anomaly, $M$ can be restricted to $M = \sigma + i\vec\pi\cdot\vec\tau$, and
$SU(2)_L \times SU(2)_R$ acts on $(\sigma, \vec\pi)$ by $O(4)$ rotations. If the finite-temperature
chiral transition is second order, it is therefore expected in the $O(4)$ class
[@o4-model-3d/pisarski1984; @o4-model-3d/rajagopal1993].

The most precise exponents come from Monte Carlo simulations of an improved lattice
$\phi^4$ model, in which the leading correction to scaling is tuned away. A mixed-correlator
bootstrap, assuming one relevant vector and one relevant singlet, confines
$(\Delta_\phi, \Delta_s)$ to a small region, larger than for $N = 2, 3$ [@o4-model-3d/kos2015];
the Monte Carlo $\nu$ and $\eta$ lie inside it.

Anisotropies are classified by the rank-$l$ traceless symmetric operators $t_l$. The
rank-2 (uniaxial), rank-3 and rank-4 (cubic) anisotropies are all relevant. In
particular $\Delta_{t_4} < 3$ by a clear margin, so cubic anisotropy drives the flow to
a cubic fixed point with distinct exponents ($\nu = 0.7202(7)$, $\eta = 0.0371(2)$ for
$N=4$ [@o4-model-3d/hasenbusch2023]).

theories.name: 3d $O(N)$ model (Wilson–Fisher family)
theories.summary: The infrared fixed points of $N$ real scalars with an $O(N)$-invariant quartic interaction, one for each $N$. They include the Ising ($N=1$), XY ($N=2$) and Heisenberg ($N=3$) classes, self-avoiding walks ($N\to0$), and the large-$N$ limit, conjectured to be dual to higher-spin gravity in AdS$_4$.
theories.description:
$N$ counts real scalar components, $\vec\phi \in \mathbb{R}^N$. For each $N$ the
critical point is reached from $N$ free scalars by the $O(N)$-invariant quartic
coupling, with the mass tuned to criticality [@on-model-3d/wilson1972]. The order parameter
is the vector $\phi_i$, and the singlet $s \sim \vec\phi^{\,2}$ is the thermal
operator, with $\nu = 1/(3-\Delta_s)$ and $\eta = 2\Delta_\phi - 1$.

For every $N \ge 1$ the fixed point is a unitary CFT with a single relevant
$O(N)$ singlet, $s$ (the tuned mass); the next singlet has
$\Delta_{s'} = 3 + \omega$ with $\omega > 0$. So it is stable against
$O(N)$-invariant perturbations. Whether it is stable against cubic anisotropy depends on $N$:
the lightest rank-4 traceless symmetric scalar $t_4$ is irrelevant at $N=2$,
relevant at $N=3$ (barely; see the $O(3)$ page) and clearly relevant at $N=4$
(Monte Carlo: $3-\Delta_{t_4} = -0.108(6)$, $0.013(4)$, $0.125(5)$ for $N=2,3,4$
[@on-model-3d/hasenbusch2011]) and at large $N$, where $\Delta_{t_4} = 2 + O(1/N)$. So for
$N \ge 3$ a cubic anisotropy drives the flow to the cubic fixed point or, for the
other sign, to a first-order transition.

The family continues to real $N$. At non-integer $N$ the theory is not unitary
[@on-model-3d/binder2019]. The limit $N \to 0$ describes self-avoiding walks [@on-model-3d/degennes1972]
and is a logarithmic CFT.

### Large $N$
Introducing a Hubbard–Stratonovich field, $\mathcal{L} = \tfrac12(\partial\vec\phi)^2 + \tfrac{1}{2\sqrt N}\,\sigma\,\vec\phi^{\,2}$,
the fixed point is described in a $1/N$ expansion in which $\Delta_\phi = \tfrac12$ and
$\Delta_\sigma = 2$ at $N=\infty$; $\sigma$ is the singlet $s$. The expansions below are
in $d=3$. Klebanov and Polyakov [@on-model-3d/klebanov2002] proposed that the singlet sector at large $N$ is dual to
the minimal bosonic Vasiliev higher-spin theory in AdS$_4$, which contains massless
gauge fields of even spin; the free and the critical model correspond to the two
possible boundary conditions on the bulk scalar dual to $\vec\phi^{\,2}$ [@on-model-3d/klebanov2002].
theories.lagrangian: \mathcal{L} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial\vec\phi)^2 + \tfrac{1}{2} m^2 \vec\phi^{\,2} + \tfrac{\lambda}{4!}(\vec\phi^{\,2})^2, \quad \vec\phi\in\mathbb{R}^N \quad (m^2 \text{ tuned to criticality, flow to the IR})

theories.name: 3d $O(m)\times O(n)$ chiral fixed points (frustrated magnets)
theories.summary: Status disputed: the stable ("chiral") fixed point of $m$ coupled $n$-vectors with $O(m)\times O(n)$ symmetry. It exists for large $n$; for frustrated XY and Heisenberg magnets ($m=2$, $n=2,3$) recent bootstrap and $\epsilon$-expansion results favour a first-order transition.
theories.description:
The fields form a real $m\times n$ matrix $\phi_{ar}$: $m$ vectors $\vec\phi_a$ of $n$
components each, with $O(m)$ acting on $a$ and $O(n)$ on $r$. Here $n$ is the number of
spin components, and $m = 2$ for coplanar noncollinear order, as in stacked triangular
antiferromagnets (120° structure) and helimagnets [@on-om-chiral-3d/kawamura1988]. Conventions vary: Nakayama–Ohtsuki [@on-om-chiral-3d/nakayama2015] write
$O(n)\times O(2)$, Reehorst et al. [@on-om-chiral-3d/reehorst2024] $O(N)\times O(2)$ with $N = n$, Henriksson et al. [@on-om-chiral-3d/henriksson2020]
$O(2)\times O(n)$, and Kompaniets et al. [@on-om-chiral-3d/kompaniets2020] $O(n)\times O(m)$, all with $n$ the number
of spin components.

In the $\epsilon$-expansion the couplings $(u, v)$ have four fixed points for
$n > n^+(m)$: Gaussian, the $O(mn)$ point ($v=0$), the stable chiral point ($v>0$) and
the unstable antichiral point. At $n = n^+(m)$ the chiral and antichiral points merge
and move into the complex plane; below it no stable fixed point remains and the
transition is first order (other regimes, with collinear fixed points at $v<0$,
occur at smaller $n$). At large $n$ the chiral point exists in $2<d<4$ and is
computable in $1/n$. The question is the value of $n^+(2)$ in $d=3$.

### Status
- **Against a fixed point at $n = 2, 3$.** The six-loop $\epsilon$-expansion, resummed,
  gives $n^+(2) = 5.96(19)$ in $d=3$ [@on-om-chiral-3d/kompaniets2020]. The functional RG finds
  $n^+(2) \simeq 5.1$ in $d=3$ and explains the nonuniversal exponents seen in experiments by
  a slow flow without a fixed point, i.e. weak first-order transitions [@on-om-chiral-3d/delamotte2004]. Wang–Landau Monte Carlo finds first-order transitions in
  the XY and Heisenberg stacked triangular antiferromagnets [@on-om-chiral-3d/ngo2008a; @on-om-chiral-3d/ngo2008b].
- **For a fixed point.** Six-loop perturbation theory directly in $d=3$, resummed,
  finds a stable chiral fixed point for $n = 2, 3$ [@on-om-chiral-3d/pelissetto2001], of
  focus type, with complex correction exponents [@on-om-chiral-3d/calabrese2002].
  Delamotte et al. [@on-om-chiral-3d/delamotte2010] argue that these fixed points are spurious, because the
  exponents depend strongly on the resummation parameters and the loop order; a
  complex correction exponent is also incompatible with a unitary fixed point
  [@on-om-chiral-3d/reehorst2024]. Monte Carlo of the Heisenberg antiferromagnet up to $384^3$
  reports a continuous transition with $\nu = 0.52(1)$ [@on-om-chiral-3d/nagano2019].
- **Bootstrap.** Nakayama and Ohtsuki [@on-om-chiral-3d/nakayama2015] found kinks for $n = 3, 4$ that they identified
  with the chiral and collinear fixed points. Henriksson, Kousvos and Stergiou [@on-om-chiral-3d/henriksson2020] found
  islands for $O(2)\times O(3)$ under gap-saturation assumptions ($\nu = 0.639(7)$),
  but also that the kinks attributed to the large-$n$ chiral point fade between
  $n = 5$ and $6$. Reehorst, Rychkov, Sirois and van Rees [@on-om-chiral-3d/reehorst2024] followed the island of the
  chiral point continuously in $(d, n)$ and found that in $d = 3$ it disappears
  already at some $n > 3.78$, i.e. $n^+(2) > 3.78$, which favours first-order
  transitions at $n = 2, 3$.

theories.name: 3d percolation CFT
aliases: Bond and site percolation universality class
theories.summary: The critical point of bond and site percolation in three dimensions, the $q \to 1$ limit of the $q$-state Potts model. A non-unitary CFT, expected to be logarithmic, whose exponents are known most precisely from Monte Carlo simulations.
theories.description:
In bond (site) percolation each bond (site) of a lattice is occupied independently with
probability $p$, and at $p = p_c$ an infinite cluster first appears. Writing the
$q$-state Potts model in terms of Fortuin–Kasteleyn clusters, the limit $q \to 1$ is a sum
over bond percolation configurations; the partition function becomes trivial, but its
correlation functions describe the geometry of critical clusters. The field theory is a
cubic theory of $q-1$ scalars with an $S_q$-invariant coupling, continued to $q - 1 \to 0$,
with upper critical dimension 6.

Two basic scaling fields are the thermal operator $\epsilon$, an $S_q$ singlet coupled to
$p - p_c$, with $\Delta_\epsilon = 3 - 1/\nu$; and the order parameter (spin) operator
$\sigma$ in the $(q-1)$-dimensional representation of $S_q$, whose two-point function
vanishes unless the two points lie in the same cluster. Its dimension is
$\Delta_\sigma = 3 - d_f = \beta/\nu$, where $d_f$ is the fractal dimension of critical
clusters. $\Delta_\sigma \approx 0.477$ lies below the unitarity bound $\tfrac12$
($\eta < 0$), a direct sign that the theory is not unitary.

The most precise exponents come from Monte Carlo simulations on several lattices with
periodic boundary conditions, analysed by finite-size scaling [@percolation-3d/wang2013; @percolation-3d/xu2014]. The
$6-\epsilon$ expansion is known to five loops [@percolation-3d/borinsky2021], but in $d = 3$ its resummed values are much
less precise. The leading correction-to-scaling exponent $\omega$ is large, though
Monte Carlo estimates of it differ.

### Conformal invariance and logarithms
Conformal invariance of 3d percolation is not proven. Gori and Trombettoni [@percolation-3d/gori2015] tested it
numerically: crossing probabilities in bounded domains are invariant under conformal
maps, most clearly in continuum percolation. As in two dimensions, the CFT is expected to
be logarithmic. Vasseur, Jacobsen and Saleur [@percolation-3d/vasseur2012] found that at $q = 1$ the energy operator
mixes with a logarithmic partner, the field that creates two propagating clusters, so
that suitable two-point functions scale logarithmically. They worked in $d = 2$ but argue
that the mechanism, which rests only on the $S_q$ symmetry, holds in any dimension.

theories.name: 3d QCD (QCD$_3$): $SU(N_c)$ gauge theory with $N_f$ fundamental fermions
aliases: QCD$_3$: $SU(N_c)$ gauge theory with $N_f$ fundamental fermions
theories.summary: $SU(N_c)$ gauge theory without Chern–Simons term, coupled to $N_f$ two-component Dirac fermions in the fundamental representation. It flows to an interacting CFT for large $N_f$; below some $N_*$ the flavor symmetry is expected to break.
theories.description:
**Counting.** $N_f$ counts two-component Dirac fermions, each a fundamental of $SU(N_c)$.
The Chern–Simons level vanishes, which with fundamental fermions requires even $N_f$; the
theory is then parity and time-reversal invariant. Giombi–Tarnopolsky–Klebanov [@qcd3-3d/giombi2016] count
four-component fermions, $N = 4N_f^{(4)} = 2N_f$; their results are converted below.

At large $N_f$ the theory flows to a CFT, and to leading order in $1/N_f$ its data follow
from those of QED$_3$ with group-theory factors: the corrections to $C_T$ and $C_J$ are
those of QED$_3$ times $d(G)/d(r) = (N_c^2-1)/N_c$. For smaller $N_f$, Komargodski and
Seiberg [@qcd3-3d/komargodski2018] conjecture that in a window $0 < N_f < N_*(N_c)$ the flavor symmetry breaks as
$U(N_f) \to U(N_f/2)\times U(N_f/2)$, with the theory conformal for $N_f \geq N_*$;
$N_*$ is not known. With a level $k$, the breaking pattern becomes
$U(N_f/2+k)\times U(N_f/2-k)$ for $2k < N_f < N_*$, and level-rank dualities to bosonic
theories hold for $N_f \leq 2k$; those theories are not part of this entry.

For $N_c = 2$ the fundamental is pseudo-real and the flavor symmetry enlarges to
$Sp(N_f)$. $SU(2)$ with $N_f = 2$ has a manifest $Sp(2) \cong Spin(5)$ and is conjectured
to be dual to the NCCP$^1$ deconfined critical point, whose $SO(5)$ it would explain.
Quantum Monte Carlo of a sign-free fuzzy-sphere realization of the $Sp(N_f)$ sigma model
with a level-1 Wess–Zumino–Witten term, expected to flow to $SU(2)$ QCD$_3$ in its critical
phase, finds such a conformally invariant phase for $N_f \geq 4$ but not for $N_f = 2$,
tentatively placing the edge of the $SU(2)$ conformal window between $N_f = 2$ and $4$
[@qcd3-3d/huffman2026].

theories.name: 3d quantum electrodynamics (QED$_3$) with $N_f$ fermion flavors
theories.summary: A $U(1)$ gauge field coupled to $N_f$ two-component Dirac fermions of unit charge, with no Chern–Simons term. It flows to an interacting CFT at large $N_f$; whether it does so at small $N_f$ (in particular $N_f = 2$) is unsettled.
theories.description:
**Counting.** $N_f$ counts two-component complex (Dirac) fermions. Many papers count
four-component fermions $N_f^{(4)} = N_f/2$ (Giombi–Tarnopolsky–Klebanov [@qed3-3d/giombi2016] also use
$N = 4N_f^{(4)} = 2N_f$); values from them are converted below. $N_f$ is even, so that
parity and time reversal are preserved without a Chern–Simons term (odd $N_f$ has a
parity anomaly).

The Maxwell coupling $e^2$ has mass dimension one, so the theory is free in the UV and
strongly coupled in the IR. At large $N_f$ it flows to an interacting CFT in which the
Maxwell term is irrelevant, and all data below are the leading terms of the $1/N_f$
expansion. Besides local operators built from $\psi_i$ and $f_{\mu\nu}$, the CFT has
monopole operators $M_q$ that carry flux $4\pi q$, $q \in \tfrac12\mathbb{Z}$, so the
minimal monopole $M_{1/2}$ has unit $U(1)_{\rm top}$ charge. Each $M_q$ is a Lorentz
scalar in the $SU(N_f)$ irrep with a rectangular Young diagram of $N_f/2$ rows and
$2|q|$ columns.

$N_f = 4$ describes the $U(1)$ Dirac spin liquid of spin-1/2 magnets, which is more
stable on the triangular and kagome lattices than on bipartite ones; monopoles allowed
by the lattice symmetries can drive confinement. $N_f = 2$ is conjectured to be
self-dual, with $(SU(2)\times U(1)_{\rm top})/\mathbb{Z}_2$ enhanced to $O(4)$, and dual to
the easy-plane NCCP$^1$ model [@qed3-3d/wang2017].

### Status at small $N_f$
Below some $N_f^*$ the IR phase may instead break $SU(N_f) \to SU(N_f/2)\times SU(N_f/2)\times U(1)$,
and the estimates of $N_f^*$ disagree. Lattice simulations with parity-invariant
regularizations [@qed3-3d/karthik2016a; @qed3-3d/karthik2016b] find no bilinear condensate for $N_f = 2, 4, 6, 8$ and scale-invariant
behavior at $N_f = 2$, with mass anomalous dimension $\gamma_m = 1.0(2)$ from Dirac
eigenvalues and $0.8(1)$ from the scalar correlator (so $\Delta = 2-\gamma_m$ for the
flavor-nonsinglet bilinear); earlier lattice work had found symmetry breaking at small
$N_f$. A one-loop $4-2\epsilon$ extrapolation [@qed3-3d/dipietro2016] finds a singlet
four-fermion operator relevant at $N_f = 2, 4$ in our counting. Conformal bootstrap kinks
in $SU(N_f)$-adjoint bounds track the large-$N_f$ spectrum and disappear at small $N_f$,
suggesting $N_f^* \in (2,4)$ [@qed3-3d/li2022a], and imposing irrelevance assumptions excludes the
$N_f = 2$ lattice data, indicating that $N_f = 2$ is not conformal [@qed3-3d/li2022b]. At $N_f = 4$ the
bootstrap gives a closed island compatible with $1/N_f$ [@qed3-3d/albayrak2022], but only under
gap assumptions taken from the $1/N_f$ spectrum; stability of the Dirac spin liquid on
the triangular and kagome lattices requires $\Delta_{M_{1/2}} > 1.046$ and $1.105$
[@qed3-3d/he2022]. The $N_f = 2$ and $N_f = 4$ members should therefore be read as
conjectural CFTs.

theories.name: 3d QED–Gross–Neveu–Yukawa model with $N_f$ fermion flavors
theories.summary: QED$_3$ with $N_f$ two-component Dirac fermions coupled through a Yukawa term to a time-reversal-odd real scalar, tuned to its time-reversal-breaking transition. The $N_f = 2$ member is conjectured to be dual to the NCCP$^1$ deconfined critical point.
theories.description:
**Counting.** $N_f$ counts two-component Dirac fermions, as for QED$_3$. Janssen and He [@qed3-gn-3d/janssen2017]
write $2N$ for this number; their $N$ is $N_f/2$.

The real scalar $\phi$ couples to the flavor-singlet mass $\bar\psi_i\psi_i$, which is odd
under parity and time reversal, so $\phi$ is odd too. Tuning the $\phi$ mass $r$ drives a
transition between a phase with $\langle\phi\rangle = 0$, whose IR limit is plain QED$_3$,
and a phase where $\langle\phi\rangle \neq 0$ gaps the fermions and breaks time reversal.
In $d = 4-\epsilon$ the critical point is stable for every $N_f$; unlike plain QED$_3$, it
does not annihilate with another fixed point at small $N_f$ [@qed3-gn-3d/janssen2017].

$N_f = 2$ is conjectured to be dual to the $SU(2)$-symmetric NCCP$^1$ model (the Néel–VBS
deconfined critical point), and the duality implies the emergent $SO(5)$ of that theory
[@qed3-gn-3d/wang2017]. Under the duality the adjoint bilinear $\bar\psi\sigma^z\psi$ maps to the tuning operator of NCCP$^1$, so
$3 - \Delta_{\rm adj} = 1/\nu_{\rm N\acute eel\text{–}VBS}$. $N_f = 4$ has been proposed for
the transition between the $U(1)$ Dirac spin liquid and a chiral spin liquid on the kagome
lattice.

The large-$N_f$ data below include Aslamazov–Larkin diagrams that exist only for
two-component fermions in $d = 3$; earlier $1/N$ and $\epsilon$-expansion studies with
four-component fermions missed them. At $N_f = 2$ the $1/N_f$ series must be resummed:
the naive values violate unitarity.

theories.name: 3d self-avoiding walk CFT ($O(N \to 0)$ model)
theories.summary: The $N \to 0$ limit of the 3d $O(N)$ Wilson–Fisher fixed point, which describes the large-scale statistics of self-avoiding walks and of dilute polymers in a good solvent. A non-unitary, logarithmic CFT.
theories.description:
De Gennes [@saw-3d/degennes1972] showed that self-avoiding walks are described by the $O(N)$ model at
$N \to 0$: the two-point function $\langle \phi_a(x)\phi_a(0)\rangle$ counts walks
from $0$ to $x$, with the fugacity per step playing the role of temperature, and the
rank-2 operator $\phi_a\phi_b$ ($a \neq b$) creates two mutually avoiding walks. A walk
of $L$ steps has mean squared radius $\propto L^{2\nu}$, and the number of walks
grows as $\mu^L L^{\gamma - 1}$. So $\nu$ is the Flory exponent and the walk has
fractal dimension $d_F = 1/\nu$.

The theory is not unitary. A CFT with $O(N)$ symmetry at non-integer $N$ cannot be
unitary [@saw-3d/binder2019], and $C_T \propto N$ vanishes in the limit. At $N=0$ the
lightest singlet (the energy operator) and the lightest rank-2 traceless symmetric
scalar (the 2-leg operator) become degenerate and form a logarithmic pair, so
correlators acquire logarithms; the stress tensor likewise becomes degenerate with a
traceless symmetric spin-2 partner, which resolves the "$c \to 0$ paradox" [@saw-3d/cardy2013].

The most precise data come from Monte Carlo simulations of walks on the cubic lattice
with the pivot algorithm, for walks of up to $2^{25} \approx 3.4\times 10^7$ steps. The numerical
bootstrap is hampered by the non-unitarity: some squared OPE coefficients have poles at
$N=0$. Shimada and Hikami [@saw-3d/shimada2016] used the bound on the rank-2 dimension at $N = 0.1$, where
unitarity is only weakly violated, and extrapolated to $N = 0$.

theories.name: 3d scalar QED with $N$ complex scalars
theories.summary: A $U(1)$ gauge field coupled to $N$ complex scalars of unit charge, tuned to its Coulomb–Higgs transition. The critical point is a CFT at large $N$ and, by particle–vortex duality, at $N = 1$; at small $N \geq 2$ the transition may be weakly first order.
theories.description:
Scalar QED$_3$ is also called the Abelian Higgs model or the noncompact
$\mathbb{CP}^{N-1}$ model.

**Counting.** $N$ counts complex scalars $z_\alpha$ (so $2N$ real components). The model is
"noncompact": monopole operators are not added to the action, so the critical point has a
$U(1)_{\rm top}$ symmetry whose charged operators are monopoles $M_q$ of flux $4\pi q$,
$q \in \tfrac12\mathbb{Z}$. This entry is the fixed point with $SU(N)$-symmetric potential
and one relevant singlet ($\mathbb{CP}^{N-1}$, or "bQED$_+$"); a second, tricritical
fixed point with the quartic coupling also tuned is not included.

In $SU(N)$ quantum antiferromagnets on bipartite lattices the critical point describes
the transition between Néel order (the Higgs phase, order parameter $z^\dagger T^a z$) and
valence-bond-solid (VBS) order. Lattice Berry phases make the monopoles transform like
the VBS order parameter, so the minimal monopole is the VBS order parameter rather than
an allowed perturbation. The large-$N$ monopole dimensions agree well with quantum Monte
Carlo of such magnets.

At $N = 1$ there is no flavor symmetry. Particle–vortex duality maps the critical point
to the $O(2)$ Wilson–Fisher CFT with the temperature axis reversed ("inverted XY"), with
$U(1)_{\rm top}$ becoming the $O(2)$ charge, so $\Delta_{M_{1/2}} = \Delta_\phi^{O(2)}$ and
$\nu = \nu_{O(2)}$. $N = 2$ is the deconfined quantum critical point between Néel and VBS
order of spin-1/2 magnets, which has its own page.

### Status at small $N$
In $d = 4-\epsilon$ the charged fixed point exists only for $N > N_c$, with
$N_c = 182.95$ at one loop [@scalar-qed3-3d/halperin1974]; the four-loop series, resummed with
input from two dimensions, gives $N_c(d=3) \approx 12.2 \pm 3.9$ [@scalar-qed3-3d/ihrig2019], with a
large spread between resummations. In Monte Carlo simulations of the noncompact lattice
model the Coulomb–Higgs transition is continuous for $N \geq 10$ and weakly first order
for $N = 2, 4$ [@scalar-qed3-3d/bonati2021]. Other lattice realizations of $N = 2$ show
apparently continuous behavior with drifting exponents; see the $N=2$ page.

theories.name: 3d $T[SU(N)]$ theory
aliases: S-duality wall theory of $SU(N)$ $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang–Mills
theories.summary: The self-mirror 3d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SCFT on the S-duality wall of 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ $SU(N)$ super Yang–Mills: the infrared limit of the linear quiver $U(1)\times U(2)\times\dots\times U(N-1)$ with $N$ flavours at the last node, with $SU(N)\times SU(N)$ global symmetry.
theories.description:
The quiver has gauge group $U(1)\times U(2)\times\dots\times U(N-1)$, bifundamental
hypermultiplets between neighbouring nodes and $N$ fundamental hypermultiplets of
$U(N-1)$. Every node is balanced (its number of flavours is twice its rank), so the
$U(1)^{N-1}$ topological symmetry is enhanced in the infrared to $SU(N)$, which acts on the
Coulomb branch; the manifest $SU(N)$ acts on the Higgs branch. The theory is self-mirror:
mirror symmetry exchanges the two $SU(N)$ factors, the Higgs and Coulomb branches, and
masses with Fayet–Iliopoulos parameters. Both branches are the nilpotent cone of
$SL(N,\mathbb{C})$, of complex dimension $N(N-1)$.

Gaiotto and Witten [@t-sun-3d/gaiotto2008] found $T[SU(N)]$ as the boundary theory obtained by S-duality from
Dirichlet boundary conditions of 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ $U(N)$ super Yang–Mills. It is also the
theory on the S-duality wall of $\mathcal{N}=4$ $SU(N)$ super Yang–Mills, and the building
block of the star-shaped quivers that are mirror to class-$\mathcal{S}$ theories reduced to
3d. At $N=2$ it is $\mathcal{N}=4$ SQED with two flavours.

The $S^3$ partition function with masses $m$ and FI parameters $\zeta$ (each in the Cartan of
$SU(N)$) has a closed form that is manifestly mirror symmetric:
$$Z(m;\zeta) = \frac{\sum_{w\in S_N}(-1)^{w}\, e^{2\pi i\sum_j m_{w(j)}\zeta_j}}{i^{N(N-1)/2}\prod_{i<j}2\sinh\pi(m_i-m_j)\,\prod_{i<j}2\sinh\pi(\zeta_i-\zeta_j)}$$
([@t-sun-3d/benvenuti2011]; Nishioka, Tachikawa and Yamazaki [@t-sun-3d/nishioka2011] give the same expression with a
different overall normalization). The conformal point is the limit $m, \zeta \to 0$. At
large $N$, $F \simeq \tfrac12 N^2\log N$, which Assel, Estes and Yamazaki [@t-sun-3d/assel2012] match with the type
IIB supergravity dual, an $AdS_4\times S^2\times S^2$ fibration over a Riemann surface.

theories.name: 3d trivial theory
theories.summary: The normalized trivial bosonic theory: one state on every closed spatial surface and partition function one. Symmetry actions and background responses must be specified when it is used as an RG-flow endpoint.
theories.description:
This is the tensor unit of three-dimensional bosonic topological field theories,
normalized to $Z(M)=1$ and $\mathcal H(\Sigma)=\mathbb C$: Moore and Saxena
[@trivial-tqft-3d/moore2025, Sec. 9] define it by the state space $\mathbb C$ on every spatial manifold and
the identity map on every bordism, so it does not depend on the metric.
It has no intrinsic topological order or chiral gravitational response.
Its only local operator is the identity: the symmetry-TFT construction of this
phase produces no genuine topological defects
[@trivial-tqft-3d/bhardwaj2024, Sec. 4.1.1, Eqs. (4.8)–(4.10)].

### Symmetry-equipped endpoints
This entry alone does not choose a global symmetry group. For the conventional
ungauged Ising disordered phase, equip it with an unbroken $\mathbb Z_2$
whose infrared action is trivial, with response $Z(M,A)=1$ for flat backgrounds
$A$: the trivial $\mathbb Z_2$ phase of Bhardwaj et al.
[@trivial-tqft-3d/bhardwaj2024, Sec. 4.1.1, Eqs. (4.8)–(4.10)]. The flow relation must record this choice.
The nontrivial $\mathbb Z_2$ SPT phase has the same underlying theory but a
different realization of the symmetry [@trivial-tqft-3d/bhardwaj2024, Eqs. (3.5)–(3.6), (4.11)–(4.13)];
a flow to it must say so. Invertible theories that are
nontrivial even without symmetry, such as those with a chiral gravitational
response, are different theories and are not this entry.

### Meaning of the infrared limit
A microscopic massive theory has finite correlation length. This entry retains
only its normalized topological infrared limit, not its massive particles.
It is also the trivial CFT: its only local operator is the identity, its
stress tensor vanishes, and local metric rescalings act trivially.

theories.name: 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ XYZ model
theories.summary: The infrared fixed point of three $\mathcal{N}=2$ chiral superfields with superpotential $W = XYZ$. By 3d mirror symmetry it is also the infrared fixed point of $\mathcal{N}=2$ SQED with one flavour.
theories.description:
Three chiral superfields $X, Y, Z$ with $W = h\,XYZ$. The superpotential is symmetric under
permutations of the fields, so at the fixed point $R_X = R_Y = R_Z = 2/3$ and the three
chiral primaries have $\Delta = 2/3$ exactly. The $F$-terms give the chiral-ring relations
$XY = YZ = ZX = 0$, and the moduli space is three one-dimensional cones meeting at the
origin.

Aharony, Hanany, Intriligator, Seiberg and Strassler [@xyz-model-3d/ahiss1997] proposed that $\mathcal{N}=2$ SQED with
one flavour (a $U(1)$ vector multiplet and chirals $Q$, $\tilde Q$ of charge $\pm1$) flows to
the same fixed point. The meson $M = \tilde QQ$ parametrizes the Higgs branch and the
monopole operators $V_\pm$ the two halves of the Coulomb branch; in the dual description
$W = -MV_+V_-$, so $(M, V_+, V_-)$ play the roles of $(X, Y, Z)$. The axial and topological
symmetries $U(1)_A\times U(1)_J$ of SQED become the $U(1)\times U(1)$ flavor symmetry, and
the permutation symmetry, which exchanges the three branches, is not visible in SQED.
Jafferis [@xyz-model-3d/jafferis2010] showed that extremizing $|Z_{S^3}|$ in SQED gives $R_Q = R_{\tilde Q} = 1/3$, hence
$\Delta_{\tilde QQ} = 2/3$, and that the SQED and XYZ $S^3$ partition functions agree as
functions of the trial R-charge.

The XYZ point lies on a one-complex-dimensional conformal manifold. The three marginal
chiral operators $X^3, Y^3, Z^3$, modulo the complexified $U(1)\times U(1)$, leave one
exactly marginal coupling: $W = h_1XYZ + \tfrac{h_2}{6}(X^3+Y^3+Z^3)$ flows to a family of
SCFTs labelled by $\tau = h_2/h_1$. The duality group is $S_4$ and the manifold is an
orbifold of $\mathbb{CP}^1$. Besides the XYZ model ($\tau=0$) it contains three decoupled
copies of the $\mathcal{N}=2$ super-Ising model ($\tau=\infty$). The localization results
for $F$ and $C_T$ hold at every point. The $4-\epsilon$ expansion and the bootstrap agree
closely for unprotected dimensions on the manifold, except near the XYZ point, where the
bootstrap bounds converge slowly; no unprotected XYZ dimension is quoted here.

The XYZ model has been proposed as the theory of the tricritical point between a Dirac
semimetal and a nematic pair-density-wave phase on the surface of a topological insulator
with three Dirac cones [@xyz-model-3d/jian2017].
