theories.name: SU(2) gauge theory with two adjoint Dirac fermions
theories.summary: $SU(2)$ Yang–Mills theory with two massless Dirac fermions in the adjoint representation. Lattice simulations indicate that it flows to an infrared CFT with a mass anomalous dimension of roughly 0.2–0.4, but the fixed point is strongly coupled and not established analytically.
theories.description:
The theory is $SU(2)$ gauge theory with $N_f = 2$ massless Dirac fermions in the adjoint
(equivalently, four Majorana fermions). For adjoint Dirac fermions asymptotic freedom requires
$N_f < 11/4$, and the two-loop beta function has an infrared zero for $N_f > 17/16$, so
$N_f = 2$ is the only integer value in that interval [@adjoint-qcd-su2-4d/ryttov2017]. That zero is at
strong coupling, and whether the theory is conformal in the infrared is decided by lattice
simulations. It was proposed for technicolor as "minimal walking technicolor".

Because the adjoint representation is real, the flavor symmetry acting on the four Majorana
fermions is $SU(4)$. If chiral symmetry were broken by a condensate, the pattern would be
$SU(4)\to SO(4)$ [@adjoint-qcd-su2-4d/bergner2017]; in the conformal phase it is unbroken.

### Status
There is no analytic control, and the infrared phase rests on lattice simulations. These are
consistent with an infrared fixed point (Ryttov and Shrock's summary of the lattice work [@adjoint-qcd-su2-4d/ryttov2017]). The
running coupling in the Schrödinger-functional scheme gives evidence of a fixed point at
$1/g_*^2 = 0.20(4)(3)$ [@adjoint-qcd-su2-4d/degrand2011] and is consistent with a fixed point in
$2.2 \lesssim g_*^2 \lesssim 3$ [@adjoint-qcd-su2-4d/rantaharju2016]. The mesonic spectrum favors infrared
conformality over chiral symmetry breaking [@adjoint-qcd-su2-4d/delDebbio2010], and a large-volume study
of finite-size effects supports conformal behavior [@adjoint-qcd-su2-4d/delDebbio2016]. The mass
anomalous dimension is small: published lattice values range from about 0.2 to 0.5, and the
more precise ones listed below lie between 0.2 and 0.38. Bergner et al. [@adjoint-qcd-su2-4d/bergner2017] find that $\gamma_*$ from the Dirac mode number depends on the lattice
coupling, $0.376(3)$ at $\beta = 1.5$ and $0.274(10)$ at $\beta = 1.7$, and conclude that
scaling corrections must be included before quoting the fixed-point value. The
scheme-independent expansion to fourth order gives a larger value, $0.556$.

theories.name: Argyres–Douglas theories
theories.summary: Isolated, non-Lagrangian $\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFTs at points of the Coulomb branch where mutually non-local BPS particles become massless. The rank-one members $H_0$, $H_1$, $H_2$ arise in $SU(2)$ with $N_f = 1, 2, 3$ flavors and have Coulomb-branch operators of dimension $6/5$, $4/3$, $3/2$.
theories.description:
Argyres and Douglas [@argyres-douglas-4d/argyres1995] showed that pure $\mathcal{N}=2$ $SU(N)$ gauge theory with $N > 2$ has
vacua in which mutually non-local dyons become massless, such as the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ point of
$SU(3)$, and proposed that the low-energy theory there is an interacting $\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFT.
Argyres, Plesser, Seiberg and Witten [@argyres-douglas-4d/argyres1995b] found fixed points of the same kind in $SU(2)$ with
$N_f = 1, 2, 3$ fundamental flavors, at points where a monopole and $N_f$ quarks become
massless together; the $N_f = 1$ point is the same SCFT as the $SU(3)$ one. These are the
rank-one theories $H_0$, $H_1$, $H_2$. The dimension $\Delta_u$ of the Coulomb-branch
operator $u$ follows from the scale-invariant form of the Seiberg–Witten curve, and the
relevant coupling paired with $u$ has dimension $2 - \Delta_u$. Because $\Delta_u$ is
fractional, the $U(1)_r$ symmetry of the fixed point is not a symmetry of the classical
Lagrangian.

Together with $D_4$ ($SU(2)$ with four flavors) and $E_6$, $E_7$, $E_8$ (the
Minahan–Nemeschansky theories), they are the theories on a single D3-brane probing an
F-theory singularity with constant dilaton. Their flavor symmetry is trivial, $SU(2)$ and
$SU(3)$, and the Higgs branches of $H_1$ and $H_2$ are the one-instanton moduli spaces of the
flavor group. Shapere and Tachikawa [@argyres-douglas-4d/shapere2008] computed $a$ and $c$ from the Seiberg–Witten geometry
through the topological twist, and Aharony and Tachikawa [@argyres-douglas-4d/aharony2007] obtained the same values, for any
rank, from holography. At rank one their formulas reduce to
$a = \tfrac34\Delta_u - \tfrac{13}{24}$, $c = \Delta_u - \tfrac56$ and $k = 2\Delta_u$.

The rank-one theories are the first members of larger families labelled by the BPS quiver
$(A_1, G)$: $H_0 = (A_1, A_2)$, $H_1 = (A_1, A_3) = (A_1, D_3)$, $H_2 = (A_1, D_4)$. The
$(A_1, A_{N-1})$ theory arises at the maximal Argyres–Douglas point of pure $SU(N)$, with
closed-form $a$ and $c$ [@argyres-douglas-4d/shapere2008], and $(A_1, D_N)$ at the maximal conformal point
of $SU(N-1)$ with two flavors. The flavor symmetry of $(A_1, D_N)$ is $SU(2)$ for odd $N$ and
$SU(2)\times U(1)$ for even $N$, enhanced to $SU(3)$ at $N = 4$ [@argyres-douglas-4d/maruyoshi2016].
From a conjectured relation between the Schur index and the BPS spectrum, Córdova and Shao [@argyres-douglas-4d/cordova2015]
found that the Schur index of $(A_1, A_{2n})$ is the vacuum character of the $(2, 2n+3)$
Virasoro minimal model, that of $(A_1, D_{2n+1})$ is the vacuum character of
$\widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)$ at level $-\tfrac{4n}{2n+1}$, and that of $(A_1, D_4)$ is the
vacuum character of $\widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(3)$ at level $-\tfrac32$.

Maruyoshi and Song [@argyres-douglas-4d/maruyoshi2016] found $\mathcal{N}=1$ gauge theories that flow to these SCFTs with
supersymmetry enhanced to $\mathcal{N}=2$. One couples an adjoint chiral multiplet $M$ of the
flavor symmetry of an $\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFT through $W = \mathrm{Tr}\,M\mu$ and gives $M$ a
principal nilpotent expectation value. $SU(2)$ with four flavors then flows to $H_0$, $SU(N)$
with $2N$ flavors to $(A_1, A_{2N-1})$, $Sp(N)$ with $2N+2$ flavors to $(A_1, A_{2N})$, and
the deformed $H_1$ and $H_2$ flow to $H_0$, in each case up to decoupled free chiral
multiplets. These Lagrangians give the full superconformal index.

The numerical bootstrap of the four-point function of $u$, with $\Delta_u$ and $c$ fixed to
the values below, gives narrow two-sided bounds on the OPE coefficient of $u^2$
[@argyres-douglas-4d/gimenezgrau2020].

theories.name: $\beta$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM
theories.summary: An exactly marginal deformation of $\mathcal{N}=4$ $SU(N)$ SYM that keeps $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetry and a $U(1)\times U(1)$ flavour symmetry, made by inserting phases $e^{\pm i\pi\beta}$ in the superpotential. For real $\beta$ its gravity dual is the Lunin–Maldacena background.
theories.description:
The field content of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM in $\mathcal{N}=1$ language (a vector multiplet and three
adjoint chiral multiplets $\Phi_{1,2,3}$) with superpotential
$$W = h\,\mathrm{Tr}\big(e^{i\pi\beta}\,\Phi_1\Phi_2\Phi_3 - e^{-i\pi\beta}\,\Phi_1\Phi_3\Phi_2\big).$$
At $\beta = 0$, with $|h|$ fixed in terms of $g$, this is $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM. Leigh and Strassler [@beta-deformed-n4-4d/ls1995]
showed that for $SU(N)$, $N > 2$, conformal invariance imposes a single condition on $g$, $h$, $\beta$
and the coefficient $h'$ of a further term $\mathrm{Tr}(\Phi_1^3+\Phi_2^3+\Phi_3^3)$, so the
$\mathcal{N}=4$ line sits inside a three-parameter family of $\mathcal{N}=1$ fixed points. Setting $h' = 0$ preserves
$U(1)\times U(1)$ (acting as $(\Phi_1,\Phi_2,\Phi_3) \to (\Phi_1, e^{i\varphi_1}\Phi_2, e^{-i\varphi_1}\Phi_3)$
and $(e^{-i\varphi_2}\Phi_1, e^{i\varphi_2}\Phi_2, \Phi_3)$) and leaves a two-parameter family
labelled by $\tau$ and $\beta$. The theory is invariant under cyclic permutations of the $\Phi_i$, and
$\beta$ is periodic, $\beta \sim \beta + 1 \sim \beta + \tau$, with $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ acting as
$\beta \to \beta/(c\tau+d)$.

**Conformality.** For $SU(N)$ the one-loop condition (a relation among $|h|$, $q = e^{i\pi\beta}$ and
$g$ with explicit $1/N^2$ terms) makes the theory conformal through two loops; higher loops can
modify it, but a fixed-point set of real codimension one in the couplings $(h, q, g)$ always exists
[@beta-deformed-n4-4d/fg2005]. For real $\beta$ in the planar limit, the one-loop condition is exact to all
orders [@beta-deformed-n4-4d/mpsz2005]. With gauge group $U(N)$ the traces
$\mathrm{Tr}\,\Phi_i$ couple to the $SU(N)$ fields through $W$ and the deformed $U(N)$ theory is not
conformal; these couplings flow to zero, leaving the $SU(N)$ theory in the infrared
[@beta-deformed-n4-4d/lm2005]. This supersymmetric deformation differs from the non-supersymmetric three-parameter
$\gamma_i$-deformation, which is not conformal even in the 't Hooft limit because a double-trace
coupling runs [@beta-deformed-n4-4d/fsw2014].

**Holography.** For real $\beta$ the deformation acts on component fields as a star product
$f * g = e^{i\pi\beta(Q^1_fQ^2_g - Q^2_fQ^1_g)}fg$ in the $U(1)\times U(1)$ charges, so planar diagrams
equal those of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM. The dual geometry follows from $AdS_5\times S^5$ by an
$SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ transformation $\rho \to \rho/(1+\beta\rho)$ of $\rho = B_{12} + i\sqrt{g}$, the
parameter of the two-torus on which $U(1)\times U(1)$ acts [@beta-deformed-n4-4d/lm2005]. Its holographic central charge is
independent of $\beta$ [@beta-deformed-n4-4d/fg2005].

**Chiral ring.** For generic $\beta$ the single-trace chiral primaries are $\mathrm{Tr}\,\Phi_i^J$ and
one operator with $U(1)^3$ charges $(J,J,J)$. The latter is not the ordered word
$\mathrm{Tr}\,\Phi_1^J\Phi_2^J\Phi_3^J$ but a coupling-dependent combination of its orderings
[@beta-deformed-n4-4d/fg2005], and the Coulomb branch consists of diagonal matrices with only
one $\Phi_i$ nonzero in each entry (for $SU(N)$ there is one further branch, from the traceless
projection of the F-terms). For rational real $\beta = m/n$ there are extra chiral primaries and extra
branches of vacua. The spin chain of the sector built from $\Phi_{1,2,3}$ is integrable for real
$\beta$ but not for complex $\beta$ (results quoted by Lunin and Maldacena [@beta-deformed-n4-4d/lm2005]).

parameters.description: Rank of the gauge group $SU(N)$. Leigh and Strassler [@beta-deformed-n4-4d/ls1995] take $N > 2$, where the symmetric invariant $d^{abc}$ is nonzero.
Deformation parameter, $q = e^{i\pi\beta}$.
Complexified gauge coupling; $h$ is fixed by the conformality condition.

theories.name: Fishnet CFT
theories.summary: A planar, non-unitary 4d CFT of two complex $N_c\times N_c$ matrix scalars with a single chiral quartic interaction, obtained as a double-scaling limit of $\gamma$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM. It is integrable, and it is conformal only at complex values of induced double-trace couplings.
theories.description:
The $\gamma$-deformation of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM twists the theory by three angles $\gamma_j$ and
breaks all supersymmetry; for $\gamma_1=\gamma_2=\gamma_3$ it reduces to the $\mathcal{N}=1$
$\beta$-deformation. Gürdoğan and Kazakov [@fishnet-4d/gurdogan2016] take $g_{\rm YM}\to 0$ together with a large imaginary
twist, keeping $\xi^2 = g_{\rm YM}^2N_c\,e^{-i\gamma_3}/(4\pi)^2$ fixed (normalization of
[@fishnet-4d/gromov2019]) and the other two effective couplings zero. The gauge fields and
fermions decouple, leaving two complex scalars $\phi_1, \phi_2$ in the adjoint of a global
$SU(N_c)$, with the Lagrangian below. The quartic term is complex (it has no
Hermitian-conjugate partner), so the theory is not unitary. With all three effective couplings
nonzero one gets a larger integrable theory with three scalars and Yukawa-coupled fermions.

In the planar limit each correlator receives contributions from very few graphs, whose bulk is
a regular square lattice (a "fishnet"). Zamolodchikov [@fishnet-4d/zamolodchikov1980] showed that such graphs define an
integrable lattice model, and the theory is described by a noncompact $SU(2,2)$ spin chain
and by a limit of the quantum spectral curve of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM [@fishnet-4d/gromov2018].

The single-trace Lagrangian is not complete: double-trace couplings are generated and run even
in the planar limit, so the original proposal is not conformal [@fishnet-4d/sieg2016]. The
completed theory has
$$\mathcal{L}_{\rm dt} = (4\pi)^2\alpha_1^2\,[\mathrm{tr}(\phi_1^2)\,\mathrm{tr}(\phi_1^{\dagger 2}) + \mathrm{tr}(\phi_2^2)\,\mathrm{tr}(\phi_2^{\dagger 2})] - (4\pi)^2\alpha_2^2\,[\mathrm{tr}(\phi_1\phi_2)\,\mathrm{tr}(\phi_1^\dagger\phi_2^\dagger) + \mathrm{tr}(\phi_1\phi_2^\dagger)\,\mathrm{tr}(\phi_1^\dagger\phi_2)].$$
The beta functions of $\alpha_1^2$ and $\alpha_2^2$ vanish only at $\alpha_2^2 = \xi^2$ and at
the two complex values $\alpha_{1,\pm}^2$ below ([@fishnet-4d/grabner2018], checked to seven loops). Each value of $\xi$ therefore gives two planar,
non-unitary CFTs, and the family consists of these two lines of fixed points. At them the
dimension of $\mathrm{tr}(\phi_1^2)$ is complex. All data are for $N_c\to\infty$; whether the
fixed points persist at finite $N_c$ is not established.

theories.name: Free Maxwell theory (4d)
theories.summary: Free $U(1)$ gauge theory in four dimensions: a conformal manifold labelled by the complexified coupling $\tau$, with $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ electric–magnetic duality.
theories.description:
The field strength $F_{\mu\nu}$ has $\Delta = 2$ and Lorentz representation
$(1,0)\oplus(0,1)$. This saturates the unitarity bound, so $F$ obeys the free
Maxwell equations $\partial^\mu F_{\mu\nu} = \partial^\mu \tilde F_{\mu\nu} = 0$.
The gauge-invariant local operators are built from $F$ and its derivatives, and
their correlators follow from Wick contractions.

The complexified coupling $\tau = \frac{\theta}{2\pi} + \frac{2\pi i}{e^2}$ is
exactly marginal. The theory is a conformal manifold: the upper half-plane
modulo $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ electric–magnetic duality. In flat space, $e$ only sets
the normalisation of $F$ and $\theta$ multiplies a total derivative, so
normalised correlators of local operators do not depend on $\tau$. The coupling
shows up in line operators (Wilson and 't Hooft lines) and in partition functions
on four-manifolds, which transform as modular forms rather than being invariant.

The global symmetries are electric and magnetic $U(1)$ one-form symmetries,
which act on Wilson and 't Hooft lines and have a mixed 't Hooft anomaly, and
charge conjugation $A \to -A$. At $\tau = i$ the $S$ transformation
$\tau \to -1/\tau$ is a symmetry. At $\tau = iN$, $S$ combined with gauging
$\mathbb{Z}_N \subset U(1)^{(1)}_e$ gives a non-invertible duality defect.

In $d \neq 4$ free Maxwell theory is scale invariant but not conformal: $F_{\mu\nu}$
is then neither a primary nor a descendant.

theories.name: Free massless scalar (4d)
theories.summary: A single free massless real scalar in four dimensions: the Gaussian fixed point, and the reference point for the 4d conformal anomalies $a$ and $c$.
theories.description:
The simplest CFT in $d=4$. All correlators follow from Wick
contractions of $\langle \phi(x)\phi(0)\rangle \propto |x|^{-2}$.

Unlike in $d=3$, the $\phi^4$ coupling is marginal at the free point, and it
is marginally irrelevant: it runs to zero in the IR, so there is no flow to an
interacting fixed point. The Wilson–Fisher fixed point merges with this one
as $d \to 4$.

theories.name: Free massless Weyl fermion (4d)
theories.summary: A single free massless Weyl fermion in four dimensions (equivalently, a Majorana fermion): the basic chiral matter field, whose $U(1)$ symmetry has 't Hooft anomalies.
theories.description:
A left-handed two-component spinor $\psi_\alpha$ with
$\langle \psi_\alpha(x)\bar\psi_{\dot\alpha}(0)\rangle \propto x_\mu\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\alpha}/|x|^4$.
All correlators follow from Wick contractions. In $d=4$ a Weyl fermion and a
Majorana fermion are the same theory. A Dirac fermion is two Weyl fermions, so
its $a$, $c$ and $C_T$ are twice the values below.

The phase rotation $\psi \to e^{i\alpha}\psi$ is a $U(1)$ symmetry with 't Hooft
anomalies: the $U(1)^3$ and mixed $U(1)$–gravitational triangle anomalies are
proportional to $\sum q^3 = 1$ and $\sum q = 1$. So this $U(1)$ cannot be gauged on
its own. The only Lorentz-invariant mass term is the Majorana mass
$m\,\psi\psi + \text{h.c.}$, which breaks $U(1)$ to fermion parity $(-1)^F$.
Every $U(1)$-invariant deformation is irrelevant: the lightest is the four-fermion
operator, with $\Delta = 6$.

symmetry.spacetime: 4d conformal group with parity combined with charge conjugation ($CP$; $P$ alone maps the left-handed fermion to a right-handed one)
symmetry.global: $U(1)$ ($\psi\to e^{i\alpha}\psi$), with $U(1)^3$ and $U(1)$–gravitational 't Hooft anomalies; it contains fermion parity $(-1)^F$

global_group.note: Parity ($CP$) maps charge $q$ to $-q$.

theories.name: Klebanov–Witten theory
aliases: $\mathcal{N}=1$ $SU(N)\times SU(N)$ theory of D3-branes at the conifold
theories.summary: The $\mathcal{N}=1$ SCFT on $N$ D3-branes at the conifold singularity: $SU(N)\times SU(N)$ gauge theory with bifundamentals $A_{1,2}$, $B_{1,2}$ and a quartic superpotential. It is dual to type IIB string theory on $AdS_5\times T^{1,1}$.
theories.description:
Gauge group $SU(N)\times SU(N)$ with chiral multiplets $A_1, A_2$ in the $(\mathbf{N}, \overline{\mathbf{N}})$
and $B_1, B_2$ in the $(\overline{\mathbf{N}}, \mathbf{N})$, and superpotential
$$W = \tfrac{\lambda}{2}\,\epsilon^{ij}\epsilon^{kl}\,\mathrm{Tr}\,A_iB_kA_jB_l .$$
On D3-branes the gauge group is $U(N)\times U(N)$, but the $U(1)$ factors are infrared free and
decouple. From the point of view of either $SU(N)$ factor the matter is $2N$ flavours, i.e.
$N_f = 2N_c$, far from both edges of the SQCD conformal window. The unique anomaly-free $R$-symmetry gives
$R_A = R_B = \tfrac12$, so $W$ has $R = 2$ and is marginal at the fixed point.

Conformal invariance imposes one condition on the gauge couplings $g_1, g_2$ and $\lambda$, so the
fixed points form a surface generated by two exactly marginal operators: $W$ and the difference of
the two gauge kinetic terms. Klebanov and Witten [@klebanov-witten-4d/kw1998] propose to identify these two complex moduli with the
type IIB coupling $\tau$ and with the periods of the NS-NS and R-R two-forms on the 2-cycle of
$T^{1,1} = (SU(2)\times SU(2))/U(1) \simeq S^2\times S^3$.

The chiral primaries $\mathrm{Tr}\,A_{k_1}B_{l_1}\cdots A_{k_n}B_{l_n}$ are symmetric in the $SU(2)$
indices (by the F-term equations) and have $R = n$, $\Delta = \tfrac{3n}{2}$; they match the scalar
harmonics on $T^{1,1}$, and $\mathrm{Tr}\,A_kB_l$ are the conifold coordinates $z_i$. The baryon-like
operators $\det A$ and $\det B$ have $\Delta = \tfrac{3N}{4}$, which supergravity reproduces from
D3-branes wrapped on 3-cycles of $T^{1,1}$ [@klebanov-witten-4d/gk1998].

**Flows.** The theory is the infrared limit of the $\mathcal{N}=2$ $\mathbb{Z}_2$ orbifold of
$\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM ($SU(N)\times SU(N)$ with bifundamental hypermultiplets) deformed by the mass
term $\tfrac{m}{2}(\mathrm{Tr}\,\Phi^2 - \mathrm{Tr}\,\tilde\Phi^2)$ for the two adjoint chiral
multiplets; integrating them out produces $W$. Geometrically this is the blow-up of $S^5/\mathbb{Z}_2$
to $T^{1,1}$. At large $N$ the central charges drop by the factor $27/32$ along this flow, which
Gubser [@klebanov-witten-4d/gubser1998] derived both from 't Hooft anomalies and from the ratio of volumes.

The ratio $27/32$ is to the orbifold, not to $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM.

relations.note: On the branch where all $A_k$, $B_l$ are proportional to the identity (the D3-branes at a smooth point of the conifold), $SU(N)\times SU(N)$ breaks to its diagonal $SU(N)$. Of the $4N^2$ chiral components, $N^2-1$ are eaten, leaving three adjoints and four gauge-singlet chiral multiplets: the low-energy theory is $\mathcal{N}=4$ $SU(N)$ SYM together with a decoupled free singlet sector.
Each $SU(N)$ node alone is SQCD with $N_f = 2N_c$, inside the conformal window.

theories.name: 4d Lee–Yang edge singularity CFT
theories.summary: The non-unitary CFT at the Lee–Yang edge singularity in four dimensions: the fixed point of one scalar with an imaginary cubic coupling, below its upper critical dimension 6. Its only relevant primary, $\phi$, lies below the unitarity bound.
theories.description:
Above the critical temperature the zeros of the Ising partition function in a complex
magnetic field end at the Lee–Yang edge, where their density vanishes with a universal
exponent $\sigma$. Fisher [@lee-yang-4d/fisher1978] described the edge by a scalar with an imaginary cubic
coupling, whose upper critical dimension is 6, so $d=4$ is $\epsilon = 2$ of the
$6-\epsilon$ expansion. The same exponents describe lattice animals (branched polymers)
in $d+2 = 6$ dimensions [@lee-yang-4d/parisi1981]. Unlike the 4d Ising critical point,
which is Gaussian, the 4d Lee–Yang fixed point is interacting.

The only relevant primary is $\phi$. At the fixed point $\phi^2$ is proportional to
$\partial^2\phi$ by the equation of motion, so it is a descendant [@lee-yang-4d/gliozzi2014],
and the next scalar primary, "$\phi^3$", is irrelevant. The exponents follow from
$\Delta_\phi$:
$$\sigma = \frac{\Delta_\phi}{4 - \Delta_\phi}, \qquad \eta = 2\Delta_\phi - 2 .$$
$\Delta_\phi \approx 0.83$ lies below the unitarity bound $\Delta \geq 1$ for a 4d
scalar ($\eta < 0$).

The estimates below come from methods whose error estimates are not directly
comparable: the $6-\epsilon$ expansion to five loops with resummation
[@lee-yang-4d/borinsky2021]; series expansions of the dimer density on the
hypersimple-cubic and hyper-body-centred-cubic lattices in $d=4$ [@lee-yang-4d/butera2012];
the functional renormalization group [@lee-yang-4d/an2016]; and a truncated,
non-rigorous bootstrap that keeps a few operators in the $\phi\times\phi$ OPE
[@lee-yang-4d/gliozzi2014], since the positivity-based numerical bootstrap does not apply to a
non-unitary theory. For $\sigma$ they agree to about $0.01$. For $\eta$ the functional
RG and the five-loop values do not overlap. Arguello Cruz, Klebanov, Tarnopolsky and
Xin [@lee-yang-4d/arguellocruz2025] also studied the quantum Ising model in an imaginary longitudinal field on the
24 vertices of the 24-cell, a regular polytope that approximates $S^3$. They find
$\Delta_\phi \approx 0.89$, within 8% of their two-sided Padé extrapolation of the
$6-\epsilon$ series, and describe these as first results, less precise than their
$d = 3$ ones.

theories.name: Asymptotically safe gauge–Yukawa theory
theories.summary: An interacting ultraviolet fixed point of $SU(N_c)$ gauge theory with $N_f$ Dirac fermions and an $N_f\times N_f$ complex scalar with a Yukawa coupling, in the Veneziano limit. It is perturbative for small $\epsilon = N_f/N_c - 11/2 > 0$, where asymptotic freedom is lost.
theories.description:
The fields are $SU(N_c)$ gauge fields, $N_f$ Dirac fermions $Q$ in the fundamental
representation, and an $N_f\times N_f$ complex scalar matrix $H$ that is neutral under the gauge
group and couples to the fermions through a Yukawa term. The four classically marginal couplings
are normalized for the Veneziano limit $N_c, N_f\to\infty$ at fixed $N_f/N_c$:
$\alpha_g = g^2N_c/(4\pi)^2$, $\alpha_y = y^2N_c/(4\pi)^2$, $\alpha_h = uN_f/(4\pi)^2$ and
$\alpha_v = vN_f^2/(4\pi)^2$. The control parameter is $\epsilon = N_f/N_c - 11/2$; for
$\epsilon > 0$ the one-loop gauge coefficient has the wrong sign for asymptotic freedom.

To the order needed for the leading fixed point (two loops in the gauge coupling, one in the
Yukawa coupling),
$\beta_g = \alpha_g^2\,[\tfrac43\epsilon + (25 + \tfrac{26}{3}\epsilon)\alpha_g - 2(\tfrac{11}{2}+\epsilon)^2\alpha_y]$
and $\beta_y = \alpha_y\,[(13+2\epsilon)\alpha_y - 6\alpha_g]$. Without the Yukawa coupling the
two-loop gauge term has the same sign as the one-loop term and no fixed point with $\alpha_g > 0$
exists. The Yukawa coupling enters $\beta_g$ with the opposite sign and produces a zero at
couplings of order $\epsilon$, so gauge fields, fermions and scalars are all required
[@litim-sannino-4d/litim2014]. Only one fixed-point value of the single-trace quartic admits a fixed point of
the double-trace quartic, which then has two; the values below are for the one where the
potential is bounded from below (FP$_1$).

With the scalar mass tuned to zero, the fixed point has a single relevant direction among the four
classically marginal couplings, with exponent of order $\epsilon^2$, so the critical surface of the
massless theory is one dimensional. The scalar mass term $\mathrm{Tr}\,H^\dagger H$ ($\Delta = 2 + O(\epsilon)$)
is a further relevant deformation. The two trajectories that leave it along that
direction run either to the free theory in the infrared or to strong coupling, where the theory
confines and breaks chiral symmetry or flows to an infrared CFT. The scaling exponents
$\vartheta$ are eigenvalues of $\partial\beta_i/\partial\alpha_j$ at the fixed point; the
corresponding scaling operators have $\Delta = 4 + \vartheta$. At this weakly coupled fixed
point scale invariance entails conformal invariance, and the unitarity bounds are satisfied in
perturbation theory [@litim-sannino-4d/litim2023].

The fixed point exists only for $0 < \epsilon < \epsilon_{\max}$. Three-loop analyses put
$\epsilon_{\max} \approx 0.09$–$0.13$, limited mainly by vacuum stability [@litim-sannino-4d/bond2018]. At four
loops, vacuum stability is lost for $\epsilon_{\max} \approx 0.087$–$0.146$ and the relevant
exponent indicates a fixed-point merger for $\epsilon_{\max} \approx 0.091$–$0.249$
[@litim-sannino-4d/litim2023]. Extrapolated to finite multiplicities, the smallest compatible $(N_c, N_f)$ moves from
$(3, 17)$ at the previous order to $(5, 28)$ at four loops. All statements here are for the Veneziano
limit.

The fermion mass operator $\bar Q Q$ mixes with other dimension-three operators, so the mass
anomalous dimension computed without this mixing is not a scaling dimension beyond leading order;
Bednyakov and Mukhaeva [@litim-sannino-4d/bednyakov2024] compute the eigenvalues of the mixing matrix at four loops. Its dimension is
therefore not listed here.

theories.name: Minahan–Nemeschansky theories
theories.summary: The isolated rank-one $\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFTs with $E_6$, $E_7$ and $E_8$ flavor symmetry, whose Coulomb-branch operators have dimension 3, 4 and 6. They have no Lagrangian, and the $E_6$ and $E_7$ theories appear at infinite coupling of conformal gauge theories.
theories.description:
Minahan and Nemeschansky [@minahan-nemeschansky-4d/minahan1996; @minahan-nemeschansky-4d/minahan1996b] constructed the Seiberg–Witten curves and differentials of
$\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFTs with a one-dimensional Coulomb branch and $E_6$, $E_7$ or $E_8$ global
symmetry. At the conformal point the curves are $y^2 = x^3 - \rho^4$, $y^2 = x^3 - 2\rho^3 x$
and $y^2 = x^3 - 2\rho^5$, the $E_n$ Kodaira singularities, and the Coulomb-branch operator
has dimension 3, 4 and 6. The curves follow from requiring that the residues of the
Seiberg–Witten differential be linear in the $E_n$ mass parameters, and mass deformations
flow from $E_8$ to $E_7$, $E_6$ and $D_4$ ($SU(2)$ with four flavors). The theories live on a single D3-brane probing an $E_n$
singularity of F-theory, in the same series as the Argyres–Douglas theories $H_0, H_1, H_2$.
The Higgs branch is the one-instanton moduli space of $E_n$, generated by the moment map
subject to the Joseph relations.

Argyres and Seiberg [@minahan-nemeschansky-4d/argyres2007] found the $E_6$ and $E_7$ theories inside Lagrangian theories at infinite
coupling. $SU(3)$ with six flavors is dual to an $SU(2)$ gauge theory with one fundamental
hypermultiplet, coupled to the $E_6$ theory by gauging the $SU(2)$ in
$SU(2)\times SU(6) \subset E_6$. $USp(4)$ with twelve fundamental half-hypermultiplets is dual
to $SU(2)$ coupled to the $E_7$ theory, gauging the $SU(2)$ in $SU(2)\times SO(12) \subset E_7$.
Conformality of the dual $SU(2)$ fixes $k_{E_6} = 6$ and $k_{E_7} = 8$. Aharony and Tachikawa [@minahan-nemeschansky-4d/aharony2007]
computed $a$, $c$ and $k$ of all these theories, and of their higher-rank versions, from
holography, and checked them against these dualities: subtracting the dual $SU(2)$ sector
from $SU(3)$ with six flavors gives $a$ and $c$ of the $E_6$ theory. The $E_6$
theory is also Gaiotto's $T_3$, the theory of three M5-branes on a sphere with three full
punctures.

The central charges saturate the unitarity bounds that follow from the chiral algebra, and
the chiral algebra is conjectured to be the $E_n$ affine algebra at level $k_{2d} = -k/2$,
that is $-3$, $-4$ and $-6$ [@minahan-nemeschansky-4d/beem2013, Sec. 4.3; @minahan-nemeschansky-4d/beem2014, Sec. 2.4]. In the numerical bootstrap of the moment-map
four-point function, every $\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFT with at least $E_6$ flavor symmetry has
$c \geq 0.83$. The $E_6$ theory lies where two analytic chiral-algebra bounds meet, but at
$k = 6$ the numerical lower bound on $c$ appears to converge to between 1.1 and 1.2, below its
value $13/6$. At the $E_6$ values of $c$ and $k$ the upper bound on the first unprotected
singlet scalar extrapolates to about 4.4 [@minahan-nemeschansky-4d/beem2014].

theories.name: Minimal Argyres–Douglas theory
theories.summary: The rank-one Argyres–Douglas SCFT with no flavor symmetry and a Coulomb-branch operator of dimension $6/5$. Its $c = 11/30$ is the smallest allowed for an interacting $\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFT, and its chiral algebra is conjectured to be the Lee–Yang minimal model.
theories.description:
The infrared SCFT at the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ point of pure $\mathcal{N}=2$ $SU(3)$ gauge theory,
where mutually non-local dyons become massless [@minimal-ad-4d/argyres1995]. Argyres, Plesser,
Seiberg and Witten [@minimal-ad-4d/argyres1995b] found the same SCFT in $SU(2)$ with one flavor, at the point where a
monopole and a quark become massless together. It is isolated (no exactly marginal
deformations), has rank one and a trivial Higgs branch, and no flavor symmetry. Its
Coulomb-branch chiral ring is generated by $u$ with $\Delta_u = 6/5$, and the coupling of the
relevant deformation paired with $u$ has dimension $2 - \Delta_u = 4/5$.

Liendo, Ramírez and Seo [@minimal-ad-4d/liendo2015] showed from the stress-tensor OPE and the chiral algebra that any
interacting $\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFT without higher-spin currents has $c \geq 11/30$; this theory
saturates the bound. It also has the smallest $a$ among the rank-one SCFTs of the
Seiberg–Witten-geometry classification, assuming the Coulomb-branch chiral ring is freely
generated [@minimal-ad-4d/cornagliotto2017]. Its chiral algebra has $c_{2d} = -12c = -22/5$ and
is conjectured to be the Virasoro vertex algebra of the Lee–Yang minimal model
$\mathcal{M}(2,5)$. Beem and Rastelli [@minimal-ad-4d/beem2017] place it as the $\mathfrak{a}_0$ (trivial Lie algebra)
entry of the Deligne–Cvitanović series of vertex algebras, whose
$\mathfrak{a}_1, \mathfrak{a}_2, \mathfrak{d}_4, \mathfrak{e}_6, \mathfrak{e}_7, \mathfrak{e}_8$
entries are the other rank-one theories on a D3-brane at an F-theory singularity. Córdova and
Shao [@minimal-ad-4d/cordova2015] found that the Schur index equals the vacuum character of
$\mathcal{M}(2,5)$, using their conjectured relation between the Schur index and the BPS
spectrum, and the saturation of the $c$ bound matches the level-four null state of the
Lee–Yang vacuum module.

Maruyoshi and Song [@minimal-ad-4d/maruyoshi2016a] gave an $\mathcal{N}=1$ gauge theory that flows to this SCFT, with
supersymmetry enhanced to $\mathcal{N}=2$. Starting from $SU(2)$ with four flavors, they
couple an adjoint chiral multiplet $M$ of $SO(8)$ through $W = \mathrm{Tr}\,M\mu$ and give $M$
a principal nilpotent expectation value. What remains is an $SU(2)$ gauge theory with an
adjoint chiral, two fundamental chirals and gauge-singlet chirals. a-maximization, after
removing the operators that violate the unitarity bound and decouple as free fields, gives
$a = 43/120$, $c = 11/30$ and a singlet of dimension $6/5$. The infrared theory is this SCFT
plus free chiral multiplets, and the description gives the full superconformal index.

The numerical bootstrap of $\langle u\,\bar u\,u\,\bar u\rangle$ with $\Delta_u$ and $c$ as
input [@minimal-ad-4d/cornagliotto2017; @minimal-ad-4d/gimenezgrau2020] gives narrow two-sided bounds
on the OPE coefficient of $u^2$ and estimates of unprotected dimensions. The lower bound on
$c$ at $\Delta_u = 6/5$ is consistent with converging to $11/30$, but this is not conclusive.

three_point_structures.name: chiral, unit-normalized
three_point_structures.description: The three-scalar structure of the chiral OPE $u\times u \ni u^2$, with unit-normalized two-point functions $\langle u(x)\bar u(0)\rangle = |x|^{-2\Delta_u}$ and $\langle u^2(x)\,\overline{u^2}(0)\rangle = |x|^{-2\Delta_{u^2}}$. The sources write $u$ as the chiral primary $\phi_r$ and define the coefficient by the chiral-channel expansion $\langle\phi_r\phi_r\bar\phi_{-r}\bar\phi_{-r}\rangle = x_{12}^{-2\Delta_\phi}x_{34}^{-2\Delta_\phi}\sum_O|\lambda_{\phi\phi\bar O}|^2g_{\Delta,\ell}(z,\bar z)$ [@minimal-ad-4d/gimenezgrau2020, Eq. (2.13), Table 2; @minimal-ad-4d/cornagliotto2017, Eq. (2.8)], with blocks $g_{\Delta,\ell} = \frac{z\bar z}{z-\bar z}\big(k_{\Delta+\ell}(z)k_{\Delta-\ell-2}(\bar z) - (z\leftrightarrow\bar z)\big)$ [@minimal-ad-4d/gimenezgrau2020, Eqs. (2.10)–(2.11); @minimal-ad-4d/cornagliotto2017, Eq. (A.1)], so that $g_{\Delta,0} = (z\bar z)^{\Delta/2}+\dots$: the quoted $\lambda^2$ is the square of the coefficient of this unit-normalized structure (generalized free field: 2).

values.note: Bounds at derivative order $\Lambda = 50$ [@minimal-ad-4d/gimenezgrau2020, Table 7].
Bounds at $\Lambda = 40$ (earlier study). Conservative extrapolation: $2.146 \lesssim \lambda^2 \lesssim 2.159$ [@minimal-ad-4d/cornagliotto2017, Eq. (3.2)].

theories.name: $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal QCD
theories.summary: The $\mathcal{N}=2$ $SU(N)$ gauge theory with $N_f = 2N$ fundamental hypermultiplets, whose gauge coupling is exactly marginal. For $SU(2)$ the flavor symmetry is $SO(8)$, and the $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ duality group acts on it by triality.
theories.description:
An $\mathcal{N}=2$ $SU(N)$ vector multiplet (gauge field, two Weyl gauginos and a complex
adjoint scalar $\phi$) coupled to $N_f = 2N$ hypermultiplets in the fundamental
representation. With $N_f = 2N$ the one-loop beta function vanishes, and with $\mathcal{N}=2$
supersymmetry this suffices for conformal invariance of the quantum theory. The complexified
coupling $\tau$ is exactly marginal: the dimension-four operator it multiplies is the top
component of the multiplet whose primary is $\mathrm{Tr}\,\phi^2$. The anomalies $a$ and $c$
do not depend on $\tau$ and follow from counting free fields, $n_v = N^2-1$ vector multiplets
and $n_h = 2N^2$ hypermultiplets. The Coulomb branch is parametrized by
$u_k = \langle\mathrm{Tr}\,\phi^k\rangle$, $k = 2,\dots,N$.

For $N = 2$ the fundamental representation is pseudoreal, so the flavor symmetry is $SO(8)$
and the four hypermultiplets form its vector $\mathbf{8}_v$. Seiberg and Witten [@n2-sqcd-4d/seiberg1994] solved the
theory and found that its $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ duality is combined with $SO(8)$ triality. The
elementary quarks, with magnetic and electric charges $(n_m, n_e) = (0,1)$, form the
$\mathbf{8}_v$, while the states with $(1,0)$ and $(1,1)$ form the $\mathbf{8}_s$ and the
$\mathbf{8}_c$, and duality permutes these three representations. The Higgs branch is the
one-instanton moduli space of $SO(8)$, and
$c$ and $k_{SO(8)}$ saturate the unitarity bounds that follow from the associated chiral
algebra, which Beem et al. [@n2-sqcd-4d/beem2013] conjecture to be the $\mathfrak{so}(8)$ affine algebra at level
$-2$. This theory is the $D_4$ member of the rank-one series that also contains the
Argyres–Douglas theories $H_0, H_1, H_2$ and the Minahan–Nemeschansky theories.

For $N \geq 3$ the flavor symmetry is $U(2N) = SU(2N)\times U(1)$ and the S-duality group is
only the subgroup $\Gamma_0(2)$ of $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$, so the space of couplings has a second,
"very strongly coupled" cusp [@n2-sqcd-4d/gaiotto2009]. For $N = 3$ Argyres and Seiberg [@n2-sqcd-4d/argyres2007] identified the theory
at this cusp: an $SU(2)$ gauge theory with one fundamental hypermultiplet, coupled to the
rank-one $E_6$ Minahan–Nemeschansky theory by gauging the $SU(2)$ in
$SU(2)\times SU(6) \subset E_6$.

Coupling an adjoint chiral multiplet $M$ of the flavor symmetry through
$W = \mathrm{Tr}\,M\mu$ and giving $M$ a principal nilpotent expectation value breaks
$\mathcal{N}=2$ to $\mathcal{N}=1$. Maruyoshi and Song [@n2-sqcd-4d/maruyoshi2016] found that these deformations flow to
Argyres–Douglas theories with enhanced $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetry: $SU(N)$ with $2N$
flavors flows to the $(A_1, A_{2N-1})$ theory, and $SU(2)$ with the whole $SO(8)$ broken flows
to the minimal Argyres–Douglas theory $H_0$ (plus free chiral multiplets).

theories.name: $\mathcal{N}=3$ S-fold theories
theories.summary: Four-dimensional SCFTs with $\mathcal{N}=3$ but not $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetry, living on $N$ D3-branes at $\mathbb{Z}_k$ S-folds ($k = 3, 4, 6$) of F-theory. They are strongly coupled and non-Lagrangian, with $a = c$.
theories.description:
An S-fold generalizes the O3-plane: the identification of type IIB string theory by a
$2\pi/k$ rotation of the transverse $\mathbb{C}^3$ is combined with an $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ duality
transformation of order $k$. This requires $k = 2, 3, 4, 6$ and, for $k > 2$, the coupling
$\tau = e^{2\pi i/k}$; equivalently it is F-theory on $(\mathbb{C}^3\times T^2)/\mathbb{Z}_k$. For
$k = 3, 4, 6$ it preserves 12 supercharges, and $N$ D3-branes probing it give a 4d $\mathcal{N}=3$
SCFT [@n3-sfold-4d/ger2016]. The quotient acts on the string background, not on the
worldvolume field theory: these theories are not discrete gaugings of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM. Discrete
gauging leaves $a$ and $c$ unchanged, whereas the S-fold theories have different central charges
(for example $a = c = 5/4$ for $N = 1$, $k = \ell = 3$, against $1/4$ for $U(1)$ $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM).

General results for $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs that are not $\mathcal{N}=4$ [@n3-sfold-4d/ae2016]:
$a = c$; there are no exactly marginal deformations preserving $\mathcal{N}=3$ and no global
symmetries beyond the $SU(3)_R\times U(1)_R$ $R$-symmetry; and there are no free or weakly coupled
examples (the only free $\mathcal{N}=3$ multiplet is the $\mathcal{N}=4$ vector multiplet), so all such
theories are strongly coupled.

**Variants.** S-folds carry a discrete torsion, labelled by a divisor $\ell$ of $k$. Aharony and
Tachikawa [@n3-sfold-4d/at2016] find that the variants that exist are $(k,\ell) = (3,1), (3,3), (4,1), (4,4), (6,1)$. The
Coulomb-branch chiral ring is freely generated, with dimensions $k, 2k, \dots, (N-1)k$ and $N\ell$.
For $\ell < k$ these are the dimensions of a parent theory with a $\mathbb{Z}_{k/\ell}$ global symmetry;
gauging it gives a theory with generators $k, 2k, \dots, Nk$ and the same central charges, and which
of the two lives on the D3-branes depends on boundary conditions. Combining $a = c$ with the
relation $2a - c = \sum_i(2\Delta_i-1)/4$ over the Coulomb-branch generators (assumed to hold for
these theories) gives the central charges below.

**Special cases.** Supersymmetry is enhanced to $\mathcal{N}=4$ exactly when a Coulomb-branch operator
has dimension 1 or 2, which happens for $\ell = 1$ and $N = 1, 2$. At $N = 1$ this is $U(1)$
$\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM; at $N = 2$ the parent theories have the spectra of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM with gauge
group $SU(3)$, $SO(5)$ and $G_2$ for $k = 3, 4, 6$, and Aharony and Tachikawa [@n3-sfold-4d/at2016] give evidence that they
are these theories. The lowest $a$ without enhancement is at $N = 1$, $k = \ell = 3$: one Coulomb-branch
operator of dimension 3 and $a = c = \tfrac54$, the value of five free $\mathcal{N}=4$ vector
multiplets. Assuming the relation above, it is the minimal $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFT.

At large $N$ the dual is F-theory on $AdS_5\times(S^5\times T^2)/\mathbb{Z}_k$. Compactified on a
circle, the theories flow at certain loci of their moduli space to 3d $\mathcal{N}=6$ ABJM theories.

theories.name: $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang–Mills
theories.summary: The maximally supersymmetric gauge theory in four dimensions: an exactly marginal family of superconformal theories, dual to type IIB string theory on $AdS_5\times S^5$.
theories.description:
A conformal manifold of SCFTs labelled by the gauge group (here $SU(N)$) and
the complexified coupling $\tau = \frac{\theta}{2\pi} + \frac{4\pi i}{g^2_{\rm YM}}$.
The field content is a single $\mathcal{N}=4$ vector multiplet: a gauge field,
four Weyl fermions and six real scalars, all in the adjoint.

Key features:
- $\beta(g_{\rm YM}) = 0$ to all orders; $\tau$ is exactly marginal.
- S-duality: $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ acting on $\tau$, exchanging $G$ with its Langlands dual.
- The planar spectrum is computable at any 't Hooft coupling $\lambda = g^2_{\rm YM}N$ via integrability.
- At large $N$ and strong coupling it is described by type IIB supergravity on $AdS_5\times S^5$.

The label of Cordova, Dumitrescu and Intriligator [@n4-sym/cdi2016] is shown on hover.

backlinks.note: The $\beta = 0$ member. $\beta$ is an exactly marginal, $\mathcal{N}=1$-preserving deformation of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, and the Lunin–Maldacena dual is an $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ transform of $AdS_5\times S^5$.
Double-scaling limit of the $\gamma$-deformation of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM: $g_{\rm YM}\to0$ with a large imaginary twist $\gamma_3$, keeping $\xi^2 = g_{\rm YM}^2N_c\,e^{-i\gamma_3}/(4\pi)^2$ fixed.
At $g_{\rm YM} \to 0$, $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM becomes free fields (keeping only gauge-invariant operators), including $\dim G$ gauge fields.
At $g_{\rm YM} \to 0$, $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM becomes free fields (keeping only gauge-invariant operators), including $6\dim G$ real scalars.
At $g_{\rm YM} \to 0$, $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM becomes free fields (keeping only gauge-invariant operators), including $4\dim G$ Weyl fermions.

On the branch where all $A_k$, $B_l$ are proportional to the identity (the D3-branes at a smooth point of the conifold), $SU(N)\times SU(N)$ breaks to its diagonal $SU(N)$. Of the $4N^2$ chiral components, $N^2-1$ are eaten, leaving three adjoints and four gauge-singlet chiral multiplets: the low-energy theory is $\mathcal{N}=4$ $SU(N)$ SYM together with a decoupled free singlet sector.

Both are $\mathcal{N}=2$ conformal gauge theories with an exactly marginal coupling ($\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM is $SU(N)$ with one adjoint hypermultiplet). For gauge group $SU(2)$ they share the $D_4$ scale-invariant Seiberg–Witten curve: $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM is the submaximal mass deformation with $\mathfrak{su}(2) \subset \mathfrak{so}(8)$ flavor symmetry [@n2-sqcd-4d/beem2014].

Both arise on $N$ D3-branes: $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM in flat space, the S-fold theories at an S-fold, a quotient of the type IIB background (not a discrete gauging of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM); for $\ell = 1$ and $N = 1, 2$ supersymmetry is enhanced to $\mathcal{N}=4$.
$T[SU(N)]$ lives on the S-duality wall of 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang–Mills [@t-sun-3d/gaiotto2008].

theories.name: 4d percolation CFT
aliases: Bond and site percolation universality class (4d)
theories.summary: The critical point of bond and site percolation in four dimensions, the $q \to 1$ limit of the $q$-state Potts model. A non-unitary CFT, expected to be logarithmic, with exponents known from Monte Carlo simulations and the $6-\epsilon$ expansion.
theories.description:
In bond (site) percolation each bond (site) of a lattice is occupied independently with
probability $p$, and at $p = p_c$ an infinite cluster first appears. Bond percolation is
the $q \to 1$ limit of the Fortuin–Kasteleyn cluster representation of the $q$-state
Potts model. The field theory is a cubic theory of $N = q - 1$ scalars with the
$S_q$-invariant tensor coupling $d_{ijk}$, continued to $N \to 0$, with upper critical
dimension 6, so $d = 4$ is $\epsilon = 2$ of the $6-\epsilon$ expansion.

The thermal operator $\epsilon$, an $S_q$ singlet coupled to $p - p_c$, has
$\Delta_\epsilon = 4 - 1/\nu$. The order-parameter (spin) operator $\sigma$, in the
$(q-1)$-dimensional representation of $S_q$, has $\Delta_\sigma = 4 - d_f$, where $d_f$
is the fractal dimension of critical clusters, and $\eta = 2\Delta_\sigma - 2$.
$\Delta_\sigma \approx 0.955$ lies below the unitarity bound $\Delta \geq 1$ for a 4d
scalar ($\eta < 0$).

The most precise values come from Monte Carlo simulations of bond percolation on
hypercubic lattices: Tan, Deng and Jacobsen [@percolation-4d/tan2020] measured the two-cluster ("two-arm")
exponent, which equals $\Delta_\epsilon$, by a transfer Monte Carlo method on cylinders,
and Zhang, Hou, Fang, Hu and Deng [@percolation-4d/zhang2021] measured $d_f$ on periodic hypercubes. Site
percolation gives consistent values of $\nu$ [@percolation-4d/ballesteros1997; @percolation-4d/koza2016] and a
slightly more negative $\eta$ [@percolation-4d/ballesteros1997]. The five-loop $6-\epsilon$
expansion [@percolation-4d/borinsky2021] is consistent with the Monte Carlo
values for $\nu$ and $\eta$, with larger errors.

### Logarithmic CFT
As in two and three dimensions, the CFT is expected to be logarithmic: at $q = 1$ the
thermal operator mixes with a partner that creates two propagating clusters (Vasseur,
Jacobsen and Saleur [@percolation-4d/vasseur2012], whose derivation rests on the $S_q$ representation theory and who
expect it to hold also for $d > 2$). Tan, Deng and Jacobsen [@percolation-4d/tan2020] measured the $N$-cluster
correlation functions ($N = 2, 3$) of this framework in $d = 4$ and $5$, including a
combination that depends logarithmically on distance with a universal amplitude, and
conclude that their results confirm the logarithmic CFT description.
theories.lagrangian: \mathcal{L} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial\phi_i)^2 + \tfrac{1}{2} m^2 \phi_i\phi_i + \tfrac{g}{3!}\, d_{ijk}\,\phi_i\phi_j\phi_k, \quad d_{ijk} = \sum_{\alpha=1}^{N+1} e^i_\alpha e^j_\alpha e^k_\alpha, \quad i = 1,\dots,N = q - 1 \to 0 \quad (m^2 \text{ tuned})

theories.name: QCD in the conformal window
theories.summary: The infrared fixed points of $SU(3)$ gauge theory with $N_f$ massless Dirac quarks in the fundamental representation. They are weakly coupled (Banks–Zaks) just below $N_f = 33/2$, where asymptotic freedom is lost; where the window ends at smaller $N_f$ is not settled.
theories.description:
$SU(N_c)$ Yang–Mills theory coupled to $N_f$ massless Dirac fermions in the fundamental
representation. With $\alpha = g^2/4\pi$ the beta function is
$\beta(\alpha) = -2\alpha\,[\,b_1\,\alpha/4\pi + b_2\,(\alpha/4\pi)^2 + \dots]$, with the
scheme-independent coefficients $b_1$ and $b_2$ below. Asymptotic freedom requires
$N_f < 11N_c/2$, and $b_2 < 0$ for $N_f > 34N_c^3/(13N_c^2-3)$. In between, the two-loop beta
function has an infrared zero $\alpha_* = -4\pi b_1/b_2$ [@qcd-conformal-window-4d/caswell1974; @qcd-conformal-window-4d/banks1982], and the
massless theory flows from the free UV fixed point to an interacting CFT. Near the upper edge
$\alpha_*$ is proportional to $\Delta_f = 11N_c/2 - N_f$, so the fixed point is perturbative,
and its data can be expanded in powers of $\Delta_f$ with scheme-independent coefficients
[@qcd-conformal-window-4d/ryttov2017]. For $SU(3)$ the two-loop zero exists for $9 \le N_f \le 16$, with
$\alpha_* = 2\pi/151 \approx 0.042$ at $N_f = 16$.

In the conformal phase the flavor symmetry $SU(N_f)_L\times SU(N_f)_R\times U(1)_V$ is
unbroken and there is no confinement. The members below are the integer $N_f$ at which the
two-loop zero exists for $SU(3)$; conformality is controlled near $N_f = 16$ and is
increasingly uncertain toward $N_f = 9$. The order-$\Delta_f^4$ values of $\gamma_{\bar\psi\psi}$
quoted for the members are truncations of the $\Delta_f$ series and carry no error
estimate. Below the lower edge $N_f^*$ the theory confines and breaks chiral symmetry to
$SU(N_f)_V\times U(1)_V$.

### Status of the lower edge
The conformal window is $N_f^* < N_f < 11N_c/2$, and the value of $N_f^*$ is not known. The
estimates for $SU(3)$ disagree. The ladder Schwinger–Dyson criterion applied to the two-loop
fixed point gives $N_f^* = N_c(100N_c^2-66)/(25N_c^2-15)$, just below 12 for $N_c = 3$
[@qcd-conformal-window-4d/appelquist1996], but this approximation is uncontrolled. The
order-$\Delta_f^4$ values of $\gamma_{\bar\psi\psi}$ stay below the conformal bound
$\gamma \le 2$ down to $N_f = 9$; assuming the bound is saturated at the lower edge,
Ryttov and Shrock [@qcd-conformal-window-4d/ryttov2016gamma] estimate $8 \lesssim N_f^* \lesssim 9$, while Lee [@qcd-conformal-window-4d/lee2021], using the criterion
$\gamma = 1$, finds $N_f = 10$ likely to lie on the lower edge. Borel resummation of the
five-loop beta function and of the $\Delta_f$ expansion [@qcd-conformal-window-4d/dipietro2020] gives
substantial evidence that $N_f = 12$ is conformal and weaker indications for $N_f = 11$;
the method fails below 11.

On the lattice, $N_f = 12$ has been debated for years. Finite-size scaling analyses find
conformal behavior with $\gamma_m = 0.235(15)$ [@qcd-conformal-window-4d/cheng2014] and $0.235(46)$ [@qcd-conformal-window-4d/lombardo2014],
and LatKMI [@qcd-conformal-window-4d/aoki2012] find their data consistent with conformality for $\gamma_m \sim 0.4$–$0.5$.
Gradient-flow step-scaling studies find an infrared fixed point, at
$g_\star^2 = 7.3\,({}^{+8}_{-2})$ in the $c = 0.25$ scheme [@qcd-conformal-window-4d/hasenfratz2018] and in the
range $5.2 \le g_c^2 \le 6.4$ [@qcd-conformal-window-4d/hasenfratz2019], whereas Fodor et al. [@qcd-conformal-window-4d/fodor2016], in the same
scheme as an earlier study, find no zero of the beta function in the interval
$6.0 < g^2 < 6.4$ where that study had placed it. For $N_f = 10$, which is "the subject of
continuing debate", a recent gradient-flow study finds a fixed point at $g^2 = 15.0(5)$ with
$\gamma_m \simeq 0.6$ [@qcd-conformal-window-4d/hasenfratz2023]. For $N_f = 8$ the spectrum indirectly
indicates chiral symmetry breaking, with a flavor-singlet scalar degenerate with the
pseudo-Goldstone states at the lightest masses simulated [@qcd-conformal-window-4d/lsd2019].

theories.name: $\mathcal{N}=1$ SQCD in the conformal window
aliases: Supersymmetric QCD in the conformal window
theories.summary: The infrared fixed points of $\mathcal{N}=1$ $SU(N_c)$ gauge theory with $N_f$ flavours of quarks, interacting for $\tfrac32 N_c < N_f < 3N_c$. By Seiberg duality the same fixed point is reached from $SU(N_f-N_c)$ with $N_f$ flavours and a gauge-singlet meson.
theories.description:
An $\mathcal{N}=1$ $SU(N_c)$ vector multiplet coupled to $N_f$ chiral multiplets $Q^i$ in the
fundamental and $N_f$ chiral multiplets $\tilde Q_{\tilde\imath}$ in the antifundamental, with no
superpotential. The theory is asymptotically free for $N_f < 3N_c$. Seiberg [@sqcd-conformal-window-4d/seiberg1995] argued that for
$\tfrac32 N_c < N_f < 3N_c$ the theory at the origin of the moduli space flows to an interacting
SCFT. Near the upper edge the fixed point is weakly coupled (a Banks–Zaks fixed point): at large
$N_c$ with $N_f/N_c = 3-\epsilon$ fixed, $N_c g_*^2 = \tfrac{8\pi^2}{3}\epsilon + O(\epsilon^2)$.

The anomaly-free global symmetry is $SU(N_f)\times SU(N_f)\times U(1)_B\times U(1)_R$. The
superconformal $R$-symmetry is anomaly-free and commutes with $SU(N_f)\times SU(N_f)$, so it is this
$U(1)_R$. Its charges give the exact dimensions $\Delta = \tfrac32 R$ of the chiral mesons and
baryons, and 't Hooft anomaly matching gives the exact central charges. The meson dimension reaches
the unitarity bound $\Delta = 1$ at $N_f = \tfrac32 N_c$, where $M$ becomes free; this is the lower edge.

**Seiberg duality.** The same fixed point is the infrared limit of a magnetic $SU(N_f-N_c)$ theory
with $N_f$ flavours $q$, $\tilde q$ of $R$-charge $N_c/N_f$, and $N_f^2$ gauge-singlet chiral fields
$M$ coupled through $W = M^i_{\ \tilde\jmath}\, q_i \tilde q^{\tilde\jmath}$. The 't Hooft anomalies of
the two descriptions match. The electric description is more weakly coupled for
$2N_c \le N_f < 3N_c$, and the magnetic one for $\tfrac32 N_c < N_f \le 2N_c$. Just outside the
window the infrared theory is free: for $N_f \ge 3N_c$ the electric theory is not asymptotically free
(free electric phase), and for $N_c+2 \le N_f \le \tfrac32 N_c$ the magnetic theory is not (free
magnetic phase). At smaller $N_f$ there is no interacting SCFT: $N_f = N_c, N_c+1$ confine, and for
$N_f < N_c$ there is no ground state [@sqcd-conformal-window-4d/seiberg1995].

At $N_f = 2N_c$ both gauge groups are $SU(N_c)$. Adding an adjoint chiral multiplet with a Yukawa
coupling turns this theory into $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal $SU(N_c)$ QCD with $2N_c$ flavours
[@sqcd-conformal-window-4d/seiberg1995]. Conversely, a mass for the adjoint of that $\mathcal{N}=2$ theory leads to $N_f = 2N_c$
SQCD with a quartic superpotential in the mesons that is exactly marginal, so this member lies on a
curve of fixed points [@sqcd-conformal-window-4d/ls1995].

**Conformal bootstrap.** Crossing symmetry of $\langle \Phi\Phi^\dagger\Phi\Phi^\dagger\rangle$ for a
chiral primary $\Phi$ bounds the central charge, flavour-current coefficients and the dimension of
$\Phi^\dagger\Phi$ in terms of $\Delta_\Phi$; near $\Delta_\Phi \simeq 1$ the last bound approaches
$\Delta_{\Phi^\dagger\Phi} \le 2\Delta_\Phi$. Applied to one meson component, the flavour-current and
central-charge bounds are satisfied throughout the window and are most constraining at small $N_c$.
For $N_c = 3$, $N_f = 5$ ($\Delta_M = 1.2$) the flavour-current contribution is about $0.3$, against
a bound of about $2$ [@sqcd-conformal-window-4d/psd2010]. For many values of $N_c$ and $N_f$, later bounds on the $SU(N_f)$ current
two-point function come within an $O(1)$ factor of the SQCD value, closest near $\Delta_M \sim 1$
[@sqcd-conformal-window-4d/psdv2011].

theories.name: $T_N$ theories
aliases: Class $\mathcal{S}$ theory of the sphere with three full punctures
theories.summary: The $\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFTs of $N$ M5-branes on a sphere with three full punctures, with $SU(N)^3$ flavor symmetry and no marginal coupling. They are the building blocks of class $\mathcal{S}$ theories; $T_2$ is free and $T_3$ is the $E_6$ Minahan–Nemeschansky theory.
theories.description:
Gaiotto [@tn-4d/gaiotto2009] obtained $T_N$ from the very strongly coupled limits of a conformal linear quiver of
$SU(k)$ gauge groups, in which groups of $N-1$ basic punctures of the Seiberg–Witten curve
collide. It is the $A_{N-1}$ $(2,0)$ theory, i.e. $N$ M5-branes, on a sphere with three full
punctures, and it has no coupling constant. Each of its three $SU(N)$ flavor symmetries, when
gauged, supplies half of the matter needed for a conformal $SU(N)$ gauge theory, since
$k_{SU(N)} = 2N$ is half of $4h^\vee$. Gauging $3g-3$ pairs of $SU(N)$ symmetries of $2g-2$
copies of $T_N$ gives the theory of a genus-$g$ surface, and every degeneration limit of a
surface with full punctures is a generalized quiver of $T_N$ blocks.

$T_2$ is four free hypermultiplets in the $(\mathbf{2},\mathbf{2},\mathbf{2})$ of
$SU(2)^3$, the "blocks of four hypermultiplets" of Gaiotto's generalized $SU(2)$ quivers [@tn-4d/gaiotto2009]. In
$T_3$ the Higgs-branch generators of dimension two include, besides the three moment maps,
operators in the $(\mathbf{3},\mathbf{3},\mathbf{3})$ and $(\bar{\mathbf{3}},\bar{\mathbf{3}},\bar{\mathbf{3}})$,
which enhance $SU(3)^3$ to $E_6$: $T_3$ is the $E_6$ Minahan–Nemeschansky theory. For
$N \geq 4$, $T_N$ is an interacting SCFT with no known Lagrangian.

Gaiotto and Maldacena [@tn-4d/gaiotto2009b] computed $a$ and $c$ by starting from a weakly coupled quiver and
subtracting the weakly coupled tail that decouples in the degeneration limit, and expressed
them through effective numbers $n_v$, $n_h$ of vector and hypermultiplets. They also
constructed the gravity duals, $AdS_5$ solutions of M-theory; at large $N$,
$a \simeq c \simeq N^3/6$. The Coulomb branch has $k-2$ operators of dimension $k$ for
$k = 3,\dots,N$ [@tn-4d/chacaltana2010]. The Higgs-branch chiral ring is generated by the
moment maps $\mu_{1,2,3}$, with
$\mathrm{Tr}\,\mu_1^k = \mathrm{Tr}\,\mu_2^k = \mathrm{Tr}\,\mu_3^k$, and by operators
$Q^{(k)}$ [@tn-4d/beem2013]. The chiral algebra has
$c_{2d} = -12c$ and $\widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(N)^3$ symmetry at level $-N$.

theories.name: $Y^{p,q}$ quiver gauge theories
aliases: Quiver gauge theories dual to $AdS_5\times Y^{p,q}$
theories.summary: An infinite family of $\mathcal{N}=1$ quiver gauge theories with $2p$ $SU(N)$ nodes, living on $N$ D3-branes at the cones over the Sasaki–Einstein manifolds $Y^{p,q}$. Their exact $R$-charges are generically quadratic irrationals, and $a$ agrees with the volume of $Y^{p,q}$.
theories.description:
The $Y^{p,q}$ ($0 < q < p$) are explicit Sasaki–Einstein five-manifolds, of topology $S^2\times S^3$
for coprime $p$, $q$, found by Gauntlett, Martelli, Sparks and Waldram [@ypq-quivers-4d/gmsw2004]; their Calabi–Yau cones are
toric. Benvenuti, Franco, Hanany, Martelli and Sparks (BFHMS) [@ypq-quivers-4d/bfhms2005] constructed the dual gauge theories:
$2p$ gauge groups $SU(N)$ and
$4p+2q$ bifundamental chiral multiplets, namely $p$ $SU(2)$ doublets $U$, $q$ doublets $V$, $p-q$
singlets $Z$ and $p+q$ singlets $Y$. The superpotential has $2q$ cubic and $p-q$ quartic terms,
each $SU(2)$-invariant. The quivers are obtained from the $\mathbb{C}^3/\mathbb{Z}_{2p}$ orbifold quiver
($q = p$) by $p-q$ successive modifications.

The non-$R$ abelian symmetries are a flavour $U(1)_F$ and a baryonic $U(1)_B$, so a-maximization runs
over two parameters, $x = R_Z$ and $y = R_Y$, with $R_U = 1 - \tfrac12(x+y)$ and $R_V = 1 + \tfrac12(x-y)$.
The maximum gives $R$-charges that are generically quadratic irrationals; they are rational when
$4p^2 - 3q^2$ is a perfect square. They equal the $R$-charges of baryons computed from volumes of
supersymmetric 3-cycles, and $a = \pi^3N^2/(4\,\mathrm{Vol}(Y^{p,q}))$ reproduces the volume
$$\mathrm{Vol}(Y^{p,q}) = \frac{q^2\big[2p + \sqrt{4p^2-3q^2}\big]}{3p^2\big[3q^2 - 2p^2 + p\sqrt{4p^2-3q^2}\big]}\,\pi^3 .$$
At leading order $\mathrm{Tr}\,R = 0$, so $a = c$. The volume lies between those of
$T^{1,1}/\mathbb{Z}_p$ and $S^5/(\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_p)$, which BFHMS [@ypq-quivers-4d/bfhms2005] take as the definitions of
$Y^{p,0}$ and $Y^{p,p}$.

theories.name: Free massless Dirac fermion (5d)
theories.summary: A single free massless Dirac fermion in five dimensions, with four complex components. Majorana spinors do not exist in 5d, so this is the smallest free spin-1/2 field; it can equivalently be written as a symplectic-Majorana pair.
theories.description:
A Dirac spinor $\psi$ in $d=5$ has ${\rm Tr}\,\mathbb{1} = 2^{(d-1)/2} = 4$ complex
components. Its propagator is
$\langle\psi(x)\bar\psi(0)\rangle \propto \gamma\cdot x/|x|^{5}$, so $\Delta_\psi = 2$,
and all correlators follow from Wick contractions.

In five-dimensional Minkowski space there are no Majorana spinors, and the
minimal spinor has 8 real components, the content of one Dirac spinor
[@free-fermion-5d/vanproeyen1999, Table 2]. Where the Majorana condition is not available one can
instead impose a symplectic Majorana condition
$(\lambda^i)^* = B\,\Omega_{ij}\lambda^j$ on a pair of spinors $\lambda^{1,2}$,
with $\Omega$ antisymmetric [@free-fermion-5d/vanproeyen1999, Eq. (3.27)]. A symplectic-Majorana pair
has the same 8 real components as one Dirac spinor, so it describes the same free
field. The data below are for one Dirac fermion.

The Dirac mass $\bar\psi\psi$ ($\Delta = 4$) is relevant. As in other odd
dimensions, it is odd under a reflection of one coordinate.

### Sphere free energy
Giombi and Klebanov [@free-fermion-5d/giombi2014] define $\tilde F = \sin(\pi d/2)\log Z_{S^d} = -\sin(\pi d/2)\,F$,
with $F = -\log Z_{S^d}$, so that $\tilde F = \log Z_{S^5} = -F$ in $d=5$. Their
fermion integral [@free-fermion-5d/giombi2014, Eq. (2.6)] is normalized per spinor component, with
${\rm Tr}\,\mathbb{1} = 2^{[d/2]}$; Klebanov, Pufu and Safdi [@free-fermion-5d/klebanov2011, Table 2] tabulate $F$ of a Dirac
fermion divided by $\dim\gamma = 2^{(d-1)/2}$. Both factors equal 4 in $d=5$.

symmetry.spacetime: 5d conformal group with parity
symmetry.global: $U(1)$ fermion number, $\psi\to e^{i\alpha}\psi$ (the manifest symmetry of the Dirac Lagrangian)

quantities.note: Klebanov, Pufu and Safdi [@free-fermion-5d/klebanov2011, Table 2] give $F_D/\dim\gamma = \frac{-1}{2^8}\left(6\log 2 + \frac{10\zeta(3)}{\pi^2} + \frac{15\zeta(5)}{\pi^4}\right) \approx -2.16\times10^{-2}$, with $\dim\gamma = 4$ in $d=5$. Multiplying by 4 and flipping the sign [@free-fermion-5d/giombi2014, Eq. (1.5)] gives this value. Four times a numerical evaluation of [@free-fermion-5d/giombi2014, Eq. (2.6)] at $d=5$ gives the same number.

[@free-fermion-5d/diab2016, fn. 2], with $S_d = 2\pi^{d/2}/\Gamma(d/2)$, at $d=5$: $S_5 = 8\pi^2/3$ and ${\rm Tr}\,\mathbb{1} = 4$. Osborn–Petkou write the factor ${\rm Tr}\,\mathbb{1}$ as $2^{d/2}$, its value in even $d$; for odd $d$ the trace is $2^{[d/2]}$ [@free-fermion-5d/giombi2014, Eq. (2.2)].

theories.name: Free massless scalar (5d)
theories.summary: A single free massless real scalar in five dimensions: the Gaussian fixed point, and the reference value for the 5d sphere free energy and $C_T$.
theories.description:
The simplest CFT in $d=5$. All correlators follow from Wick contractions of
$\langle \phi(x)\phi(0)\rangle \propto |x|^{-3}$, so $\Delta_\phi = \tfrac32$ and
the normal-ordered power $\phi^n$ has $\Delta = \tfrac{3n}{2}$. On a curved
background the scalar is conformally coupled, which fixes its partition
function on the round $S^5$.

In $d=5$ the cubic operator $\phi^3$ is relevant and the quartic operator
$\phi^4$ is irrelevant. For $4<d<6$ the large-$N$ analysis of the $O(N)$ model
with a $(\phi^i\phi^i)^2$ interaction indicates a unitary UV fixed point, and
Fei, Giombi and Klebanov [@free-scalar-5d/fei2014] proposed that the same CFT is the IR fixed point of a
cubic theory of $N+1$ scalars (see the 5d $O(N)$ model entry for its status).
The $\tilde F$-theorem then requires
$N\tilde F_s < \tilde F_{\rm crit} < (N+1)\tilde F_s$, with $\tilde F_s$ the value
below. Fei, Giombi and Klebanov [@free-scalar-5d/fei2014] checked this inequality in $d=5$.

### Sphere free energy
Giombi and Klebanov [@free-scalar-5d/giombi2014, Eq. (1.5)] define $\tilde F = \sin(\pi d/2)\log Z_{S^d} = -\sin(\pi d/2)\,F$,
where $F = -\log Z_{S^d}$. In $d=5$, $\sin(5\pi/2) = 1$, so $\tilde F = \log Z_{S^5} = -F$.
For the free conformal scalar $F$ is negative in $d=5$
[@free-scalar-5d/klebanov2011, Table 1], and $\tilde F$ is positive. For free fields $\tilde F$ is a smooth,
positive function of continuous $d$ that equals $(-1)^{(d+1)/2}F$ in odd $d$ and
tends to $(-1)^{d/2}\frac{\pi}{2}a$ in even $d$. Giombi and Klebanov [@free-scalar-5d/giombi2014] conjecture
that $\tilde F$ decreases under RG flow in every $d$ (the $\tilde F$-theorem).

theories.name: 5d Lee–Yang edge singularity CFT
theories.summary: The non-unitary CFT at the Lee–Yang edge singularity in five dimensions: the fixed point of one scalar with an imaginary cubic coupling, one dimension below its upper critical dimension 6. Its only relevant primary, $\phi$, lies just below the unitarity bound.
theories.description:
The Lee–Yang edge singularity is the end point of the line of zeros of the Ising
partition function in an imaginary magnetic field above the critical temperature.
Fisher [@lee-yang-5d/fisher1978] described it by a scalar with an imaginary cubic coupling, whose upper critical
dimension is 6; at and above $d = 6$ the edge exponent takes its mean-field value
$\sigma = \tfrac12$. In $d = 5$ the fixed point is $\epsilon = 1$ of the $6-\epsilon$
expansion, and the five-loop resummed exponents have errors in the third decimal or
below. The same exponents describe lattice animals (branched polymers) in
$d + 2 = 7$ dimensions [@lee-yang-5d/parisi1981].

The only relevant primary is $\phi$; $\phi^2$ is a descendant of $\phi$ by the equation
of motion [@lee-yang-5d/gliozzi2014], and the next scalar primary, "$\phi^3$", is irrelevant but
only by $\omega \approx 0.7$. The exponents follow from $\Delta_\phi$:
$$\sigma = \frac{\Delta_\phi}{5 - \Delta_\phi}, \qquad \eta = 2\Delta_\phi - 3 .$$
$\Delta_\phi \approx 1.42$ lies below the unitarity bound $\Delta \geq \tfrac32$ for a
5d scalar ($\eta < 0$).

The estimates below come from methods whose error estimates are not directly
comparable: the $6-\epsilon$ expansion to five loops with resummation
[@lee-yang-5d/borinsky2021]; series expansions of the dimer density on the
hypersimple-cubic and hyper-body-centred-cubic lattices in $d = 5$
[@lee-yang-5d/butera2012]; the functional renormalization group [@lee-yang-5d/an2016]; and a
truncated, non-rigorous bootstrap that keeps a few operators in the $\phi\times\phi$
OPE [@lee-yang-5d/gliozzi2014], since the positivity-based numerical bootstrap does not apply to
a non-unitary theory. For $\sigma$ the five-loop and series values agree within about
two standard deviations, while the functional RG and the truncated bootstrap are higher
by about $0.005$ and $0.012$. For $\eta$ the functional RG value differs from the
five-loop one by about four combined standard deviations.

At $N = 0$ the cubic Lagrangian reduces to one scalar with a $\sigma^3$ coupling, Fisher's Lee–Yang theory, whose fixed point sits at imaginary coupling [@on-model-5d/fei2014].

Both are fixed points of cubic scalar theories with upper critical dimension 6: one real field with an imaginary coupling, or $N = q-1 \to 0$ fields with the Potts tensor $d_{ijk}$. Borinsky et al. [@percolation-5d/borinsky2021] obtain both $6-\epsilon$ expansions from the same five-loop renormalization of the general cubic theory, which differ only in the tensor factors of each Feynman graph.

theories.name: 5d $O(N)$ model
aliases: UV fixed point of the $(\phi^i\phi^i)^2$ theory in $d=5$
Cubic $O(N)$ model of Fei, Giombi and Klebanov
theories.summary: Status disputed: the large-$N$ UV fixed point of $N$ scalars with a $(\phi^i\phi^i)^2$ interaction, equivalently the IR fixed point of a cubic theory of $N+1$ scalars. It is unitary order by order in $1/N$, but instantons give its scaling dimensions imaginary parts of order $e^{-Nf}$.
theories.description:
$N$ counts real scalars $\phi^i$. In $d > 4$ the quartic coupling $(\phi^i\phi^i)^2$ is
irrelevant, so $N$ free scalars are the IR end of the flow. At large $N$, a
Hubbard–Stratonovich field $\sigma \sim \phi^i\phi^i$ shows a UV fixed point with
$\Delta_\phi = \tfrac{d}{2} - 1 + O(1/N)$ and $\Delta_\sigma = 2 + O(1/N)$; since
$\Delta_\sigma$ must exceed the unitarity bound $\tfrac{d}{2} - 1$, the interesting range
is $4 < d < 6$. In $d = 4 + \epsilon$ the same fixed point sits at negative quartic
coupling. Fei, Giombi and Klebanov [@on-model-5d/fei2014] proposed that it is the IR fixed point of the cubic
theory below, whose couplings are relevant for $d < 6$: near $d = 6$ the fixed point is
at real couplings for $N$ above a critical value $N_{\rm crit}$, and its $6-\epsilon$
expansions match the $1/N$ expansions of the quartic model.

The fixed point has two relevant $O(N)$ singlets, $\sigma$ and $\sigma^2$, so on a
lattice two couplings would have to be tuned, and even then only near-critical
behaviour in a long-lived metastable state is expected [@on-model-5d/giombi2019]. Its $C_T$ is smaller than that of $N$ free
scalars, so the flow from it to $N$ free scalars violates a would-be $C_T$ theorem, while
the $\tilde F$-theorem holds for the flows from $N+1$ and to $N$ free scalars
[@on-model-5d/fei2014]. At large $N$ the singlet sector is conjectured to be dual to the
Vasiliev higher-spin theory in AdS$_6$ with the alternate ($\Delta = 2 + O(1/N)$)
boundary condition on the bulk scalar; Giombi et al. [@on-model-5d/giombi2019] expect that choice to be
metastable in the bulk as well.

### Status
**Perturbative evidence.** Perturbatively in $1/N$ the fixed point exists, with real
dimensions above the unitarity bounds. How far it extends to finite $N$ is unclear.
The one-loop $N_{\rm crit} \approx 1038$ near $d = 6$ drops to about 64 when the
three-loop series is evaluated at $\epsilon = 1$ [@on-model-5d/fei2014b], but four-loop Padé
approximants settle near 400 in $d = 5$ [@on-model-5d/gracey2015]. The
$1/N^3$ value of $\Delta_\phi$ crosses the unitarity bound at $N \approx 35$, a crude
estimate.

**Instability.** The cubic potential is unbounded below, and on $S^5$ or
$\mathbb{R}\times S^4$ the conformal coupling makes the perturbative vacuum metastable.
Giombi et al. [@on-model-5d/giombi2019] studied the instantons that mediate the decay, both near $d = 6$ and at
large $N$. They give the scaling dimensions, the sphere free energy, $C_J$ and OPE
coefficients imaginary parts of order $e^{-Nf(d)}$, where $f(d)$ is the sphere free
energy of a conformal scalar in $d - 2$ dimensions, with
$f(5) = \frac{\log 2}{8} - \frac{3\zeta(3)}{16\pi^2} \approx 0.0638$. So at every
finite $N$ the theory is at best a complex CFT. In $d = 5$, $|{\rm Im}\,\Delta_\phi| < 10^{-2}$ ($10^{-3}$) requires
$N > 172$ ($220$), and $|{\rm Im}\,\Delta_\sigma| < 10^{-2}$ ($10^{-3}$) requires
$N > 310$ ($355$). This fits the expectation, supported by rigorous results, that
interacting $\phi^4$ theory has no true critical point in $d > 4$.

**Bootstrap.** Unitarity-based bootstrap studies find features at the large-$N$ values
but disagree on small $N$. Nakayama and Ohtsuki [@on-model-5d/nakayama2014] find that the lower bound on $C_J$ has a
minimum at the large-$N$ $\Delta_\phi$ for $N = 500$ and $1000$; the minimum persists for
all $N$ they studied. Chester, Pufu and Yacoby [@on-model-5d/chester2014] find a kink at the large-$N$ values for
$N = 500$, which disappears between $N = 15$ and $22$ (assuming
$\Delta_{\sigma^2} \ge 3.8$). Bae and Rey [@on-model-5d/bae2014], with a different two-gap approach, find
indications that the fixed point persists down to $N = 1$. Li and Su [@on-model-5d/li2016], with mixed
correlators, find a closed island around the large-$N$ values at $N = 500$, but for
$N \le 100$ their islands disappear as the number of derivatives grows, and they
conclude that the unitary range starts above $N = 100$. Giombi et al. [@on-model-5d/giombi2019] note that their
thresholds on $N$ are roughly commensurate with Li and Su's, and that the bootstrap
cannot distinguish a complex CFT with tiny imaginary parts from a unitary one.

For $2 < d < 4$ the critical $O(N)$ model is the IR (Wilson–Fisher) fixed point of the quartic theory; for $4 < d < 6$ the $1/N$ expansion continues to a UV fixed point of the quartic theory, equivalently an IR fixed point of the cubic theory [@on-model-5d/fei2014].
The fixed point flows in the IR to $N$ free scalars and, in the cubic description, is reached from $N+1$ free scalars; the sphere free energy satisfies $N\tilde F_s < \tilde F < (N+1)\tilde F_s$.
At $N = 0$ the cubic Lagrangian reduces to one scalar with a $\sigma^3$ coupling, Fisher's Lee–Yang theory, whose fixed point sits at imaginary coupling [@on-model-5d/fei2014].

theories.name: 5d percolation CFT
aliases: Bond and site percolation universality class (5d)
theories.summary: The critical point of bond and site percolation in five dimensions, the $q \to 1$ limit of the $q$-state Potts model, one dimension below the upper critical dimension 6. A non-unitary CFT, expected to be logarithmic, with exponents from Monte Carlo and the $6-\epsilon$ expansion.
theories.description:
Percolation is the $q \to 1$ limit of the Fortuin–Kasteleyn cluster representation of
the $q$-state Potts model. Its field theory is a cubic theory of $N = q - 1$ scalars
with the $S_q$-invariant tensor coupling $d_{ijk}$, continued to $N \to 0$, with upper
critical dimension 6. In $d = 5$ it is $\epsilon = 1$ of the $6-\epsilon$ expansion, and
the five-loop resummed $\nu$ and $\eta$ agree with the Monte Carlo values to within
about $0.005$.

The thermal operator $\epsilon$, an $S_q$ singlet coupled to $p - p_c$, has
$\Delta_\epsilon = 5 - 1/\nu$. The order-parameter (spin) operator $\sigma$, in the
$(q-1)$-dimensional representation of $S_q$, has $\Delta_\sigma = 5 - d_f$, where $d_f$
is the fractal dimension of critical clusters, and $\eta = 2\Delta_\sigma - 3$.
$\Delta_\sigma \approx 1.474$ lies below the unitarity bound $\Delta \geq \tfrac32$ for a
5d scalar ($\eta < 0$).

The most precise values come from Monte Carlo simulations of bond percolation on
hypercubic lattices: the two-cluster exponent, which equals $\Delta_\epsilon$, from a
transfer Monte Carlo method on cylinders [@percolation-5d/tan2020], and $d_f$ on periodic
hypercubes [@percolation-5d/zhang2021]. For $1/\nu$ these two groups and Koza and
Poła [@percolation-5d/koza2016] (site percolation, $1/\nu \approx 1.747$) differ by up to about two standard
deviations; Tan et al. [@percolation-5d/tan2020] argue that the central value $1.747$ is nearly excluded by their
data.

### Logarithmic CFT
Vasseur, Jacobsen and Saleur [@percolation-5d/vasseur2012] showed that at $q = 1$ the thermal operator mixes with a
partner that creates two propagating clusters, so that suitable two-point functions
scale logarithmically, and expect the mechanism to hold also for $d > 2$. Tan, Deng and
Jacobsen [@percolation-5d/tan2020] measured the $N$-cluster correlation functions ($N = 2, 3$) of this
logarithmic CFT in $d = 4$ and $5$, including the logarithmic combination and its
universal amplitude, and conclude that their results confirm the logarithmic CFT
description.

theories.name: Seiberg $E_n$ theories
aliases: UV completions of 5d $SU(2)$ gauge theory with $N_f \le 7$ flavors
theories.summary: The interacting 5d $\mathcal{N}=1$ SCFTs with a one-dimensional Coulomb branch. For $1\le n\le 8$ the $E_n$ theory has $E_n$ flavor symmetry and flows to $SU(2)$ gauge theory with $N_f=n-1$ flavors; the family also contains $\tilde E_1$ and $E_0$.
theories.description:
Five-dimensional $SU(2)$ gauge theory with $N_f$ fundamental hypermultiplets is
non-renormalizable, but on its Coulomb branch $\mathbb{R}^+$ the one-loop effective coupling
at zero masses is $1/g_{\rm eff}^2 = 1/g^2 + 2(8-N_f)\phi$. For $N_f\le7$ it stays positive as
$g\to\infty$, and Seiberg [@seiberg-en-5d/seiberg1996] argued, from the D4–D8–O8 system of type I$'$ string theory, that this
limit is an interacting SCFT. Its flavor symmetry is $E_{N_f+1}$, enhanced from the
$SO(2N_f)\times U(1)_I$ of the gauge theory, where $U(1)_I$ is the instanton-number symmetry:
$E_8$, $E_7$, $E_6$, $E_5=Spin(10)$, $E_4=SU(5)$, $E_3=SU(3)\times SU(2)$,
$E_2=SU(2)\times U(1)$ and $E_1=SU(2)$. The inverse coupling $1/g^2$, of mass dimension one,
is a relevant deformation of the SCFT; it triggers the flow to the gauge theory. The quark
masses are further relevant deformations and induce flows $E_n\to E_m$, $m<n$. The Higgs branch
is the moduli space of $E_n$ instantons.

Morrison and Seiberg [@seiberg-en-5d/morrison1996] found two more rank-1 fixed points. $\tilde E_1$ has $U(1)$ flavor
symmetry, one relevant parameter and no Higgs branch. $E_0$ has no flavor symmetry and no
relevant deformation that preserves super-Poincaré symmetry, so it is not the UV completion of
any gauge theory. Pure $SU(2)$ gauge theory has a discrete theta angle,
$\theta\in\{0,\pi\}$, from $\pi_4(SU(2))=\mathbb{Z}_2$; $E_1$ completes the theory at
$\theta=0$ and $\tilde E_1$ the theory at $\theta=\pi$. For $N_f>0$ the two values of
$\theta$ give equivalent theories. In M-theory on a Calabi–Yau threefold these SCFTs appear
when a del Pezzo surface shrinks to a point: $E_{N+1}$ for $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$
blown up at $N$ points, $\tilde E_1$ for $\mathbb{P}^2$ blown up at one point, and $E_0$ for
$\mathbb{P}^2$. Ganor, Morrison and Seiberg [@seiberg-en-5d/ganor1996] obtain the $E_n$ theories from the circle
compactification of the 6d E-string theory.

### Localization data
Chang, Fluder, Lin and Wang [@seiberg-en-5d/chang2017] computed the $S^5$ partition function of the $E_1,\dots,E_8$ and
$\tilde E_1$ theories from the infrared $SU(2)$ gauge theory, assuming that it factorizes into
three Nekrasov partition functions, and summed the instanton series to four instantons. They
define $F = -\log Z_{S^5}$ and tabulate $-F$, which is positive. In the convention
$\tilde F = \log|Z_{S^5}|$ of Klebanov, Pufu and Safdi [@seiberg-en-5d/klebanov2011, Sec. 2], $\tilde F = -F$. Their
$C_T$ is normalized so that a free real scalar has $C_T = d/(d-1) = 5/4$, a free Dirac fermion
$C_T = 10$, and a free hypermultiplet $C_T = 15$. The members table quotes their four-instanton
totals [@seiberg-en-5d/chang2017, Tables 2–3]. No error estimates are given; the summed instanton corrections to
$-F$ are at most $1.2\times10^{-2}$ in magnitude. Along the flows $E_n\to E_m$ both $-F$ and $C_T$
decrease. $E_0$ has no gauge-theory description, and no such data exist for it.
