theories.name: 5d $USp(2N)$ SCFTs with an antisymmetric hypermultiplet
aliases: 5d SCFTs dual to massive IIA on AdS$_6$
theories.summary: The UV fixed points of 5d $USp(2N)$ gauge theory with one antisymmetric and $N_f\le7$ fundamental hypermultiplets, on $N$ D4-branes near an O8-plane with $N_f$ D8-branes. Flavor symmetry $E_{N_f+1}\times SU(2)$; at large $N$ they are dual to massive type IIA on a warped AdS$_6$ background.
theories.description:
The rank-$N$ generalization of the Seiberg $E_n$ theories. $N$ D4-branes probe an O8-plane
with $N_f$ coincident D8-branes in type I$'$ string theory. At finite coupling their
world-volume theory is 5d $\mathcal{N}=1$ $USp(2N)$ gauge theory with $N_f$ fundamental
hypermultiplets and one hypermultiplet in the antisymmetric representation. For $N_f\le7$ the
infinite-coupling limit is expected to be an interacting SCFT [@usp-5d/intriligator1997]. Its flavor symmetry $E_{N_f+1}\times SU(2)$ is enhanced from the
$SO(2N_f)\times U(1)_I\times SU(2)$ of the gauge theory, where $U(1)_I$ counts instantons and
$SU(2)$ acts on the antisymmetric hypermultiplet. The Higgs branch is expected to be the moduli
space of $N$ $E_{N_f+1}$ instantons. At $N_f=0$ there are two fixed points, analogues of $E_1$
and $\tilde E_1$, labeled by the discrete theta angle of $USp(2N)$, and an analogue of $E_0$.
At $N=1$ the antisymmetric representation of $USp(2)=SU(2)$ is trivial, the antisymmetric
hypermultiplet is free and decoupled, and the extra $SU(2)$ acts only on it.

Brandhuber and Oz [@usp-5d/brandhuber1999] found the dual background as the near-horizon limit of the D4–D8 system in
massive type IIA supergravity: a warped product of AdS$_6$ with a hemisphere of $S^4$. Its
boundary, at the O8-plane, has the form AdS$_6\times S^3$; there the dilaton diverges and the
$E_{N_f+1}$ gauge fields live. The $SO(4) = SU(2)\times SU(2)$ isometry is the $SU(2)_R$
R-symmetry times the $SU(2)$ flavor symmetry, and the superalgebra is $F(4)$. Supergravity is
reliable at large $N$ away from the boundary, and its action scales as $N^{5/2}$.

Jafferis and Pufu [@usp-5d/jafferis2012] evaluated the $S^5$ partition function of the gauge theory at large $N$ by
supersymmetric localization. They argue that instanton contributions are exponentially
suppressed there, and they reproduce the $N^{5/2}$ scaling. The free energy agrees with a
holographic computation of the entanglement entropy in the dual. Chang, Fluder, Lin and Wang [@usp-5d/chang2018]
extracted $C_T$ from the squashed-sphere partition function and matched it to Romans $F(4)$
gauged supergravity.

theories.name: 6d conformal matter
theories.summary: The 6d $(1,0)$ theory on one M5-brane probing the ADE singularity $\mathbb{C}^2/\Gamma_G$, with $G\times G$ flavor symmetry. It is a free bifundamental hypermultiplet for $G=SU(k)$ and an interacting SCFT for $G$ of type $D$ or $E$.
theories.description:
M-theory on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{C}^2/\Gamma_G$, with $\Gamma_G\subset SU(2)$ the finite
subgroup of type $G = A, D, E$, carries 7d super Yang–Mills theory with gauge group $G$. An
M5-brane at a point of $\mathbb{R}$ is a domain wall of this theory, and the 7d gauge fields on
its two sides give the 6d theory on the brane a $G_L\times G_R$ flavor symmetry. Del Zotto,
Heckman, Tomasiello and Vafa [@conformal-matter-6d/delzotto2014] call it $(G,G)$ conformal matter, since it plays the role of
bifundamental matter. For $G=SU(k)$ it is a free hypermultiplet in the bifundamental. For $D$-
and $E$-type $G$ it is an interacting 6d $(1,0)$ SCFT. In F-theory it sits where two
non-compact seven-branes with gauge algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ collide; resolving the collision
gives its tensor branch, on which the M5-brane splits into fractional M5-branes.

The tensor branches (curves listed by minus their self-intersection) are:
$(D_k,D_k)$, one $-1$ curve with $\mathfrak{usp}(2k-8)$ and half-hypermultiplets in the
bifundamentals of $\mathfrak{so}(2k)\times\mathfrak{usp}(2k-8)$ on each side;
$(E_6,E_6)$, curves $1,3,1$ with $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ on the $-3$ curve;
$(E_7,E_7)$, curves $1,2,3,2,1$ with $\mathfrak{su}(2)\oplus\mathfrak{so}(7)\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$;
$(E_8,E_8)$, curves $1,2,2,3,1,5,1,3,2,2,1$ with
$\mathfrak{sp}(1)$, $\mathfrak{g}_2$, $\mathfrak{f}_4$, $\mathfrak{g}_2$, $\mathfrak{sp}(1)$ on the
third, fourth, sixth, eighth and ninth curves. The empty curves carry E-strings: rank 1 on an
isolated $-1$ curve, rank 2 on the $1,2$ ends of the $(E_8,E_8)$ chain.
$N$ M5-branes on the singularity give a generalized quiver with gauge group $G^{N-1}$ on a chain
of $-2$ curves, linked by conformal matter.

### Anomalies
Ohmori, Shimizu, Tachikawa and Yonekura [@conformal-matter-6d/ohmori2014b] obtain the anomaly polynomial by anomaly matching on
the tensor branch:
$I_8 = \frac{\alpha}{24}c_2(R)^2 - \frac{\beta}{48}c_2(R)p_1(T) + \gamma\,\frac{7p_1(T)^2-4p_2(T)}{5760} + \left(-\frac{x}{8}c_2(R)+\frac{y}{96}p_1(T)\right)\left(\mathrm{Tr}F_L^2+\mathrm{Tr}F_R^2\right) + \frac{1}{48}\left(\mathrm{tr}_G F_L^4+\mathrm{tr}_G F_R^4\right) - \frac12\left(\frac14\mathrm{Tr}F_L^2-\frac14\mathrm{Tr}F_R^2\right)^2$
[@conformal-matter-6d/ohmori2014b, Eq. (3.19)], with $\gamma = \dim G + 1$, $x = |\Gamma_G| - h^\vee_G$ and $y = h^\vee_G$.
The members table gives [@conformal-matter-6d/ohmori2014b, Table 1]. The $a$-anomaly, in the normalization with $a = 1$ for
a free $(2,0)$ tensor multiplet, is derived here from the formula of Córdova, Dumitrescu and
Intriligator [@conformal-matter-6d/cordova2015], which in the coefficients above reads
$a = \tfrac{16}{7}\alpha + \tfrac{8}{7}\beta + \tfrac{11}{210}\gamma$.

The tensor branches of $(E_6,E_6)$ and $(E_8,E_8)$ conformal matter contain the $-3$ curve with $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ and the $-5$ curve with $\mathfrak{f}_4$ of the minimal 6d SCFTs, joined to the rest through $-1$ curves.

theories.name: E-string theory
theories.summary: The 6d $(1,0)$ SCFT on $Q$ M5-branes inside the $E_8$ end-of-the-world brane of M-theory, equivalently $Q$ small $E_8$ instantons of the heterotic string. Flavor symmetry $E_8$ ($E_8\times SU(2)$ for $Q\ge2$); its anomaly polynomial is known exactly.
theories.description:
When an $E_8$ instanton of the $E_8\times E_8$ heterotic string shrinks to zero size, a
tensionless non-critical string appears [@e-string-6d/ganor1996a; @e-string-6d/seiberg1996b], and the low-energy
theory near the small instanton is an interacting 6d $(1,0)$ SCFT with $E_8$ flavor symmetry.
In M-theory it lives on an M5-brane inside the $E_8$ end-of-the-world brane. $Q$ coincident
M5-branes give the rank-$Q$ E-string theory together with a decoupled free hypermultiplet,
the center-of-mass motion along the wall. Its tensor branch has dimension $Q$ and is reached
by moving the M5-branes off the wall. The Higgs branch is the moduli space of $Q$ $E_8$
instantons, of quaternionic dimension $30Q$; it is reached by dissolving the M5-branes into
the wall. The R-symmetry is $SU(2)_R\subset SO(4)$, the rotations transverse to the branes
within the wall. The other factor $SU(2)_L$ is a flavor symmetry; at $Q=1$ it acts only on the
free hypermultiplet. Like every 6d $(1,0)$ SCFT, the theory has no relevant or marginal
supersymmetric deformation.

In F-theory the rank-1 theory comes from a single curve of self-intersection $-1$ in the base
carrying no gauge algebra, and the rank-$Q$ theory from the chain of curves $1,2,\dots,2$
(in minus the self-intersections). It is the glue of the F-theory classification: other 6d
SCFTs are built by joining curves with gauge algebras through $-1$ curves, which gauges a
subgroup of the $E_8$ of the E-string. The anomaly polynomial, computed by anomaly inflow
[@e-string-6d/ohmori2014a] and rederived from the circle compactification [@e-string-6d/ohmori2014b], determines the anomalies below.

theories.name: Free massless scalar (6d)
theories.summary: A single free massless real scalar in six dimensions: the Gaussian fixed point, and the simplest field for the 6d Weyl anomaly. Five of them, with two Weyl fermions and a self-dual 2-form, make up the free (2,0) tensor multiplet.
theories.description:
The simplest CFT in $d=6$. All correlators follow from Wick contractions of
$\langle \phi(x)\phi(0)\rangle \propto |x|^{-4}$, so $\Delta_\phi = 2$ and
$\phi^n$ has $\Delta = 2n$. The cubic operator $\phi^3$ is classically marginal.
On a curved background the scalar is conformally coupled, with kinetic operator
$-\nabla^2 + \tfrac15 R$.

The free $(2,0)$ tensor multiplet, the low-energy theory on a single M5-brane,
consists of 5 such scalars, 2 Weyl fermions and a 2-form with self-dual field
strength [@free-scalar-6d/bastianelli2000].

### Weyl anomaly
On a curved background the trace of the stress tensor of a 6d CFT has the form
[@free-scalar-6d/bastianelli2000, Eqs. (1.1), (2.9)]
$$\langle T^m{}_m\rangle = a\,E_6 + c_1 I_1 + c_2 I_2 + c_3 I_3 + \nabla_i J^i ,$$
with the Euler density $E_6 = -\epsilon_6\epsilon_6 RRR$ and the Weyl invariants
$I_1 = C_{amnb}C^{mijn}C_i{}^{ab}{}_j$,
$I_2 = C_{ab}{}^{mn}C_{mn}{}^{ij}C_{ij}{}^{ab}$ and
$I_3 = C_{mabc}\left(\nabla^2\delta^m_n + 4R^m_n - \tfrac65 R\,\delta^m_n\right)C^{nabc}$
plus a total derivative. The last term is scheme dependent. The coefficients are
computed from the heat-kernel coefficient $b_6$ of the kinetic operator. In this
normalization $a$ is negative for the free scalar, the Dirac fermion and the
2-form; other papers use other signs and normalizations. Bastianelli, Frolov and Tseytlin [@free-scalar-6d/bastianelli2000] relate $c_3$ to the
coefficient of $\langle TT\rangle$, and $c_1, c_2$ to $\langle TTT\rangle$.

Giombi and Klebanov's [@free-scalar-6d/giombi2014] $\tilde F = \sin(\pi d/2)\log Z_{S^d}$, continued in $d$, is
finite at $d=6$ and equals $(-1)^{d/2}\frac{\pi}{2}a$ for the $a$-anomaly in their
own normalization, which differs from the one above.

theories.name: Free self-dual 2-form (6d)
theories.summary: A free 2-form gauge field in six dimensions whose 3-form field strength is self-dual. It is conformal, unlike free Maxwell theory in $d \neq 4$, and is the chiral bosonic field of the free (2,0) and (1,0) tensor multiplets.
theories.description:
The gauge field is a 2-form $B$ with gauge symmetry $B \to B + d\Lambda$. Its field
strength $H = dB$ is a 3-form, constrained to be self-dual, $H = \star H$ (or
anti-self-dual, depending on conventions). The two-point function of $H$ falls
off as $|x|^{-6}$, so $\Delta_H = 3$. A free $k$-form gauge field is conformal in
$d = 2k+2$ [@free-self-dual-tensor-6d/bastianelli1999]: $k=1$ is Maxwell theory in
$d=4$, and $k=2$ is this theory. Free Maxwell theory in $d \neq 4$ is scale
invariant but not conformal [@free-self-dual-tensor-6d/elshowk2011].

Lorentz-covariant actions for the self-dual field exist, for example that of
Pasti, Sorokin and Tonin [@free-self-dual-tensor-6d/pst1997], with one auxiliary scalar entering non-polynomially,
but they are hard to use at the quantum level. In practice correlators and
anomalies are computed with a non-chiral 2-form, projecting onto the self-dual
part of $H$ in composite operators. With this prescription the two- and
three-point functions of the stress tensor of the chiral field are half those of
the non-chiral 2-form [@free-self-dual-tensor-6d/bastianelli1999], and so is its
trace anomaly [@free-self-dual-tensor-6d/bastianelli2000].

A self-dual antisymmetric tensor coupled to gravity in $4k+2$ dimensions has a
one-loop gravitational anomaly [@free-self-dual-tensor-6d/agw1984].

### Tensor multiplets
The free $(2,0)$ tensor multiplet, the low-energy theory on a single M5-brane,
consists of 5 real scalars, 2 Weyl fermions and this field. Its trace anomaly
[@free-self-dual-tensor-6d/bastianelli2000, Eq. (2.29)] has $a = -\frac{245}{8}$,
$c_1 = -1680$, $c_2 = -420$, $c_3 = 140$, in units of $\frac{1}{(4\pi)^3\,7!}$ and
the conventions of the free 6d scalar page, and $C_T = \frac{84}{\pi^6}$
[@free-self-dual-tensor-6d/bastianelli1999, Eq. (3.23)]. The values for the free
scalar, the free Weyl fermion and this field add up to these totals. Compared
with the AdS$_7$ supergravity prediction for the $(2,0)$ theory of $N$ M5-branes
at large $N$, the coefficients obey $c_n^{(2,0)} = 4N^3 c_n^{\rm (tens.)}$ but
$a^{(2,0)} = \frac{16}{7}N^3 a^{\rm (tens.)}$ [@free-self-dual-tensor-6d/bastianelli2000, Eq. (1.4)].

A self-dual tensor also sits in each $(1,0)$ tensor multiplet. On the tensor
branch of 6d $(1,0)$ SCFTs its Bianchi identity can be deformed to $dH = I$, which
gives the Green–Schwarz contribution to the anomaly polynomial
[@free-self-dual-tensor-6d/osty2014].

theories.name: Free massless Weyl fermion (6d)
theories.summary: A single free massless Weyl fermion in six dimensions. It is chiral, so it has a gravitational anomaly; two of them are the fermions of the free (2,0) tensor multiplet.
theories.description:
A Weyl spinor $\psi$ in $d=6$ has 4 complex components, half of the
${\rm Tr}\,\mathbb{1} = 2^{d/2} = 8$ of a Dirac spinor. The propagator
$\langle\psi(x)\bar\psi(0)\rangle \propto \gamma\cdot x/|x|^{6}$, projected on one
chirality, gives $\Delta_\psi = \tfrac52$, and all correlators follow from Wick
contractions. In six-dimensional Minkowski space there are no Majorana or
Majorana–Weyl spinors, but symplectic Majorana–Weyl spinors exist, and the
minimal spinor has 8 real components [@free-weyl-fermion-6d/vanproeyen1999, Table 2], the content of one
Weyl spinor.

A Weyl fermion of spin $\tfrac12$ coupled to gravity in $4k+2$ dimensions has a
one-loop gravitational anomaly [@free-weyl-fermion-6d/agw1984], so this theory cannot
be coupled consistently to dynamical gravity on its own. The anomaly comes from
the imaginary part of the Weyl determinant. The trace anomaly comes from the real
part and is half that of a Dirac fermion (Bastianelli, Frolov and Tseytlin [@free-weyl-fermion-6d/bastianelli2000, Sec. 2], who
write the $(2,0)$ tensor multiplet anomaly as half that of a non-chiral multiplet
with Dirac fermions).

The free $(2,0)$ tensor multiplet consists of 5 scalars, 2 such Weyl fermions and
a 2-form with self-dual field strength.

### Weyl anomaly
The coefficients $a, c_1, c_2, c_3$ below are those of
$\langle T^m{}_m\rangle = a\,E_6 + c_1 I_1 + c_2 I_2 + c_3 I_3 + \nabla_i J^i$ in
the conventions of Bastianelli, Frolov and Tseytlin [@free-weyl-fermion-6d/bastianelli2000], defined on the page of the
free 6d scalar. Each is half of the Dirac-fermion value in [@free-weyl-fermion-6d/bastianelli2000, Eq. (2.20)].

theories.name: Minimal 6d $(1,0)$ SCFTs (non-Higgsable clusters)
theories.summary: The 6d $(1,0)$ SCFTs of F-theory on one curve of self-intersection $-n$, $n=3,\dots,8,12$. On the tensor branch they are $\mathfrak{su}(3)$, $\mathfrak{so}(8)$, $\mathfrak{f}_4$, $\mathfrak{e}_6$, $\mathfrak{e}_7$ or $\mathfrak{e}_8$ gauge theories, with a half-hypermultiplet at $n=7$.
theories.description:
In F-theory on an elliptically fibered Calabi–Yau threefold, a rational curve of
self-intersection $-n$ with $n\ge3$ in the base forces a singular elliptic fiber over it, and
hence a gauge algebra that cannot be Higgsed [@nhc-6d/morrison2012]. For an isolated curve the
algebra and matter are fixed by $n$: $\mathfrak{su}(3)$, $\mathfrak{so}(8)$, $\mathfrak{f}_4$,
$\mathfrak{e}_6$ for $n=3,4,5,6$, $\mathfrak{e}_7$ with a half-hypermultiplet in the
$\mathbf{56}$ for $n=7$, $\mathfrak{e}_7$ for $n=8$, and $\mathfrak{e}_8$ for $n=12$. Curves
with $n=9,10,11$ require further blow-ups of the base, a $-1$ curve gives the rank-1 E-string
and a $-2$ curve the $A_1$ $(2,0)$ theory. Shrinking the curve to zero size gives a 6d SCFT.
On its tensor branch there is one tensor multiplet, whose scalar sets the inverse gauge
coupling, the vector multiplet, and at $n=7$ the half-hypermultiplet. The SCFTs have no Higgs
branch. "Minimal" here means these single-curve clusters; the two- and three-curve
non-Higgsable clusters ($\mathfrak{g}_2\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and
$\mathfrak{su}(2)\oplus\mathfrak{so}(7)\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$) are not included.

The non-Higgsable clusters and chains of $-2$ curves are the building blocks of the F-theory
classification of 6d SCFTs: they are glued by $-1$ curves, and the algebras
$\mathfrak{g}_L$, $\mathfrak{g}_R$ on the two curves meeting a $-1$ curve must satisfy
$\mathfrak{g}_L\times\mathfrak{g}_R\subset\mathfrak{e}_8$ [@nhc-6d/heckman2015].

### Anomalies
Ohmori, Shimizu, Tachikawa and Yonekura [@nhc-6d/ohmori2014b] obtain the anomaly polynomial of the SCFT on its tensor
branch: the one-loop anomaly of the tensor, vector and hypermultiplets plus a Green–Schwarz
term $\tfrac{n}{2}I^2$, fixed by the cancellation of gauge anomalies. In their conventions
$I = \tfrac14\mathrm{Tr}F^2 + \tfrac{n-2}{4n}p_1(T) + \tfrac{h^\vee}{n}c_2(R)$, where Tr is the
adjoint trace divided by the dual Coxeter number $h^\vee$ ([@nhc-6d/ohmori2014b, Eqs. (3.29)–(3.32)] for one
curve). They give the $c_2(R)^2$ coefficient in closed form. The full coefficients and $a$ in
the members table were computed here with the same procedure and are marked as derived. As
checks, the $c_2(R)^2$ coefficients agree with [@nhc-6d/ohmori2014b, Eq. (1.11)], and the same computation
reproduces their $(E_6,E_6)$ conformal-matter anomaly [@nhc-6d/ohmori2014b, Eq. (3.12)]. The normalization is that
of Córdova, Dumitrescu and Intriligator [@nhc-6d/cordova2015],
$I_8 = \tfrac{1}{4!}\left(\alpha c_2(R)^2 + \beta c_2(R)p_1(T) + \gamma p_1(T)^2 + \delta p_2(T)\right)$,
and $a = \tfrac{16}{7}(\alpha-\beta+\gamma)+\tfrac67\delta$, with $a=1$ for a free $(2,0)$
tensor multiplet.

theories.name: Branched polymers (7d)
theories.summary: The critical point of randomly branched polymers (lattice animals) in seven dimensions: an interacting, non-unitary fixed point above six dimensions, described by a Parisi–Sourlas supersymmetric theory that reduces to the 5d Lee–Yang CFT.
theories.description:
A branched polymer is a connected cluster (a "lattice animal", or a tree) on a lattice. The
number of $N$-site animals grows as $P(N) \sim N^{-\theta}\lambda^N$ and their size as
$R \sim N^\nu$. Their field theory is a cubic theory in a replica limit; Parisi and Sourlas [@branched-polymers-7d/parisi1981]
interpreted it as a random-field model with cubic potential and showed that its supersymmetry relates branched polymers in $d$ dimensions to the Lee–Yang edge
singularity in $d-2$ dimensions. The upper critical dimension is therefore 8
[@branched-polymers-7d/kaviraj2020b, App. A.4], so the fixed point is interacting in $d = 7$, the only integer
dimension above six where it is.

Brydges and Imbrie [@branched-polymers-7d/brydges2003] proved the dimensional reduction exactly for a continuum model of
branched polymers with manifest supersymmetry, mapping it to the hard-core gas at negative
activity in $d-2$ dimensions, a microscopic realization of the Lee–Yang class. Kaviraj,
Rychkov and Trevisani [@branched-polymers-7d/kaviraj2020] showed in general how a $d$-dimensional Parisi–Sourlas supersymmetric
CFT reduces to an ordinary CFT in $d-2$ dimensions. The predicted relations are
$\theta(d) = \sigma_{\rm LY}(d-2) + 2$ and $\theta = (d-2)\nu + 1$. Monte Carlo simulations of
lattice animals confirm them below the upper critical dimension. At $d = 8$ the exponents take
the values $\theta = 5/2$, $\nu = 1/4$ with logarithmic corrections, and above $d = 8$ they stay
at these mean-field values, where the second relation no longer holds
[@branched-polymers-7d/hsu2005, Table I].

symmetry.notes: The Parisi–Sourlas supersymmetry acts on a superspace with two Grassmann coordinates; it is not a Poincaré supersymmetry.

theories.name: Free massless Dirac fermion ($d > 6$)
theories.summary: A single free massless Dirac fermion in $d = 7, \dots, 11$ dimensions, filed under $d = 7$. With the free scalar and the free middle-form field, it is one of the only known unitary CFTs above six dimensions.
theories.description:
One page for the free Dirac fermion in every dimension above six; the members table lists
the values for each $d$. The propagator is
$\langle\psi(x)\bar\psi(0)\rangle = \frac{1}{S_d}\frac{\gamma\cdot x}{|x|^d}$, so
$\Delta_\psi = \tfrac{d-1}{2}$. A Dirac spinor has ${\rm Tr}\,\mathbb{1} = 2^{[d/2]}$ complex
components (8 in $d=7$, 16 in $d=8, 9$, 32 in $d=10, 11$). In even $d$ a Weyl fermion has half
as many, and half the $C_T$ below. The mass term $\bar\psi\psi$ has $\Delta = d-1 < d$ and is
relevant, while every four-fermion interaction has $\Delta = 2(d-1) > d$ and is irrelevant.

See the free-scalar page ($d > 6$) for why free fields are the only known unitary CFTs in
this range.

theories.name: Free massless scalar ($d > 6$)
aliases: Free conformal scalar in high dimensions
theories.summary: A single free massless real scalar in $d = 7, \dots, 11$ dimensions, filed under $d = 7$. Above six dimensions free fields are the only known unitary CFTs, and there are no superconformal theories at all.
theories.description:
One page for the free scalar in every dimension above six; the members table lists the
values for each $d$. All correlators follow from Wick contractions of
$\langle \phi(x)\phi(0)\rangle \propto |x|^{-(d-2)}$, so $\Delta_\phi = \tfrac{d-2}{2}$ and
$\phi^n$ has $\Delta = \tfrac{n(d-2)}{2}$. Already $\phi^3$ is irrelevant for $d > 6$, so
no polynomial interaction of a single scalar is renormalizable there.

### CFTs above six dimensions
Superconformal algebras exist only for $d \le 6$ [@free-scalar-d7plus/nahm1978], so there are no SCFTs in
$d > 6$. The familiar interacting fixed points of statistical mechanics become Gaussian
above their upper critical dimension: 4 for the Ising and $O(N)$ classes, 6 for
$\phi^3$-type theories (Lee–Yang, percolation). No interacting unitary CFT is known in
$d > 6$, although there is no general theorem excluding one. Free scalars, free fermions
and, in even $d$, the free $(d/2-1)$-form gauge field are the known unitary examples. The
critical point of branched polymers is an interacting but non-unitary example in $d = 7$.

theories.name: Free $(d/2-1)$-form gauge field ($d = 8, 10$)
theories.summary: The free gauge field whose field strength has rank $d/2$: a 3-form potential in $d=8$ and a 4-form potential in $d=10$ (optionally with self-dual field strength). Filed under $d=8$. It is the even-$d$ analogue of Maxwell theory in 4d and of the self-dual 2-form in 6d.
theories.description:
In $d = 2n$ the standard free kinetic term of an $(n-1)$-form potential $A$ is conformally
invariant [@free-form-d8plus/buchel2010]. The gauge-invariant local operator is the field strength
$F = dA$, an $n$-form of dimension $\Delta = n = d/2$. Maxwell theory is the case $n = 2$; in
$d \ne 4$ the free Maxwell field is scale but not conformally invariant [@free-form-d8plus/elshowk2011], which is why only the middle-dimensional form appears here.

For odd $n$ one may impose that $F$ be (anti-)self-dual, which halves the number of degrees of
freedom and $C_T$ [@free-form-d8plus/buchel2010]. In this range that happens in $d = 10$ (a chiral 4-form, as
in type IIB supergravity); the 6d case is the separate self-dual tensor page.

members.label: 3-form potential
members.note: $\Delta_F = 4$; $\tilde n_t = 20$; $C_T = \frac{5760}{\pi^8}$ (560 times the free scalar).

members.label: 4-form potential
members.note: $\Delta_F = 5$; $\tilde n_t = 70$; $C_T = \frac{504000}{\pi^{10}}$ (3150 times the free scalar). With self-dual $F$: $\tilde n_t = 35$, $C_T = \frac{252000}{\pi^{10}}$.

methods.name: Exact result
methods.description: Known in closed form or to arbitrary precision: a solved model, a symmetry or a proof. The qualifier says how, e.g. `exact, planar limit`.

methods.name: Numerical conformal bootstrap
methods.description: Crossing symmetry and unitarity of four-point functions, imposed numerically (usually by semidefinite programming), exclude regions of CFT data. Gives rigorous bounds or islands, or estimates where stated in the qualifier (`CB, non-rigorous error`).

methods.name: Conformal bootstrap, extremal functional method
methods.description: Reads off the spectrum and OPE coefficients from the functional that saturates a numerical bootstrap bound, assuming the theory lies at the boundary. An estimate, without a rigorous error.

methods.name: Truncated conformal bootstrap
methods.description: Gliozzi's method: keeps a few operators in the crossing equations and solves the truncated system (vanishing minors). Works without unitarity, e.g. for Lee–Yang; no rigorous error.

methods.name: Monte Carlo simulation
methods.description: Stochastic sampling of a classical lattice model in the universality class, with finite-size scaling to extract exponents. The qualifier names the lattice model or algorithm.

methods.name: Monte Carlo, improved Blume–Capel model
methods.description: Monte Carlo simulation of the Blume–Capel model (spins $0, \pm1$ on the cubic lattice) at the value of its vacancy coupling where the leading correction to scaling vanishes, so that small lattices already give precise exponents. `MC-BC, isotropic`: also tuned to cancel the leading breaking of rotation symmetry.

links.label: Wikipedia: Monte Carlo method in statistical mechanics

methods.name: Quantum Monte Carlo
methods.description: Monte Carlo sampling of a quantum lattice Hamiltonian (or its path integral), e.g. a fermion or spin model realizing the transition.

methods.name: Lattice gauge theory
methods.description: Monte Carlo simulation of the gauge theory discretized on a spacetime lattice, extrapolated to the continuum. The qualifier names the observable (e.g. Schrödinger functional, Dirac mode number).

methods.name: Fuzzy sphere regularization
methods.description: The critical theory is realized by interacting fermions in the lowest Landau level on a sphere with a magnetic monopole; scaling dimensions are read off from the energy spectrum by the state–operator correspondence (usually by exact diagonalization or DMRG).

methods.name: ε-expansion
methods.description: Perturbation theory in $\epsilon$ below an upper (or above a lower) critical dimension, e.g. $d = 4-\epsilon$ or $6-\epsilon$, usually resummed and evaluated at the physical $\epsilon$. The qualifier gives the expansion, the loop order and the resummation.

methods.name: Large-$N$ expansion
methods.description: Expansion in $1/N$, the inverse number of field components or colours, around the solvable $N=\infty$ limit.

methods.name: Large-$N_f$ expansion
methods.description: Expansion in $1/N_f$, the inverse number of matter flavours, in gauge theories such as QED$_3$ and QCD$_3$.

methods.name: Perturbation theory
methods.description: Expansion in a small coupling (Feynman diagrams); the qualifier gives the loop order or limit.

methods.name: Banks–Zaks expansion
methods.description: Expansion of a gauge theory's infrared fixed point in the distance from the top of the conformal window, $\Delta_f = N_f^{\max} - N_f$; scheme-independent when organized in powers of $\Delta_f$.

methods.name: Functional renormalization group
methods.description: Non-perturbative flow equation for the effective average action, solved in a truncation (e.g. the derivative expansion).

methods.name: Lattice series expansion
methods.description: Long high-temperature, low-temperature or activity series of a lattice model, extrapolated to the critical point (ratio or differential approximants).

methods.name: Padé approximants
methods.description: Rational functions matched to known expansions, e.g. interpolating between two expansions ($4-\epsilon$ and $2+\epsilon$, or large $N$ and $N=1$). An estimate, without a rigorous error.

methods.name: Supersymmetric localization
methods.description: The path integral of a supersymmetric theory on a curved space (e.g. $S^3$) reduces to a finite-dimensional matrix model, giving exact results for protected quantities such as the sphere free energy $F$ and $C_T$.

methods.name: a-maximization
methods.description: In 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ SCFTs the superconformal R-symmetry maximizes the trial $a$ built from 't Hooft anomalies; this fixes $a$, $c$ and the dimensions of chiral operators.

methods.name: F-maximization
methods.description: In 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFTs the superconformal R-symmetry extremizes the sphere free energy $F$ (computed by localization), fixing $F$ and the R-charges.

methods.name: Anomaly matching
methods.description: Quantities fixed by 't Hooft anomalies, which match along RG flows and across moduli spaces; computed e.g. on the tensor branch or by anomaly inflow.

methods.name: Holography (AdS/CFT)
methods.description: Computed in a dual gravitational theory, usually supergravity, valid at large $N$ and strong coupling.

methods.name: Experiment
methods.description: A laboratory measurement on a physical system in the universality class.

three_point_structures.name: three scalars, unit-normalized
three_point_structures.description: Three scalars $O_1, O_2, O_3$ that are singlets of any continuous global symmetry, with unit-normalized two-point functions $\langle O_i(x) O_i(0)\rangle = |x|^{-2\Delta_i}$: $\langle O_1(x_1) O_2(x_2) O_3(x_3)\rangle = \lambda_{123}\, |x_{12}|^{\Delta_3-\Delta_1-\Delta_2}|x_{13}|^{\Delta_2-\Delta_1-\Delta_3}|x_{23}|^{\Delta_1-\Delta_2-\Delta_3}$. In 2d it is often written $C_{123}$. The sign of $\lambda$ depends on the signs chosen for the operators. In embedding space it is the scalar three-point function of [@costa2011, Eq. (2.8)] with $\lambda_{123}$ as its constant, where $P_{ij} \equiv -2P_i\cdot P_j$ [@costa2011, Eq. (2.9)] becomes $x_{ij}^2$ on the Poincaré section [@costa2011, Eq. (2.10)].

three_point_structures.name: vector × vector → singlet, $\delta_{ij}$
three_point_structures.description: Two scalars $\phi_i$ in the vector of $O(N)$ and a singlet scalar $s$, with $\langle \phi_i(x)\phi_j(0)\rangle = \delta_{ij}|x|^{-2\Delta_\phi}$ and $s$ unit-normalized: $\langle\phi_i\phi_j s\rangle = \lambda_{\phi\phi s}\,\delta_{ij}$ times the three-scalar structure [@costa2011, Eq. (2.8)].

three_point_structures.name: free-scalar ⟨TTT⟩
three_point_structures.description: The parity-even stress-tensor three-point function of a 3d CFT is a combination of two structures, $\langle TTT\rangle = n_B\langle TTT\rangle_B + n_F\langle TTT\rangle_F$, where $\langle TTT\rangle_B$ is that of one free real scalar and $\langle TTT\rangle_F$ that of one free Majorana fermion (each with its own $T$ normalized by the Ward identity). $n_B$ is the coefficient of the free-scalar structure.
three_point_structures.relation: $n_B + n_F = C_T/C_T^{\rm free}$, with $C_T^{\rm free}$ that of one free real scalar (equal to that of one Majorana fermion in 3d).

three_point_structures.name: free-Majorana ⟨TTT⟩
three_point_structures.description: The coefficient of the free-Majorana-fermion structure $\langle TTT\rangle_F$ in $\langle TTT\rangle = n_B\langle TTT\rangle_B + n_F\langle TTT\rangle_F$ (see the free-boson structure).
